【99】KEY FACTS

【100】Clinical

【101】 HOA can be secondary to a wide variety of conditions, including pulmonary (bronchogenic carcinoma, lymphoma, abscess, bronchiectasis, cystic fibrosis, metastasis, emphysema), pleural (mesothelioma, fibroma), cardiovascular (cyanotic congenital heart disease, infected vascular grafts), and GI (inflammatory disorders, biliary cirrhosis, biliary atresia, polyposis, neoplasms) etiologies.

【102】 The pathogenesis is unknown, but neurogenic mechanisms, increased blood flow, and chemical mediators have been implicated.

【103】 Articular findings occur in about 40% of patients with HOA. Joint pain and swelling can be the presenting complaint. Joint effusions are common.

【104】 Digital clubbing is a frequent, but nonspecific, finding.

【105】 Treatment of the underlying lesion (e.g. thoracotomy, chemotherapy, or radiotherapy for lung carcinoma) is often followed by rapid clinical improvement of symptoms related to HOA.

【106】 There is anecdotal evidence that regrowth of a previously treated neoplasm causing HOA is associated with worsening HOA. In the case illustrated, appearance of HOA was the first indication of a recurrence of lung carcinoma.

【107】Radiologic

【108】 Bone scintigraphy is a highly sensitive method for detecting HOA. The scintigraphic findings appear before radiographic abnormalities, correspond to clinical signs and symptoms, and regress with therapy.

【109】 The “tram track” or “parallel stripe” sign is due to diffuse cortical radiotracer uptake in the metaphyses and diaphyses of tubular bones that results from periosteal new bone formation.

【110】 HOA findings are typically bilateral and symmetric and primarily involve the appendicular skeleton. Less common sites include the clavicles, scapulae, pelvis, digits, and facial bones.

【111】 Increased periarticular radiotracer uptake in HOA often indicates associated synovitis.

【112】 Plain film appearance of periostitis in HOA is variable. Findings include: 通用删除7(英):<u>(1)</u> simple periosteal elevation, 通用删除7(英):<u>(2)</u> smooth laminated (“onion-skin”) periostitis, 通用删除7(英):<u>(3)</u> irregular, wavy, or solid periostitis, and 通用删除7(英):<u>(4)</u> cortical thickening.

【113】 The periostitis of HOA begins in the diaphyses then later involves the metaphyses and sometimes tendinous insertions.

【114】 Digital clubbing can manifest as soft tissue swelling, with or without focal tuftal resorption or hypertrophy.

【115】 The soft tissue swelling, periarticular osteoporosis, and joint effusions of HOA can mimic rheumatoid arthritis. However, the joint space narrowing and erosions seen in rheumatoid arthritis are not present in HOA.

The uptake is most increased in the metaphyseal regions at the knees and ankles but also involves the diaphyses.</u>

【91】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【92】 Primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy (pachydermoperiostosis): This is a rare, familial, autosomal dominant disorder that occurs predominantly in men. However, the periostitis appears shaggy, irregular, and commonly involves epiphyses, unlike the findings in this case (metaphyseal and diaphyseal), making it an unlikely diagnosis.

【93】 Vascular insufficiency: The distribution of periostitis in vascular insufficiency is similar to that seen in the case under discussion, but the appearance is typically thicker and undulating.

【94】 Thyroid acropachy: The typical periostitis of thyroid acropachy appears solid and spiculated, not smooth (as in the case illustrated), and primarily involves the diaphyses of metacarpals and phalanges (and not the long bones).

【95】 Fluorosis: Solid, undulating periosteal thickening (periostitis deformans) in the appendicular skeleton, somewhat similar to that in the present case, can occur in fluorosis. However, osteosclerosis of the axial skeleton, the most striking feature in fluorosis, is absent in the case illustrated.

【96】 Secondary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy (HOA): HOA is the best diagnosis because of the metaphyseal and diaphyseal involvement, soft tissue swelling, joint pain, and a history of lung cancer.

【97】DIAGNOSIS

【98】Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy (secondary to a previously undiagnosed recurrence of lung adenocarcinoma)

【99】KEY FACTS

【100】Clinical

【101】 HOA can be secondary to a wide variety of conditions, including pulmonary (bronchogenic carcinoma, lymphoma, abscess, bronchiectasis, cystic fibrosis, metastasis, emphysema), pleural (mesothelioma, fibroma), cardiovascular (cyanotic congenital heart disease, infected vascular grafts), and GI (inflammatory disorders, biliary cirrhosis, biliary atresia, polyposis, neoplasms) etiologies.

【102】 The pathogenesis is unknown, but neurogenic mechanisms, increased blood flow, and chemical mediators have been implicated.

【103】 Articular findings occur in about 40% of patients with HOA. Joint pain and swelling can be the presenting complaint. Joint effusions are common.

【104】 Digital clubbing is a frequent, but nonspecific, finding.

【105】 Treatment of the underlying lesion (e.g. thoracotomy, chemotherapy, or radiotherapy for lung carcinoma) is often followed by rapid clinical improvement of symptoms related to HOA.

【106】 There is anecdotal evidence that regrowth of a previously treated neoplasm causing HOA is associated with worsening HOA. In the case illustrated, appearance of HOA was the first indication of a recurrence of lung carcinoma.

【107】Radiologic

【108】 Bone scintigraphy is a highly sensitive method for detecting HOA. The scintigraphic findings appear before radiographic abnormalities, correspond to clinical signs and symptoms, and regress with therapy.

【109】 The “tram track” or “parallel stripe” sign is due to diffuse cortical radiotracer uptake in the metaphyses and diaphyses of tubular bones that results from periosteal new bone formation.

【110】 HOA findings are typically bilateral and symmetric and primarily involve the appendicular skeleton. Less common sites include the clavicles, scapulae, pelvis, digits, and facial bones.

【111】 Increased periarticular radiotracer uptake in HOA often indicates associated synovitis.

【112】 Plain film appearance of periostitis in HOA is variable. Findings include: 通用删除7(英):<u>(1)</u> simple periosteal elevation, 通用删除7(英):<u>(2)</u> smooth laminated (“onion-skin”) periostitis, 通用删除7(英):<u>(3)</u> irregular, wavy, or solid periostitis, and 通用删除7(英):<u>(4)</u> cortical thickening.

【113】 The periostitis of HOA begins in the diaphyses then later involves the metaphyses and sometimes tendinous insertions.

【114】 Digital clubbing can manifest as soft tissue swelling, with or without focal tuftal resorption or hypertrophy.

【115】 The soft tissue swelling, periarticular osteoporosis, and joint effusions of HOA can mimic rheumatoid arthritis. However, the joint space narrowing and erosions seen in rheumatoid arthritis are not present in HOA.

【123】**RINGING IN THE EARS (TINNITUS)**

【124】**_Case Presentation： A 77-year-old patient complains of"ringing in his ears"and states_ _his hearing has gotten progressively worse._**

【125】**INTRODUCTION TO COMPLAINT**

【126】Tinnitus is not a condition itself-it is a symptom of an underlying condition， such as age-related hearing loss， ear injury， or a circulatory system disorder. Causes are：

【127】· Presbycusis： occurs with aging

【128】· Acoustic trauma：long exposure to loud noise

【129】**· Ear infections： bacterial or viral infections**

【130】·Earwax blockage： causes hearing loss or irritation of the eardrum， which can lead to tinnitus

【131】·Bony structure changes： otosclerosis

【132】· Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders： TMJ impairment

【133】· Head injuries or neck injuries： head or neck trauma， hearing nerves， or brain function linked to hearing

【134】· Acoustic neuroma： This noncancerous (benign) tumor develops on the cranial nerve that runs from the brain to the inner ear and controls balance and hearing； condition generally causes tinnitus in only one ear

【135】Ototoxicity： a side effect of certain medications or alcohol

【136】·Ménière’s disease： inner ear disorder that may be caused by abnormal inner ear fluid pressure

【137】·Pulsatile tinnitus： head and neck tumors， atherosclerosis， high blood pressure (BP)， turbulent blood flow， and malformation of capillaries

【1】**_Case Presentation： A 38-year-old Caucasian female presents to the acute care office_ _with complaints of rectal pain (proctalgia)._**

【2】**INTRODUCTION TO COMPLAINT**

【3】· Pain is subjective and needs to be assessed by asking about the severity of the pain

【8】**·Could be from a sexually transmitted disease (STD)， which would present as perianal discomfort with discharge**

【115】**Case Study Analysis**

【116】Gradual pain worsening in nature. The pain is constant and throbbing occurring around the rectum. An erythematous mass is present in the perianal area. White blood cell (WBC) count on the complete blood count (CBC) is slightly elevated； however， the patient is afe-brile. The absence of bleeding ruled out an anal fissure， cancer， or hemorrhoids.

【117】**_Diagnosis： Perianal abscess_**

【118】**· Incision and drainage of the abscess is performed and wound is cultured**

【122】The patient is to return for a follow-up appointment in 1 week at which time the results from the wound culture will be reviewed and antibiotics adjusted if necessary.

【123】**RINGING IN THE EARS (TINNITUS)**

【124】**_Case Presentation： A 77-year-old patient complains of"ringing in his ears"and states_ _his hearing has gotten progressively worse._**

【125】**INTRODUCTION TO COMPLAINT**

【126】Tinnitus is not a condition itself-it is a symptom of an underlying condition， such as age-related hearing loss， ear injury， or a circulatory system disorder. Causes are：

【127】· Presbycusis： occurs with aging

【128】· Acoustic trauma：long exposure to loud noise

【129】**· Ear infections： bacterial or viral infections**

【130】·Earwax blockage： causes hearing loss or irritation of the eardrum， which can lead to tinnitus

【131】·Bony structure changes： otosclerosis

【132】· Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders： TMJ impairment

【133】· Head injuries or neck injuries： head or neck trauma， hearing nerves， or brain function linked to hearing

【134】· Acoustic neuroma： This noncancerous (benign) tumor develops on the cranial nerve that runs from the brain to the inner ear and controls balance and hearing； condition generally causes tinnitus in only one ear

【135】Ototoxicity： a side effect of certain medications or alcohol

【136】·Ménière’s disease： inner ear disorder that may be caused by abnormal inner ear fluid pressure

【137】·Pulsatile tinnitus： head and neck tumors， atherosclerosis， high blood pressure (BP)， turbulent blood flow， and malformation of capillaries

In summary, the exams were within normal limits for her age and gender. Homeopathic medication was prescribed, which corrected the constipation but did not heal the perianal lesion. After around 60 days of treatment, the constipation had not returned but the same initial complaint was present, so the mother went to a pediatrician again where a biopsy was taken of the condyloma acuminata, which was taken to another hospital. He was head of the household where the patient lived and forced her to leave the house. 【1】The Eight Direction perception Meditation

【2】The Eight Direction Perception Meditation is designed to enable the Medical Qigong doctor to expand his or her field of awareness and intuitive perception by directing the imagination and intention. This meditation facilitates absorption of sensory and mental stimulation, and serves to combine both internal and external perceptional awareness to the degree that the doctor will eventually reach a state of being where there is no distinction between the two.

【3】Through consistent practice, the doctor will begin to blend with the surroundings and feel as though he or she is becoming invisible. As the distinction between the doctor and the surroundings starts to disperse, the doctor will begin to feel as though he or she is part of the universal and environmental rhythms and movements that surround the doctor, becoming one with the infinite space of the Wuji.

【4】This meditation requires a great deal of relaxation, intense concentration, and daily practice to achieve the above mentioned results. The meditation consists of mentally touching every cell of the body, inside and out, and then expanding this body awareness to fill the surroundings.

【5】This meditation serves to increase psychic awareness. However, it is important for the doctor to maintain balance between all of the psychic energies if he or she is to progress rapidly. This balance can be achieved by harmonizing sensory input.

【6】Psychic energy is stored in the Yin organs and can be depleted through the emotions and senses. In all Shengong (Spirit Skill) meditations and exercises, it is important to achieve a balance between all five senses. If the five senses are not balanced, psychic energy will be drained and the awareness will be hindered. The five senses are related to the Yin organ energies as follows:

【7】•    The desire of seeing (sight) depletes Liver energy.

【8】•    The desire of feeling (touch) depletes Heart energy.

【9】•    The desire of eating (taste) depletes Spleen energy.

【10】•    The desire of fragrances (smell) depletes Lung energy.

【11】•    The desire of listening to sounds (hearing) depletes Kidney energy.

【12】While performing this meditation, all of the senses should "expand into the infinite." This means that they are sensing all things, but are not focused on any one particular thing.

【13】Preparation

【14】To perform this meditation, assume a standing Wuji posture. Place the feet slightly wider than the shoulders, with the knees bent, the spine straight, and the buttocks tucked under. Imagine that the feet are rooted deep into the Earth, while the head pushes up against the Heavens. The shoulders are to be kept relaxed and rounded. The arms should hang freely by the sides of the body, with the palms facing towards the back of the body. The tongue should touch the roof of the mouth on the hard palate. Relax and close the anal sphincter. Breathe softly through the nose and perform Natural Breathing.

【15】The eight directions are: the front, back, right, left, top, and bottom of the body (the six directions of space), as well as the inside and outside of the body .

【16】1st Direction

【17】Begin this meditation by focusing your attention on the front of your body. Start with the face and work down to the feet. Try to feel every cell of your skin, every hair follicle, every curve, every crevice of your forehead, eyes, nose, cheeks, lips, chin, neck, chest, upper abdomen, lower abdomen, groin, thighs, shins and feet. Be sure to include the front part of your arms. Take your time and focus on touching each detail with your imagination. Feel not only the surface, but expand the imagery to three dimensions so that you feel the area around the body part. Form an imaginary cast that covers the part of the body you are concentrating on.

【18】Paint this cast so that it starts about one-quarter inch under the skin and extends to about one inch beyond the skin, creating an imaginary force field. Take your time and feel the energy build as your mind focuses on each minute detail of your body. As you move down from the forehead to the feet, keep that imaginary cast on. In other words, do not forget about your forehead as you move on to other parts of the front of the body. Once you have touched a body part with your imagination, you will remain in touch with it through the entire meditation. Throughout the meditation you must constantly tell yourself to

【20】relax and sink into the Earth. Your mind is in the Earth and your imagination is touching the different parts of the front side of your body.

【21】2nd Direction

【22】Once you have touched on every part of the front of your body, start at the top of your head and mentally touch each part of the back of your body with your imagination. Build the energy cast as you did on the front of the body. This imagery is extremely important. Most practitioners do not have a very strong awareness of what is happening behind them. This section of the exercise will help to build that awareness. Make sure that you proceed at a relatively slow pace and truly get in touch with your back.

【23】3rd Direction

【24】After you have mentally touched the front and back of your body, move your attention to the right side of your body. You should continue to mentally maintain the sensation of being covered with the energy cast on the front and back parts of the body. Start at the top of your head on the right side and move down over the ear and neck, the right shoulder, the right arm, the right side of your chest and back, the right hip and waist, groin and buttocks, the right side of the leg and the right foot. As you build this energy cast, feel it fuse with the cast that you created on the front and back of your body. Throughout this exercise it is important that you spend time trying to feel each and every cell of your skin.

【25】4th Direction

【26】When you have completed the right side of the body, move your imagination to the left side of the body and follow the same procedure.

【27】5th Direction

【28】Move your attention to the top of your head and sequentially start to fill in the holes of your perception by touching all of the portions of your body that are facing upward. Imagine that a spotlight is above your head. Touch every part of your body that the spotlight would shine on. Touch the top of your head, nose, ears, cheeks, shoulders, chest, back, forearms, hands, groin, buttocks, thighs, calves, and the tops of your feet, etc.

【29】6th Direction

【30】The last step in finishing the exterior energy cast is to mentally touch each part of your body that is facing down. Imagine that you are standing on a spotlight. Touch every part of your body that the spotlight would shine on. Fill in the gaps under your nose, under your chin, your armpits, and your groin area, etc. When you are finished, your entire body should now be covered with an imaginary energy cast which travels from one-quarter of an inch below your skin to about one inch outside your body. Remember the importance in this exercise does not lie in simply building the cast, but in trying to get a good feel for each part of your body. You have now completed fusing the energy of the Heavens, the Earth, and the four winds into your body.

【31】7th Direction

【32】The seventh direction is inward. Starting from the top of your head, fill in the hollow part of the energy cast as you touch each inch of tissue, organ, muscle, tendon, and bone in your body. Try to feel each portion of your body down to the cellular level. While you are concentrating inward, it is important that you do not forget about the previous directions. When you have reached the ends of your toes after slowly working all the way through the body, you should feel as though you are in touch with your entire being. You should have a sense of wholeness and total body integration. You will now take this new found awareness and expand it into the entire room.

【33】8th Direction

【54】Talking with the Patient to Establish Treatment Goals

【55】After completing the diagnosis, establishing the treatment principle, and determining the treatment strategy, the Qigong doctor discusses with the patient the treatment goals (e.g. which internal organs, channels, and tissue areas are associated with the primary cause of the patient's disease and how to address these). The treatment areas are specifically chosen to facilitate a rapid effect on the healing process. The doctor explains the intended goal of using purging, tonifying, or regulating techniques and how they will affect the patient's body.

【56】Explaining and Reaching Agreements on the Treatment Modalities to be Used

【57】The Qigong doctor explains in clear, comprehensive terminology what he or she has determined is the best way of approaching the patient's condition (e.g. having the patient in a lying, sitting, or standing posture), rectifying the condition (e.g. purgation, tonification, or regulation), and what treatment modalities the doctor will be using (e.g. Qi Emission Therapy, Qigong Massage Therapy, Sound and Light Therapy, etc.).

【58】The more the patient understands the doctor's approach to addressing the condition, the greater the likelihood of the patient relaxing during the treatment. This explanation also assists the development of trust, which will encourage the patient when practicing the Medical Qigong Prescription exercises or when receiving suggestions on lifestyle modifications.

【59】Honoring the Patient’s Spiritual Belief System

【60】When treating patients, it is important that the Qigong doctor not become distracted by the illusion of solid tissue matter; instead, the doctor remembers that we are spirit and that healing begins in this fifth dimension. The primary belief in Medical Qigong therapy is that tangible and intangible energy, through faith, will merge at the highest level of cultivation. Prayer is an invocation that extends through the mind, emotion, and spirit to the Divine, while meditation is a state of mental, emotional, and spiritual receptivity for divine inspiration, guidance, and manifestation. Both actions (prayer and meditation) connect the doctor and patient to the Divine and help bring the patient back into awareness of his or her body and to initiate divine healing.

【61】In China, Qigong doctors have a saying, "train your virtue and morality to increase your energy, allow your Shen to lead your Qi and the Qi will flow pure." Meaning, the stronger the individual's virtue has been developed, the more powerful his or her spiritual intention and flow of Qi will be.

【62】The healing modality chosen by the doctor must be in line with the patient's spiritual belief structure. The patient must be connected to his or her own unique interpretation of universal consciousness (Divine) for healing to take place.

【63】When the patient disbelieves in a Higher Power — be it God or a universal consciousness -- the doctor can still help the patient heal, providing the patient has established sufficient trust and hope in the doctor. If the patient feels listened to, understood, and respected by the doctor, this can empower the patient to heal regardless of his or her own conscious belief system.

【64】If the doctor, on the other hand, does not believe that a true healing can take place unless the patient believes in a Higher Power or God - then no healing will take place, for the doctor will lack confidence and trust. The therapeutic bond between the doctor and patient will be broken and replaced by a battle of wills.

【65】For patients who lack faith, applying a hands-on Qigong Massage technique may be more effective. Gradually, over the course of time, the doctor may incorporate other healing modalities as greater trust is established.

【66】The Qigong doctor should always begin treatment in harmony with the patient's spiritual belief system (which may change in time), through touch, verbal conversation, empathy, and unconditional love. The doctor should also compassionately communicate through his or her subconscious mind to the patient's subconscious mind; this will facilitate trust at a deeper subconscious level.

【57】**Pathology of the Thyroid Gland**

【58】参考段删除-1:<u>_ASHRAF KHAN， MD， FRCPATH AND VANIA NOSE， MD， PHD_</u>

【59】**DEVELOPMENT AND EMBRYOLOGY**

【60】The thyroid gland develops from the larger median analage and the two lateral analagen. The medial analage， which forms the major portion of the thyroid， is derived from the floor of the foregut and the two lateral analagen are derived from the endoderm of the fourth and the fifth branchial pouches as the ultimobranchial bodies. The medial analage appears by d 24 as median endodermal diverticulum from the base of the tongue in the region of foramen cecum. The diverticulum descends down from the foramen cecum into the neck along the midline attached to the thyroglossal duct. It reaches its final position anterior to the trachea by about 7 wk； it then grows laterally， and becomes bilobed 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1\]</u>. Early during the fifth week， the thyro-glossal duct loses its lumen and shortly afterwards breaks into fragments 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2\]</u>. However， the caudal end of the thyroglossal duct may persist in some embryos， and this constitutes the pyrami-dal process， which is present in about 75% of mature human thyroids 通用删除6(英):<u>\[3\]</u>. The lateral thyroid analage becomes attached to the posterior surface of the thyroid during the fifth week and contributes up to 30% to the thyroid weight 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2\]</u>. The causes of the fusion of the lateral and medial analage are unknown 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2\]</u>. It is speculated that migration of the ultimobranchial body con-trols the growth of the medial analage， or that the growth of the medial analage laterally and caudally inhibits expansion of the ultimobranchial body 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2\]</u>. Thelateral thyroid analage is thought to give rise to the calcitonin producing C cells and the solid cell nests. It is believed that the C cells are derived from the neural crest； they migrate to the ultimobranchial body and are subse-quently incorporated into the thyroid 通用删除6(英):<u>\[4\]</u>. However， the exist-ence of mixed follicular and C-cell tumors raises the possibility of the common stem cell origin for both follicular and C cells as is seen in the gastrointestinal tract 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1\]</u>.

【61】The thyroid gland initially consists of a solid mass of endo-dermal cells， but small groups of epithelial cells are soon iden-tified. The first follicles form from epithelial plates at the beginning of the eighth week and by the twelfth week the plates are entirely converted into follicles 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2\]</u>. The development of the human fetal thyroid has been divided into three stages by LiVolsi to include precolloid stage(7-13wk)； the colloid stage(13-14wk)；and the follicular stage (after 14 wk) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[5\]</u>.Evidence

【64】**NORMAL ANATOMY AND HISTOLOGY**

【65】The thyroid is normally located in the midportion of the neck anterior to the trachea and larynx， just below the cricoid carti-lage attached by a loose connective tissue capsule. The recur-rent laryngeal nerves lie in the groove between the lateral lobes and the trachea. The superior and inferior parathyroid glands are found close to the posterior surface of the gland or they may be located within the gland itself.

【66】The thyroid gland consists of two lobes joined by an isthmus. In adults the two lobes measure approx 2-2.5 cm wide and 4-5 cm long 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1\]</u>. In some glands a pyramidal lobe， derived from the distal portion of the thyroglossal duct， extends upwards from the isthmus. At birth the thyroid weighs 1-2 g and increases to10-15 g at puberty 通用删除6(英):<u>\[6\]</u>. In the adult the normal weight ranges from 15 to 35 g 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1\]</u>. The weight varies with iodine intake， sex， age， and functional status of the gland. In addition there are geographic variations ranging from an upper limit of up to 42g in a Portuguese study 通用删除6(英):<u>\[7\]</u> to about 10-20 g in a North Ameri-can population 通用删除6(英):<u>\[8，9\]</u>. The mean weight is always higher in women， and the weight varies in size with the menstrual cycle通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>. In the elderly the weight may sometimes decrease to as little as 10 g通用删除6(英):<u>\[1\]</u>.

【67】On section， the thyroid gland has a brown cut surface and it is composed of multiplelobules separated by thin fibrous septa. Each lobule is made up of 20-40 follicles and is supplied by a single intralobular artery 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1\]</u>. The thyroid gland contains three major types of epithelial cells： follicular cells， which line the follicles and secrete thyroxin and triiodothyronine(T3)；Ccells， which secrete calcitonin； and the solid cell nests (SCN)，which are remnants of the ultimobranchial body. The follicles are filled with colloid， range in size from 50 to 500 um (average200 um) in diameter， and are lined by cuboidal to low columnar epithelium. The cells lining the follicles have a basal nucleus and rest on a basement membrane composed of laminin and collagen IV 通用删除6(英):<u>\[11\]</u>. The colloid includes thyroglobulin， which is a glycoprotein giving it a periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive diastase-resistant staining characteristic. The amount of the colloid and the height of the follicular lining cells vary with the

【69】functional status of the gland. Inahyperactive state the follicles are lined by tall cells and have less colloid. In addition to col-loid the follicles contain birefringent calcium oxalate monohy-drate crystals， the numbers of which may increase with age 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1\]</u>. This finding may be useful at times to differentiate between thy-roid follicles and parathyroid tissue at frozen section 通用删除6(英):<u>\[12\]</u>. Intra-cytoplasmic fat within thyroid follicular cells may be detected in 50% of glands on oil red-O staining and this may increase with age 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1\]</u>. Owing to the intimate development of thyroid with the mesodermal structures of the neck， fat， cartilage， and/or muscle may be found within the thyroid capsule 通用删除6(英):<u>\[5\]</u>. For the same reason normal thyroid tissue may be found intermingled with the neck soft tissues including muscle， which should not be mistaken for metastatic carcinoma.

【70】Onimmunohistochemistry the follicular cells stainpositively with low-molecular-weight cytokeratin and with thyroglobu-lin， and may also coexpress vimentin 通用删除6(英):<u>\[4\]</u>. In situ hy bridization studies have revealed thyroglobulin mRNA within the follicu-lar cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[4\]</u>.

The C cells are intrafollicular and sometimes parafollicular in location. In normal glands they are not visualized on routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. However， special his-tochemical stains such as Gremelius and immunohistochemi-cal stains using pan-neuroendocrine antibodies such as chro-mogranin and synaptophysin and specific antibodies including calcitonin and calcitonin-gene-related peptide (CGRP) can identify them 通用删除6(英):<u>\[4\]</u>. Inaddition，C cells may also stain positive for bombesin，somatostatin， gastrin-releasing peptide，low-molec-ular-weight cytokeratin， and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) onimmunohistochemistry.Onelectron microscopy，the Ccells have the characteristic neurosecretory granules； these granules are of two types， the larger and moderately electron dense type I granules measuring 280 nm， and the smaller 130 nm more elec-tron dense type II granules. Both type I and II granules show cal-citonin on immunoelectron microscopy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[13\]</u>.On in situ hybrid-|删除0换行|ization， both calcitonin and CGRP mRNA can be localized in C cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[4\]</u>.**

【72】The solid cell nests (SCN) can be seen in up to 60% of thyroid glands in the midportions of the lateral lobes 通用删除6(英):<u>\[14\]</u>. They are solid irregular masses of epithelial cells measuring about 1mm or less in maximum diameter and may be solitary or mul-tiple， unilateral or bilateral. They are composed of polyhedral or oval cells with oval nuclei containing finely granular chro-matin ；nuclear grooves may be seen 通用删除6(英):<u>\[4\]</u>.SC

【63】ICHEN simplex chronicus and hypertrophic lichen planus are pruritic conditions， both of which show histologic signs of persisteni rubbing. In fact， hypertrophic lichen planus is lichen simplex chronicus superimposed upon ordinary lesions of lichen planus. Common to both conditions are compact orthokeratosis， irregular psoriasiform hyper-plasia， focal hypergranulosis， coarse collagen bundles arranged in vertical streaks in a thickened papillary dermis， a superficial perivascular inflam-matory-cell infiltrate of lymphocytes and histiocytes， widely dilated vascular spaces oriented perpendicularly to the skin surface， an increased number of melanophages and fibroblasts in the upper part of the dermis， follicular dilation with plugging by cornified cells， and hypergranulosis within follicu-lar infundibula.

【64】In lichen simplex chronicus， all of the described changes result from persistent rubbing. There are no features of lichen planus. The histologic characteristics of persistent rubbing of skin in the hyperkeratotic type of lichen simplex chronicus are compact orthokeratosis with abundant para-keratosis， hypergranulosis， irregular psoriasiform hyperplasia， and， some-times， coarse collagen bundles in vertical streaks in a thickened papillary dermis. In short， all of the components of the skin above the reticular der-mis become thickened. Scratching of these lesions of lichen simplex chronicus may result in erosions， ulcerations， crusts， and focal necrosis of the upper part of the epidermis. In hypertrophic lichen planus， in addition to changes of chronic rubbing， there is relatively little parakeratosis， the granular zone is thickened in wedge-shaped fashion (cspecially prominent within dilated infundibula). A lichenoid infiltrate obscures the dermo-epidermal junction focally at the rounded bases of rete ridges (with sparing of the tips of dermal papillae)， and there is vacuolar alteration with necrotic keralinocytes in the basal portion of the epidermis.

【65】Lesions of prurigo nodularis and its excoriated， ulcerated form， namely， picker's nodule， result from persistent rubbing (and scratching)； they represent localized， nodular variants of lichen simplex chronicus. Rather than persistent rubbing of a broad arca to produce a pladuc of lichen simplex chronicus， a smaller spot of skin is assaulted with a blunt object， usually a finger tip or knuckle， to produce a nodule. As a rule， the initiating cause of the pruritus is not identified by history or histologic analysis. Prurigo nodularis occurs mostly in middle-aged persons， especially women. There usually are a few nodules， mostly situated on anatomic sites easily accessible to fingers and fingernails， such as the extensor parts of the fore-arms， the thighs， and the legs. The course is protracted.

【66】There are two basic histologic patterns that result from chronic rub-bing. When the cornificd laver is markedly thickened and completely ortho-keratotic， like that normally present only on palms or soles， we term the lesion the hyperkeratotic type of lichen simplex chronicus. These lesions appear commonly on certain anatomic sites， such as on a lip (as keratosis oris)， on the perianal mucosal-epidermal junction (as a consequence of pru-ritus ani)， on the genitals， and on the scalp. In the second type of lichen simplex， encountered more comionly， the changes in the cornified layer are less impressive than those in the papillary dermis. In this second type， the papillary dermis is markedly thickened by altered collagen， both coars-cned and oriented perpendicularly to the surface of the epidermis. Some-times both patterns are present in a single biopsy specimen. As a rule， however， the hyperkeratotic type of lichen simplex chronicus is not associ-ated with coarse collagen bundles in vertical streaks in a thickened papillary dermis.

【67】Hypertrophic lichen planus is merely one of many manifestations of lichen planus； in this case， in addition to lichen planus there are the changes caused by superimposition of persistent rubbing. Individual lesions are scaly， hyperpigmented plaques or dome-shaped nodules. Although lichen planus is characteristically pruritic， rubbing sufficient to produce the addi-tional changes of lichen simplex chronicus is seen rarely， and then with greater frequency on the legs， especially near the ankles. Other variants of lichen planus include the bullous and atrophic types， those of the nails and mucous membranes， and lichen planopilaris.

【68】Lichen planus， in its classic histologic form， has epidermal hyperplasia with jagged rete ridges， orthokeratosis， and a dense lichenoid， predomi-nantly lymphocytic infiltrate that obscures the dermo-epidermal junctione S1：venly across the entire lesion. With the superimposition of persistent rub-bing， histologic changes of lichen simplex alter the basic pattern of lichen planus. The epidermal hyperplasia becomes even more marked， the bases of the rete ridges become rounded and lose their jagged outline， small foci of parakeratosis may be present in the hyperkeratotic cornified layer， and the band-like infiltrate of lymphocytes develops skip areas， i.e.， sparing the tips of the dermal papillae where there is more coarsening of the collagen bun-dles.

【69】The changes of lichen simplex added to lichen planus are much the same as lichen simplex superimposed on macular amyloidosis to produce lichen amvloidosis.

【70】Clinically， lichen simplex chronicus is a plaque characterized by accen-tuation of normal skin markings， hyperpigmentation， and a keratotic sur-face. Hypertrophic lichen planus consists of purplish papules， nodules， and plaques that are markedly keratotic， especially in the skin overlying the anterior tibia， which is casily accessible to persistent rubhing by a heel.

【96】**_Lichen Sclerosus et Atrophicus_ _Chronic Radiation Dermatitis_**

LICHEN sclerosus et atrophicus and chronic radi-|删除0换行|ation dermatitis are both fibrosing dermatitides that may closely resemble one another when viewed with the scanning objective of the conventional light microscope. Both diseases are characterized by hyperkeratosis， vacuo-lar alteration of the basal layer， subepidermal clefts， sclerosis and fibrin deposition in the dermis， and dilated dermal vascular spaces with a sur-rounding infiltrate of inflammatory cells， extravasated erythrocytes， and pigment-laden macrophages. Both lesions are rubbed commonly， producing compact orthokeratosis. Major features that enable the two conditions to be differentiated are changes in the dermis in lichen sclerosus et atrophicus that arc confined to the papillary dermis， i.e.， there are no changes in the collagen of the reticular dermis. Furthermore， in lichen sclerosus， the ostia of epithelial structures of adnexa are plugged by cornified cells. In contrast， in chronic radiation dermatitis， there is sclerosis at all levels of the dermis and occasionally of the subcutis， and ostia of adnexal structures are not plugged. In addition， there are many more atypical keratinocytes， melano-cytes， and fibroblasts in chronic radiodermatitis， and the dilated blood ves-sels have abnormal shapes and atypical endothelial cells.

【98】Lichen sclerosus et atrophicus， in contrast to chronic radiation derma-titis， is often pruritic rather than painful and most often affects the external genitalia of women. Lichen sclerosus may also affect the genitalia of men， and， when on the glans， is termed balanitis xerotica obliterans. Regardless of location (and it may be extragenital on nearly any cutaneous site)， lesions are hypopigmented papules or plaques showing atrophy characterized by“cigarette-paper”wrinkling， follicular plugging， and telangiectases. As with chronic radiation dermatitis， although with far less frequency， squamous cell carcinomas may develop within lesions of lichen sclerosus et atrophicus on the vulva.

【99】Chronic radiation dermatitis usually occurs in one of two circum-stances. The more common type is the result of radiation therapy， most often administered in fractionated doses for treatment of cutaneous malig-nancies. The second type of chronic radiation dermatitis follows long-term exposures at lower doses and is usually an occupational disease， most often seen in careless dentists and dental assistants who take radiographs without precautions， Patterns of radiation exposure similar to those ofoccupational exposure have been used therapeutically for the treatment of acne， epilation of excess hair， “neurodermatitis，" recalcitrant verrucae， and other benign conditions of the skin.

【100】**Dermatitis from high doses of radiation given over a short period of time， i.e.， as a means of therapy， are seen at the site of treatment beginning severalyears after the initial therapy. The clinical changes are atrophic scars， loss of hair， telangiectases， and hyper- and hypopigmentation. Occu-pational radiation dermatitis is seen most often on the hands， which show drying and scaling， sparse hair， flattening of skin lines， verrucous keratoses， and painful ulcerations. Some cases， usually those on the face， eventuate in scleroderma-like bird-nose facies and warty keratoses. Radiation keratoses， squamous-cell carcinomas， and sarcomas occur with increased frequency in both types of radiation-induced dermatitis.**

【101】**The clinical features of hardness， whiteness， telangiectases， and atro-phy， shared by lichen sclerosus and chronic radiation dermatitis， have simi-lar histologic aspects in both diseases. The hardness results from the altered， sclerotic connective tissue in the dermis. The whiteness resuits from loss of epidermal melanin， as well as from sclerosis in the upper part of the dermis. Telangiectases are dilated vessels， often in increased numbers， within the dermis made all the more visible by epidermal thinning. Atrophy is charac-terized histologically by flattening and thinning of the epidermis but rnostly by flattening of the normal pattern of rete ridges and dermal papillae. If a biopsy specimen is superficial， the two conditions may be indistinguishable histologically， because only those features common to both diseases may be seen in the specimen.**

【126】**_Chronic Urticaria_**

CHRONIC urticaria and the urticarial stage of|删除换行|bullous pemphigoid have several histologic features in common， such as a superficial and mid- or deep dermalperivascular and interstitial mixed-cell infiltrate of neutrophils and eosinophils in addition to lymphocytes and histiocytes， edema in the dermis， and dilated blood vessels. The cardinal features that enable chronic urticaria to be differentiated from urticarial lesions of pemphigoid are that the infiltrate is sparse， there is more edema in the reticular than in the papillary dermis， and neutrophils tend to out-number eosinophils in the inflammatory-cell infiltrate. In contrast， the infil-trate in the urticarial stage of pemphigoid is moderately dense and concen-trated in the papillary dermis， the edema in the papillary dermis is greater than that in the reticular dermis， and eosinophils outnumber neutrophils in the inflammatory-cell infiltrate.

【128】Urticaria is a commonly encountered clinical problem. It has been esti-mated that 15 to 20% of people experience at least one episode of urticaria in their lifetimes. Clinically， a wheal is an edernatous， irregularly shaped， pinkish papule or plaque that blanches upon pressure and itches， often intensely. Individual wheals are transient， not usually persisting for more than 24 hours. If an individual hive persists for longer than 36 hours， it is probably not true urticaria， but rather is part of an urticaria-like process such as an urticarial drug reaction or the urticarial stage of bullous pemphi-goid.

【129】Acute and chronic urticaria are defined by the duration of the entire process rather than by the duration of individual hives. Urticaria is said to be chronic if the process lasts for more than 6 weeks. In reality， hives that come and go for more than a few days are likely to persist for much longer than that， in some patients even for years. The individual wheals in both acute and chronic urticaria tend to disappear in less than 24 hours. Acute urticaria， which is often explosive in onset and may be associated with angioedema， is almost always an allergic response， and the cause is usually identified by the patient， e.g.， an ingestant， inhalant， or injected substance. In contrast， the cause of longlasting， i.e.， chronic， urticaria is practically never identifiable by either patient or physician， and it may be that the mechanism for it is not related to allergy. Hives of acute urticaria respond quickly and effectively to various antihistamines or to systemic corticoste-roids； those of chronic urticaria are not controlled invariably by any medica-tion， although H-1 blocking antihistamines such as hydroxyzine are some-times palliative.

【130】Unlike individual lesions of true hives， the urticarial lesions of pemphi-goid persist for more than 36 hours； some lesions may be surmounted by tense vesicles or bullae. Patients afflicted with pemphigoid tend to be older， i.e.， in their seventh and cighth decades， than those with true urticaria， and the lesions are often accompanied by evidence of excoriations. The urticarial lesions of pemphigoid often assume arcuate， annular， gyrate， and serpigi-nous configurations， Rarely， the lesions disappearr“spontaneously”and completely， but as a rule， their appearance presages the coming of more typical blisters of pemphigoid. True urticaria never vesiculates.

【131】The histologic findings in true urticaria and in urticarial lesions of bullous pemphigoid are quite specific. A sparse superficial and deep peri-vascular and interstitial mixed-cell infiltrate containing eosinophils and neutrophils is virtually diagnostic of chronic urticaria. Urticarial allergic eruptions caused especially by drugs are indistinguishable histologically from the lesions of chronic urticaria. Differentiation histologically of acute urticaria from chronic urticaria is accomplishable. Lesions of acute urti-caria tend to have mostly lymphocytes in the sparse infiltrate and few eosin-ophils. Furthermore， neutrophils are usually absent from lesions of acute urticaria，

【132】A moderately dense superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial infiltrate that is also moderately dense and lichenoid in the papillary dermis and is associated with innumerable eosinophils is virtually diagnostic of the urticarial stage of pemphigoid. Herpes gestationis， one of the pruritic papu-lar and vesicular eruptions of pregnancy， is indistinguishable histologically from bullous pemphigoid. 【63】ICHEN simplex chronicus and hypertrophic lichen planus are pruritic conditions， both of which show histologic signs of persisteni rubbing. In fact， hypertrophic lichen planus is lichen simplex chronicus superimposed upon ordinary lesions of lichen planus. Common to both conditions are compact orthokeratosis， irregular psoriasiform hyper-plasia， focal hypergranulosis， coarse collagen bundles arranged in vertical streaks in a thickened papillary dermis， a superficial perivascular inflam-matory-cell infiltrate of lymphocytes and histiocytes， widely dilated vascular spaces oriented perpendicularly to the skin surface， an increased number of melanophages and fibroblasts in the upper part of the dermis， follicular dilation with plugging by cornified cells， and hypergranulosis within follicu-lar infundibula.

【64】In lichen simplex chronicus， all of the described changes result from persistent rubbing. There are no features of lichen planus. The histologic characteristics of persistent rubbing of skin in the hyperkeratotic type of lichen simplex chronicus are compact orthokeratosis with abundant para-keratosis， hypergranulosis， irregular psoriasiform hyperplasia， and， some-times， coarse collagen bundles in vertical streaks in a thickened papillary dermis. In short， all of the components of the skin above the reticular der-mis become thickened. Scratching of these lesions of lichen simplex chronicus may result in erosions， ulcerations， crusts， and focal necrosis of the upper part of the epidermis. In hypertrophic lichen planus， in addition to changes of chronic rubbing， there is relatively little parakeratosis， the granular zone is thickened in wedge-shaped fashion (cspecially prominent within dilated infundibula). A lichenoid infiltrate obscures the dermo-epidermal junction focally at the rounded bases of rete ridges (with sparing of the tips of dermal papillae)， and there is vacuolar alteration with necrotic keralinocytes in the basal portion of the epidermis.

【65】Lesions of prurigo nodularis and its excoriated， ulcerated form， namely， picker's nodule， result from persistent rubbing (and scratching)； they represent localized， nodular variants of lichen simplex chronicus. Rather than persistent rubbing of a broad arca to produce a pladuc of lichen simplex chronicus， a smaller spot of skin is assaulted with a blunt object， usually a finger tip or knuckle， to produce a nodule. As a rule， the initiating cause of the pruritus is not identified by history or histologic analysis. Prurigo nodularis occurs mostly in middle-aged persons， especially women. There usually are a few nodules， mostly situated on anatomic sites easily accessible to fingers and fingernails， such as the extensor parts of the fore-arms， the thighs， and the legs. The course is protracted.

【66】There are two basic histologic patterns that result from chronic rub-bing. When the cornificd laver is markedly thickened and completely ortho-keratotic， like that normally present only on palms or soles， we term the lesion the hyperkeratotic type of lichen simplex chronicus. These lesions appear commonly on certain anatomic sites， such as on a lip (as keratosis oris)， on the perianal mucosal-epidermal junction (as a consequence of pru-ritus ani)， on the genitals， and on the scalp. In the second type of lichen simplex， encountered more comionly， the changes in the cornified layer are less impressive than those in the papillary dermis. In this second type， the papillary dermis is markedly thickened by altered collagen， both coars-cned and oriented perpendicularly to the surface of the epidermis. Some-times both patterns are present in a single biopsy specimen. As a rule， however， the hyperkeratotic type of lichen simplex chronicus is not associ-ated with coarse collagen bundles in vertical streaks in a thickened papillary dermis.

【67】Hypertrophic lichen planus is merely one of many manifestations of lichen planus； in this case， in addition to lichen planus there are the changes caused by superimposition of persistent rubbing. Individual lesions are scaly， hyperpigmented plaques or dome-shaped nodules. Although lichen planus is characteristically pruritic， rubbing sufficient to produce the addi-tional changes of lichen simplex chronicus is seen rarely， and then with greater frequency on the legs， especially near the ankles. Other variants of lichen planus include the bullous and atrophic types， those of the nails and mucous membranes， and lichen planopilaris.

【68】Lichen planus， in its classic histologic form， has epidermal hyperplasia with jagged rete ridges， orthokeratosis， and a dense lichenoid， predomi-nantly lymphocytic infiltrate that obscures the dermo-epidermal junctione S1：venly across the entire lesion. With the superimposition of persistent rub-bing， histologic changes of lichen simplex alter the basic pattern of lichen planus. The epidermal hyperplasia becomes even more marked， the bases of the rete ridges become rounded and lose their jagged outline， small foci of parakeratosis may be present in the hyperkeratotic cornified layer， and the band-like infiltrate of lymphocytes develops skip areas， i.e.， sparing the tips of the dermal papillae where there is more coarsening of the collagen bun-dles.

【69】The changes of lichen simplex added to lichen planus are much the same as lichen simplex superimposed on macular amyloidosis to produce lichen amvloidosis.

【70】Clinically， lichen simplex chronicus is a plaque characterized by accen-tuation of normal skin markings， hyperpigmentation， and a keratotic sur-face. Hypertrophic lichen planus consists of purplish papules， nodules， and plaques that are markedly keratotic， especially in the skin overlying the anterior tibia， which is casily accessible to persistent rubhing by a heel.

LICHEN sclerosus et atrophicus and chronic radi-|删除0换行|ation dermatitis are both fibrosing dermatitides that may closely resemble one another when viewed with the scanning objective of the conventional light microscope. Both diseases are characterized by hyperkeratosis， vacuo-lar alteration of the basal layer， subepidermal clefts， sclerosis and fibrin deposition in the dermis， and dilated dermal vascular spaces with a sur-rounding infiltrate of inflammatory cells， extravasated erythrocytes， and pigment-laden macrophages. Both lesions are rubbed commonly， producing compact orthokeratosis. Major features that enable the two conditions to be differentiated are changes in the dermis in lichen sclerosus et atrophicus that arc confined to the papillary dermis， i.e.， there are no changes in the collagen of the reticular dermis. Furthermore， in lichen sclerosus， the ostia of epithelial structures of adnexa are plugged by cornified cells. In contrast， in chronic radiation dermatitis， there is sclerosis at all levels of the dermis and occasionally of the subcutis， and ostia of adnexal structures are not plugged. In addition， there are many more atypical keratinocytes， melano-cytes， and fibroblasts in chronic radiodermatitis， and the dilated blood ves-sels have abnormal shapes and atypical endothelial cells.

【98】Lichen sclerosus et atrophicus， in contrast to chronic radiation derma-titis， is often pruritic rather than painful and most often affects the external genitalia of women. Lichen sclerosus may also affect the genitalia of men， and， when on the glans， is termed balanitis xerotica obliterans. Regardless of location (and it may be extragenital on nearly any cutaneous site)， lesions are hypopigmented papules or plaques showing atrophy characterized by“cigarette-paper”wrinkling， follicular plugging， and telangiectases. As with chronic radiation dermatitis， although with far less frequency， squamous cell carcinomas may develop within lesions of lichen sclerosus et atrophicus on the vulva.

【99】Chronic radiation dermatitis usually occurs in one of two circum-stances. The more common type is the result of radiation therapy， most often administered in fractionated doses for treatment of cutaneous malig-nancies. The second type of chronic radiation dermatitis follows long-term exposures at lower doses and is usually an occupational disease， most often seen in careless dentists and dental assistants who take radiographs without precautions， Patterns of radiation exposure similar to those ofoccupational exposure have been used therapeutically for the treatment of acne， epilation of excess hair， “neurodermatitis，" recalcitrant verrucae， and other benign conditions of the skin.

【100】**Dermatitis from high doses of radiation given over a short period of time， i.e.， as a means of therapy， are seen at the site of treatment beginning severalyears after the initial therapy. The clinical changes are atrophic scars， loss of hair， telangiectases， and hyper- and hypopigmentation. Occu-pational radiation dermatitis is seen most often on the hands， which show drying and scaling， sparse hair， flattening of skin lines， verrucous keratoses， and painful ulcerations. Some cases， usually those on the face， eventuate in scleroderma-like bird-nose facies and warty keratoses. Radiation keratoses， squamous-cell carcinomas， and sarcomas occur with increased frequency in both types of radiation-induced dermatitis.**

【101】**The clinical features of hardness， whiteness， telangiectases， and atro-phy， shared by lichen sclerosus and chronic radiation dermatitis， have simi-lar histologic aspects in both diseases. The hardness results from the altered， sclerotic connective tissue in the dermis. The whiteness resuits from loss of epidermal melanin， as well as from sclerosis in the upper part of the dermis. Telangiectases are dilated vessels， often in increased numbers， within the dermis made all the more visible by epidermal thinning. Atrophy is charac-terized histologically by flattening and thinning of the epidermis but rnostly by flattening of the normal pattern of rete ridges and dermal papillae. If a biopsy specimen is superficial， the two conditions may be indistinguishable histologically， because only those features common to both diseases may be seen in the specimen.**

【126】**_Chronic Urticaria_**

CHRONIC urticaria and the urticarial stage of|删除换行|bullous pemphigoid have several histologic features in common， such as a superficial and mid- or deep dermalperivascular and interstitial mixed-cell infiltrate of neutrophils and eosinophils in addition to lymphocytes and histiocytes， edema in the dermis， and dilated blood vessels. The cardinal features that enable chronic urticaria to be differentiated from urticarial lesions of pemphigoid are that the infiltrate is sparse， there is more edema in the reticular than in the papillary dermis， and neutrophils tend to out-number eosinophils in the inflammatory-cell infiltrate. In contrast， the infil-trate in the urticarial stage of pemphigoid is moderately dense and concen-trated in the papillary dermis， the edema in the papillary dermis is greater than that in the reticular dermis， and eosinophils outnumber neutrophils in the inflammatory-cell infiltrate.

【128】Urticaria is a commonly encountered clinical problem. It has been esti-mated that 15 to 20% of people experience at least one episode of urticaria in their lifetimes. Clinically， a wheal is an edernatous， irregularly shaped， pinkish papule or plaque that blanches upon pressure and itches， often intensely. Individual wheals are transient， not usually persisting for more than 24 hours. If an individual hive persists for longer than 36 hours， it is probably not true urticaria， but rather is part of an urticaria-like process such as an urticarial drug reaction or the urticarial stage of bullous pemphi-goid.

【129】Acute and chronic urticaria are defined by the duration of the entire process rather than by the duration of individual hives. Urticaria is said to be chronic if the process lasts for more than 6 weeks. In reality， hives that come and go for more than a few days are likely to persist for much longer than that， in some patients even for years. The individual wheals in both acute and chronic urticaria tend to disappear in less than 24 hours. Acute urticaria， which is often explosive in onset and may be associated with angioedema， is almost always an allergic response， and the cause is usually identified by the patient， e.g.， an ingestant， inhalant， or injected substance. In contrast， the cause of longlasting， i.e.， chronic， urticaria is practically never identifiable by either patient or physician， and it may be that the mechanism for it is not related to allergy. Hives of acute urticaria respond quickly and effectively to various antihistamines or to systemic corticoste-roids； those of chronic urticaria are not controlled invariably by any medica-tion， although H-1 blocking antihistamines such as hydroxyzine are some-times palliative.

【130】Unlike individual lesions of true hives， the urticarial lesions of pemphi-goid persist for more than 36 hours； some lesions may be surmounted by tense vesicles or bullae. Patients afflicted with pemphigoid tend to be older， i.e.， in their seventh and cighth decades， than those with true urticaria， and the lesions are often accompanied by evidence of excoriations. The urticarial lesions of pemphigoid often assume arcuate， annular， gyrate， and serpigi-nous configurations， Rarely， the lesions disappearr“spontaneously”and completely， but as a rule， their appearance presages the coming of more typical blisters of pemphigoid. True urticaria never vesiculates.

【131】The histologic findings in true urticaria and in urticarial lesions of bullous pemphigoid are quite specific. A sparse superficial and deep peri-vascular and interstitial mixed-cell infiltrate containing eosinophils and neutrophils is virtually diagnostic of chronic urticaria. Urticarial allergic eruptions caused especially by drugs are indistinguishable histologically from the lesions of chronic urticaria. Differentiation histologically of acute urticaria from chronic urticaria is accomplishable. Lesions of acute urti-caria tend to have mostly lymphocytes in the sparse infiltrate and few eosin-ophils. 【1】**Active bleeding originating in the colon： Unless ret-rograde movement of radiotracer from the cecum into the terminal ileum occurs， radiotracer activity in the small bowel is generally not seen after hemorrhage from a colonic bleeding source. The findings in the patient shown are therefore unlikely to be due to an active bleeding site originating in the colon.**

【2】**__ Active small bowel bleeding： Active small bowel hemorrhage can usually be distinguished from that arising in large bowel and further localized to the proximal， mid-， or distal small bowel. The findings of this case make the diagnosis of a mid-small bowel(jejunal) bleeding site the most likely diagnosis.**

【3】**DIAGNOSIS： Acute mid-jejunal gastrointestinal hemorrhage.**

【4】**KEY FACTS**

【5】**_CINICAT_**

【6】**The presence of melena usually denotes bleeding from the esophagus， stomach， or duodenum， but lesions in the jejenum， ileum， and the ascending colon can cause melena， depending on the transit time of blood within the GI tract.**

**__ Hematochezia generally signifies a bleeding site from a source distal to the ligament of Treitz， but rapid hem-orrhage from the esophagus， stomach， or duodenum|删除0换行|with rapid peristalsis can also produce bright red rectal bleeding.**

【8】**Initial attempts to localize a GI bleeding site should include nasogastric tube insertion，esophagogastroduo-denoscopy， sigmoidoscopy， and colonoscopy (which is impaired when the lumen of the colon is obscured by large amounts of brisk bleeding).**

【9】**Peptic ulceration， erosive gastritis， variceal bleeding， and Mallory-Weiss syndrome account for 90% of all cases of upper GI hemorrhage in which a definite cause is found.**

【10】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【11】**The primary purpose of the scintigraphic GI bleeding study is to localize an active bleeding site to serve as a guide before selective abdominal angiography.**

【12】**In general， the rate of bleeding required for scinti-graphic detection of GI bleeding is less than that required for detection by angiography. Therefore， if the scintigraphic GI bleeding study is negative， angiog. raphy is not indicated.**

【13】**Evaluation for GI bleeding by scintigraphy can be per-formed using sulfur colloid. The major disadvantage of this technique is rapid removal of the sulfur colloid by the liver， spleen， and bone marrow. Active bleeding must occur within minutes of radiotracer injection if the bleeding site is to be shown.**

【14】**Because GI bleeding is often intermittent， the labeled red blood cell technique is the preferred method for scintigraphic evaluation. Imaging is performed for a minimum of 2 hours， allowing a reasonable time for bleeding to occur.**

【15】**GI bleeding study findings are evaluated best by reviewing the images in a dynamic cine display(obtained at a rate of 1 frame per minute)， which increases conspicuity of radiotracer movement com pared to sequential static images by making subtle findings more apparent. Dynamic display should be a routine part of the imaging protocol.**

【31】**\*KEY FACTS _CLINICAL_**

【32】**1Neuroendocrine tumors are derived from the amine precursor uptake and decarboxylation (APUD) system and contain secretory granules.**

【33】**Somatostatin， a peptide hormone consisting of 14 amino acids， has a short plasma half-lifc (2 to 4 minutes).**

【34】**Octreotide， a peptide that has eight amino acids， is an analog of somatostatin that is used therapeutically to block secretions from neuroendocrine tumors that contain somatostatin receptors.**

**Somatostatin receptors have been demonstrated in a wide variety of tumors， including pituitary tumors，|删除0换行|gastrinomas， insulinomas， glucagonomas， paragan-gliomas， medullary thyroid carcinomas， pheochromo-cytomas， carcinoid tumors， small cell lung cancer， neuroblastomas， meningiomas， breast cancers， lym phomas， granulomatous diseases， and the thyroid glands of patients with Graves’disease.**

【36】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【37】**Indium-111 octreotide localizes in most ncuroendocrine tumors because they have somatostatin receptors.**

【38】**Indium-111 octreotide imaging can be used to select patients who are likely to respond to octreotide treatment.**

【39】**__ MIBG labeled with either I-131 or I-123 localizes in most neuroendocrine tumors because of the presence of a neuronal pump mechanism for norepinephrine.**

【40】**MIBG and In-111 octreotide demonstrate different metabolic functions， and the images in a patient may be abnormal with one radiotracer but not with the other.**

【41】**Iodine-131 MIBG has been used therapeutically in patients who have neuroendocrine tumors that accu-mulate radiotracer on diagnostic imaging.**

【42】**At present， there is no therapeutic analog of In-111octreotide.**

【49】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【50】** Carcinoma： Carcinoma constitutes 10% to 20% of solitary nonfunctioning nodules. The nodules are usu-ally very firm or hard on palpation. This is the most likely diagnosis.**

【51】**Functioning adenoma： These lesions are usually firm but not hard in texture. This is an unlikely diagnosis because a functioning adenoma would be expected to accumulate Te-99m sodium pertechnetate.**

【52】**Colloid cyst： This entity is usually soft on palpation and therefore unlikely to be the etiology in this case.**

【54】**These lesions are usually well defined by sonography， but biopsy is dcfinitive.**

【55】**Chronic thyroiditis (Hashimoto’s disease)： This is an unlikely diagnosis because chronic thyroiditis is usu-ally multinodular on palpation and has a more inho-mogeneous appearance on radionuclide imaging than the finding in the patient illustrated.**

【56】**Hemorrhage： Hemorrhage into an adenoma or cyst can present as a solitary nodule but is usually tender， making it an unlikely diagnosis in this patient.**

【57】**\*DIAGNOSIS： Thyroid carcinoma.**

【58】**KEY FACTS**

【59】**_CLINICAL_**

【60】**Papillary carcinomas are the most common thyroid neoplasm in North America， are four times more fre-quent in women， and have peak incidence between ages 20 and 40 years. They metastasize primarily via the lymphatic system. Patients with papillary carcino-mas have about a 90% 10-year survival rate.**

【61】**Follicular carcinomas comprise about 15% of thyroid carcinomas and usually occur after 40 years of age. They metastasize via hematogenous spread. Patients with follicular carcinomas have a 10-year survival rate of about 70%.**

【62】**Hurthle cell carcinomas are considered variants of fol-licular cell carcinoma， are relatively rare， and have a variable prognosis.**

【63】**Medullary carcinomas comprise 5% to 10% of thyroid carcinomas. About one-fifth of these patients inherit this disease as part of one of the following three syn-dromes： multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) groups I and 2 and a non-MEN syndrome. The familial non-MEN group has the best prognosis， followed by the familial MEN 2A， and then the nonfamilial (sporadic) form. Familial MEN 2B syndrome has the worst prog nosis. Overall 10-year survival for all patients with medullary carcinoma of the thyroid is about 60%，**

【64】**__ Anaplastic carcinomas comprise about 10% of thyroid carcinomas， usually occur late in life (after the sixth decade)， and have a 5-year survival for all patients with medullary carcinoma of the thyroid rate of <5%.**

【65】**TThe risk of metastasis increases with age at time of diagnosis， particularly for follicular thyroid carcinoma. In addition， recurrence and mortality rates are signifi-cantly higher after 45 years of age.**

【66】**External beam radiation therapy to the neck region before late adolescence increases the risk of developing either or both benign and malignant thyroid nodules.**

【67】**Based on autopsy series， incidental small foci of occult malignant thyroid cells are found in about 10% of patients with no prior clinical evidence of thyroid malignancy.**

【68】**Between 10% and 20% of solitary nonfunctioning nod-ules seen on radioiodine thyroid imaging studies in adults are malignant.**

**(Only 5% of thyroid nodules are hyperfunctioning and cause suppression of normal thyroid tissue. These nod-ules may result in toxic nodular goiter. A very small percentage (2% to 4%) of hyperfunctioning thyroid nodules have been reported to have regions of malig-nant neoplasia. Clinicians who treat toxic nodular goi-ter with radioiodine usually presume the|删除0换行|hyperfunctioning nodule to be of benign histology.**

【70】**With the advent of fine-needle aspiration biopsy， large-needle aspiration biopsy， and large-needle cutting("core”) biopsy as definitive means of evaluating thy-roid nodules， radionuclide imaging studies for this pur-pose are performed infrequently. Nonetheless， these studies can be useful in defining an autonomous func-tioning or hyperfunctioning thyroid nodule， which usually precludes the need for biopsy.**

【71】**A solitary thyroid nodule in a prepubescent child has a higher likelihood of being malignant than that in an adult.**

【72】**1Initial reports suggested that the presence of a diffuse toxic goiter offered protection from developing a thy-roid malignancy. However， it has subsequently been1. shown that the likelihood of a solitary nonfunctioning thyroid nodule being malignant does not differ in patients with diffuse toxic goiter and patients who are euthyroid.**

【73】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【74】**The radiopharmaceutical tracer of choice for thyroid imaging is I-123 sodium iodide. Tec-99m sodium per-technetate， which is less expensive and readily available， is an acceptable alternative. I-131 sodium iodide can be used when I-123 sodium iodide is not available or in patients who are suspected of having a substernal thyroid.**

【75】**Thyroid gland palpation at the time of imaging is mandatory and allows the examiner to outline the thy-roid nodule or superimpose a radionuclide point source marker in the region of the nodule.**

【76】**The hypertrapping nodule on Te-99m sodium pertechnetate images is usually hyperfunctioning on radioiodine images. However， there is an approxj-mately 10% frequency of hypertrapping nodules on a Tc-99m sodium pertechnetate study that are hypo- to nonfunctioning on radioiodine thyroid images (SO-called discordant nodules). Even less frequent are instances in which a nontrapping thyroid nodule on a Tc-99m sodium pertechnetate study is seen to be a functioning nodule on radioiodine imaging.**

【77】**An acronym for the differential diagnosis of solitary nonfunctioning thyroid nodules is CATCH PALLM：Carcinoma， Adenoma， Thyroiditis， Colloid cyst， Hemorrhage， Parathyroid adenoma， Abscess， Lymph node， Lymphoma， and Metastasis.**

【89】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【90】**Low-grade tumor： A low-grade tumor with associ-ated edema can have diminished F-18 FDG uptake. The loss of hippocampal volume， rather than a mass lesion， on the MR image makes this diagnosis unlikely.**

【91】**Radiation necrosis： Tissue necrosis following radia-tion therapy can have diminished F-18 FDG uptake， but the absence of a brain tumor or prior radiation therapy excludes this diagnosis.**

【92】**__ Ictal seizure focus： After F-18 FDG injection at the time of a seizure， increased radiotracer uptake would bc expected rather than the decreased uptake seen in the case presented， making this diagnosis incorrect.**

【93】**Interictal seizure focus： When F-18 FDG is injected at a point when the patient is between seizures (i.e.， interictally)， the uptake of radiotracer in the dormant seizure focus is diminished. This choice， therefore， is the most likely diagnosis.**

【94】**Infarction： Infarcted brain tissue can have diminished F-18 FDG uptake. The clinical history and the fact that the abnormality is confined to the hippocampus on the MR image make this diagnosis unlikely.**

【95】**DIAGNOSIS： Interictal seizure focus.**

【96】**KEY FACTS**

【97】**_CLINICAL_**

【98】**Complex partial seizures (psychomotor or temporal lobe seizures) are frequently preceded by an aura man-ifested by hallucinations， illusions， affective changes， or aberrations of cognition， and often are accompanied by complex movements. These auras are characteristic of a seizure focus in certain regions of the temporal lobe or limbic system.**

【99】**Most complex partial seizures are due to epileptiform activity in the temporal lobes (especially the hippocam-pus or amygdala)， but they can also originate from mesial parasagittal or orbital frontal regions.**

【100】**The surface electroencephalogram (EEG) can be nor-mal in patients with complex partial seizures. Depth electrode placement may be required to define the seizure focus by EEG criteria more accurately.**

【101】**Complex partial seizures can progress to generalized major motor (grand mal) seizures， manifested by loss of consciousness and tonic/clonic movements.**

【102】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【103】**F-18 FDG is a positron-emitting radiopharmaceutical with a half-life of 110 minutes that functions as an ana-log of glucose. It accumulates in viable cells in propor-tion to the individual cellular consumption of glucose.**

【104】** F-18 FDG imaging of the central nervous system is optimally performed at approximately 30 minutes fol-lowing the injection of radiotracer. During the 30-minute delay， the patient should be unstimulated-i.e.， kept in a quiet， dimly lit environment with only back-ground noise.**

【105】**In the evaluation of patients for a seizure focus， an EEG should be acquired during the 30-minute uptake phase of F-18 FDG to document the presence or absence of seizure activity that may not be apparent clinically during this interval.**

【106】**Metabolic imaging with F-18 FDG of patients with seizures can show fuinctional abnormalities even when MRI studies and histologic specimens obtained from the temporal lobe fail to show an abnormality.**

【107】**F-18 FDG imaging is more usefuil for localization of a seizure focus in patients with suspected temporal lobc scizures than in those with a suspccted extratemporal lobe origin of seizure activity.**

【108】**Single-photon emission computed tomography(SPECT) brain perfusion imaging performed in the ictal and interictal statcs has an accuracy similar to F-18 FDG PET in localizing the seizure focus.**

【109】**High-resolution MRI of the hippocampus also has an accuracy similar to F-18 FDG PET in localization of the seiziire site.**

【9】**Amnesia associated with head injury**

【10】**·Head injury is a frequent cause of amnesia， especially in young males.**

【11】**·There are three distinct types of amnesia related to head injury.**

【12】**1FPost-traumatic amnesia (PTA)**

【13】·PTA refers to the period of amnesia following head trauma during which patients fail to acquire new information in normal and continuous fashion， despite being conscious and awake. Patients often deny memory problems， although it is apparent that they cannot learn new information.

【14】Information is not encoded， and is not improved with cues.

【15】The duration of PTA is a reliable marker of the severity of head injury， and also constitutes one of the best predictors of outcome.

【16】2 Retrograde amnesia

【17】·Patients with head injuries often experience defective recall that occurred imme-diately before the injury. Information from the time closest to the injury is most likely to be lost， and the further back in time one goes， the less the impairment.

【18】The extent of retrograde amnesia usually improves as the patients recover.

【19】3AAnterograde amnesia

【20】·Moderate to severe head injuries often cause permanent damage to mesial temporal lobe structures (hippocampus)， resulting in defective learning.

【21】__ The impairment is usually centered on declarative knowledge and patients are usually sensitive to distraction， fatigue， and other influences that can produce suboptimal learning performance.

【22】**Aphasia**

【23】**· Aphasia describes a difficulty in language.**

【24】**· Aphasia should be differentiated from dysarthria， which implies slurred or poorly articulated speech with intact grammar and word selection.**

【25】**·Nearly all aphasic states localize to the left hemispheric cortex. Exceptions include：**

【26】**Left-handed persons (<50%) with language-dominant right hemispheres**

【27】** Severe elevation in ICP or profound metabolic derangements with predominantanomia**

【28】** Thalamic and/or basal ganglia lesions**

【29】**·Aphasia is often associated with right hemiparesis.**

【30】**·Acute onset aphasias are nearly always vascular in origin. Some types of epilepsy may also generate acute onset aphasias， though typically with return of function. Subacute and chronic etiologies include infectious/inflammatory pathologies， space occupying lesions， and several subtypes of dementia.**

【31】**· Strictly speaking， most aphasic states exist on both a categorical and severity continuum. However， categorization is valuable both in attempting to localize a lesion and understanding language function.**

【38】**Apraxia**

【39】**· Apraxia refers to the inability to perform the movement on command when the disturbance could not be attributed to strength， coordination， sensory loss， or impaired comprehension.**

【40】**· Apraxia is less predictable in left-handed individuals than in right-handed ones. Left-handers have right dominance for praxis regardless of which hemisphere is dominant for language. Apraxia in right-handed individuals is almost always associated with a left hemispheric lesion， although only about50% of aphasic patients exhibit apraxia， suggesting that the right hemisphere compensates more readily for apraxia than for aphasia.**

【41】Three types of apraxia are recognized：

【42】1 Limb-kinetic apraxia

【43】 Limb-kinetic apraxia refers to the loss of dexterity and coordination of distal limb movements that cannot be accounted for by weakness or sensory loss.

【44】 It is evident in pantomime， imitation， and use of objects.

【45】 It occurs contralateral to a hemispheric lesion.

【46】2 Ideomotor apraxia

【47】 Ideomotor apraxia refers to the inability to perform a learned movement on command when the disturbance cannot be attributed to weakness， incoordi-nation， sensory loss， or impaired comprehension.

【48】 It is obvious when asking patients to pantomime the use of objects.

【49】This type ofapraxia can occur with lesions in the inferior parietal lobe involv-ing arcuate fasciculus，anterior callosal fibers， and frontal lobe.

【50】**3 Ideational apraxia**

【51】 Ideational apraxia refers to the loss of the ability to pantomime the execution of an act that requires multiple steps to complete.

【52】 This type of apraxia is rare and occurs in diffuse brain lesions， such as head injury or dementia.
