【3】degeneration， in classical pathology， refers to certain alterations in the cyto-plasm of cells and in non-epithelial tissues， e.g.， degeneration of colla-gen.

【4】**degeneration ofcollagen refers to structural and tinctorial changes in bun-dles of collagen， narely， the appearance of smudged bundles stained basophilically. The causes of degeneration of collagen are several， e.g.， anoxemia， the effects of actions of enzymes fiom neutrophils， and elec-trical burns such as inflicted by electrocautery. The word “degenera-tion，" rather than “necrosis，" should be applied to injury to collagen because histopathologic criteria for identification of necrosis involve nuclear changes only， and collagen is an anuclear fiber. Fibrocytes may undergo necrosis， but collagen cannot.**

【5】deposit is a substance， such as mucin， amyloid， or urate， that is not nor-mally present in quantity in the skin.

【6】**desmoplasia designates the fibroplasia that develops in response to certain epithelial neoplasms， such as malignant melanoma， Spitz’s nevus， and breast carcinoma.**

【7】**differentiation is any change whereby things become unlike and， in biology， refers to the process by which， in the course of development， cells be-come modified into a specific form. Differentiation occurs in an em-bryo as germinative cells evolve into tissues and organs， such as the follicular germ into a hair follicle， and in neoplasms that attempt to recapitulate events in an embryo by forming parts of tissues or organs， as is the case， for example， in trichoblastoma. Theoretically， differenti-ation of a neoplasm refers to the relative capability of neoplastic cells to form structures that resemble those in embryonic or mature tissues or organs. In practice， however， it often is difficult to identify， with cer-tainty， embryonal structures， e.g.， subtle follicular germs and papillae， whereas it is much easier to recognize more mature structures in a neoplasm， e.g.， follicular bulbs and papillae. When no evidence of nor-mal structures is apparent， a neoplasm is designated undifferentiated； ATM when seemingly normal structures are apparent， a neoplasm is consid-ered well differentiated， and when there are only vague hints of normal structures， a neoplasm is termed poorly differentiated.**

【8】**Maturation is a kind of differentiation， namely， the specific differ-entiation of cells as they age， e.g.， a basal keratinocyte into a corneo-cyte.**

【9】digitated refers to one type of papillated epidermal proliferation， namely， finger-like projections above the skin surface， as in verruca vulgaris.

【10】DOPA is an acronym for dihydroxyphenylalanine which is oxidized by dopa-oxidase in a positive dopa reaction， i.e.， one in which melanogenesis Occurs.

【11】dyskeratosis refers to premature cornification of individual cells within the viable layers of the epidermis and of epithelial structures of adnexa. Dyskeratotic cells have pyknotic nuclei and cosinophilic cytoplasm that， by electron microscopy， is seen to be packed with filaments of keratin in perinuclear aggregates. These prematurely cornified cells may be encountered in inflammatory diseases like the verrucous stage of incon-tinentia pigmenti； in neoplastic diseases like subungual keratoacantho-mas， solar keratoses， and Bowen’s disease； in genodermatoseslike Darier's discase； and in cystic conditions like warty dyskeratoma. In all instances， dyskeratosis is an expression of premature， but slow， cell death. Rapidly dying keratinocytes do not have time to cornify and this is reflected by a normal basket-woven stratum corneum， as in ery-thema multiforme， fixed drug eruption， or pityriasis lichenoides acuta. Slowly dying keratinocytes cornify so that the stratum corneum is cither parakeratotic or compactly orthokeratotic.

【12】dvskeratotic cell is one that has cornifiedprematurely， with a pyknotic nu-cleus and brightly eosinophilic cytoplasm， as in focal acantholytic dys-keratosis or in squamous-cell carcinoma in situ.

【13】dysplasia， in classical pathology， had a specific meaning， namely， an aber-ration that resulted from abnormal alteration in the embryologic an-lage. Unfortunately， that definition has been perverted in recent years， beginning in gynecologic pathology in regard to morphologic changes in the cervix， “invading”to cutaneous pathology in the realm of pur-ported morphologic findings in a type of melanocytic nevus， and then metastasizing”to pathology of all organs. In regard to melanocytic neoplasia， the term“dysplasia"has not been defined in a repeatable， reliable， and comprehensible fashion. Some pathologists use it synony-mously with “melanocytic nuclear atypia，” others with “disordered hyperplasia，” and still others with “architectural and cytologic atypia.”Many reflective pathologists do not use the term"dysplasia" at all be-cause they understand that to employ it means to obfuscate， rather than clarify， an issue under discussion.

【14】Because the bastardization of the word “dysplasia” has had a re-tarding influence on the study of neoplasia in the cervix， the skin， and
other organs， we advise that it be eschewed. In the realm of melano-cytic neoplasia， for example， there is no place for the terms“dysplasia，”“dysplastic cells，"“dysplastic nevus，"and "dysplastic nevus syndrome.”

【15】ecchymosis is a broad， flat purpuric lesion that results from bleeding into the upper part of the dermis.

【16】elastotic material is synonymous with solar elastosis， i.e.， basophilic spa-ghetti-like connective tissue produced by fibrocytes that for many years have been exposed to damaging effects of sunlight.

【17】**endophytic means growing iinward from the skin surface.**

【18】epidermal hyperplasia refers to increased numbers of spinous cells in the epidermis. We use it as a synonym for acanthosis.

【19】epidermal nevus denotes a congenital malformation characterized by papil-lated or digitated epidermal proliferation accompanied by hyperkera-tosis.

【20】epidermal proliferation refers to increased numbers of spinous cells in the epidermis； we use it as a synonym for acanthosis.

【21】**epidermopoiesis means the making ofepidermis， i.e.， the process of matura-tion whereby epidermal basal cells become transformed into cornified cells.**

【22】epidermotropism describes the movement of cells toward and into the epi-dermis. Neoplasms metastatic to skin sometimes involve the epidermis， in addition to the dermis. The most common of these is melanoma、and epidermotropically metastatic melanoma may be difficult to dif-ferentiate from primary cutaneous melanoma. The stimulus for move-ment of cells of a melanoma into the epidermis is unknown. Neoplastic ymphocytes of mycosis fungoides， especially in the plaque stage of that disease， tend to pepper the epidermis.

【23】epithelioid refers to the cohesive arrangement of non-epithelial cells in a manner like epithelial cells， e.g.， typical epithelioid histiocytes in sar-coidosis and atypical “histiocytes”in epithelioid sarcoma. Epithelioid cells have oval nuclei and pink cytoplasm when stained by hematoxylin and eosin.

【24】**epithelioid tubercle describes a collection of epithelioid histiocytes； when not surrounded by lymphocytes， they are termed naked tubercles， a charac-teristic feature of the granulomas of sarcoidosis and its simulators.**

【25】**epithelium denotes a layer ofcells that covers the surfaces of the body and of membranes that line it. Epithelia are derived from all three germ lay-ers， although most of them arise from ectoderm and endoderm.**

【26】**Epithelia are classified on the basis of their number of layers into simple and stratified， and on the basis of cellular characteristics into squamous， cuboidal， and columnar. Simple squamous epithelium con-sists of a single layer of flat cells like those found in the air spaces of the un gssi.m iElpairt hmeloirap thhoalt line the lumina of blood vessels and body cavities are similar morphologically to simple squamous type， but are classified separately as endothelium and mesothelium， respectively. Simple cu-boidal epithelium may be observed in the lining of the ovary. Simple columnar epithelium appears in portions of many ducts and glands， such as apocrine glands. Specialized columnar epithelium with capa-bility to secrete mucus is characteristic for the lining of the stomach， the cervical canal of the uterus， and the conjunctiva. Pseudostratified columnar epithelium is found in the male urethra and in large excre-tory ducts of a parotid gland and consists of a single layer of tall cells whose nuclei are situated at different levels and thus create the impres-sion of being arranged in several layers. Stratified columnar epithelium may be seen in large ducts ofexocrine glands. Stratified epithelium that does not cornify is typical of mucous membranes of the mouth， upper esophagus， and vagina. Stratified epithelium that cornifies， known also as epidermis， covers the surface of the skin. Transitional epithelium， seen only in the urinary bladder， is comprised of but one or two layers of cells when the bladder is stretched， but numerous layers when the bladder is empty and relaxed.**

【27】**erosion signifies loss of part or all of the epidermis without loss of any dermis， in contrast to ulcer， which denotes loss of the entire epidermis and at least part of the dermis.**

**erythroderma means red skin and refers to nearly universal redness of the skin as occurs mostly in a variety of inflammatory diseases， e.g.， psoria-sis， pityriasis rubra pilaris， and allergic contact dermatitis， but also in a neoplastic disease， i.e.， mycosis fungoides， especially in Sezary’s syn-drome. Allergic reactions to certain drugs may be expressed as erythro-derma. Seborrheic dermatitis is reputed to eventuate in an erythro-derma， but that assumption probably is untrue. A person affected by|删除0换行|an erythroderma may be designated “Thomme rouge，"and an erythro-derma typified by striking desquamation is termed an “exfoliative erythroderma." Study of histopathologic sections from a biopsy speci-men of an erythroderma often enables specific diagnosis to be accom-plished.**

【29】**exo-endophylic means growing outward and inward from the skin surface.**

【30】ecophytic means growing outward from the skin surface.

【31】**fascicles are small bundles of oval or spindle cells that tend to interweave in storiform pattern.**

【32】**fibrillar denotes arrangement in fibrils， i.e.， delicate slender strands of con-nective tissue.**

【33】**fibrin is a filamentous protein derived from fibrinogen by the action of thrombin during coagulation of the blood. It is seen in histologic sec-tions stained by hematoxylin and eosin as fibrillary eosinophilic mate-rial.**

【34】**fibrosis is a formation of fibrous tissue characterized by an increase in the amount of collagen at a particular site. Fibrocytes are increased in number in the early stages of fibrosis， but they are reduced at a much later stage characterized by sclerosis. Fibrosis is a consequence of any pathologic process associated with loss of parenchyma and its frame-work， such as occurs in long-standing inflammatory processes like ca-seous tuberculosis and gummatous syphilis. In general， the quantity of fibrosis is related to the extent of damage to tissue caused by an acute inflammatory process or by a chronic one. Fibroplasia is a synonym for fibrosis. When fibroplasia occurs in response to a benign or malignant neoplasm， it is called "desmoplasia，”e.g.， desmoplastic Spitz’s nevus and desmoplastic melanoma.**

【35】**fibrotic tructs are linear bands of fibrosis that form at sites of follicles that have become extinct as a consequence of the effects of dense infiltrates of inflammatory cells.**

**fibrous septa are struts formed of bundles of collagen and fibrocytes that separate compartments， such as lobules of adipose tissue， from one another. In sections of normal subcutaneous tissue， fibrous septa are thin and outline rectangles of fat lobules. They are oriented both per-|删除0换行|pendicular and parallel to the skin surface. Fibrous septa also are known as fibrous trabecula.**

【37】**fibrous tracts are linear bands of fibrous tissue that form normally behind hair follicles that have retracted in catagen and telogen. They appear independent of any inflammatory-cell infiltrates.**

【38】通用删除16(英):<u>**figurate means to represent by a figure， outline， or visible shape and is usually applied to erythemas like erythema annulare centrifugum. Figurate presentations also are associated with inflammatory diseases like the urticarial stage of bullous pemphigoid， erythema multiforme， and Lyme disease， and the plaque stage of the neoplastic disease， my-cosis fungoides.“Figurate" is a better term for these erythemas than“gyrate，” which means to move in a spiral.**</u>

【39】**foam cells arc lipid-laden macrophages in which the pale cytoplasm con-tains numerous vacuoles from which lipids had been extracted during fixation in formalin and subsequent processing in alcohols of different grades. The lipid nature of the droplets can be demonstrated in frozen sections by fat stains such as scarlet red， oil red O， or Sudan black. Foam cells are not specific for a single pathologic process， but predomi-nate in lipidoses and xanthomatoses， a broad category of diseases char-acterized by deposits of excessive amounts of lipids in various organs of the body， including the skin. Any resolving inflammatory process asso-ciated with degradation of red blood cells consequent to extravasation of numerous erythrocyies， as well as inflammatory processes that in-volve adipose tissue with necrosis of adipocytes， e.g.， lupus erythema-tosus profundus， may be accompanied by foam cells.**

【40】**focal acantholytic dyskeratosis signifies a focus of suprabasal cleft， above which are acantholytic and dyskeratotic cells in the spinous and granu-lar layers， and above them， columns of parakeratosis.**

【41】**follicular germ， imprecisely termed "hair germ，”is a primordium of the folliculo-sebaceous-apocrine unit. It is a crescentic collection of closely-crowded germinative cells at the base of an embryonic epidermis， below which are crowded mesenchymal cells of an embryonic follicu-lar papilla. The basal cells of a follicular germ are columnar and are aligned in a palisade. Follicular germinative cells consist mostly of nu-cleus devoid of a detectable nucleolus； cytoplasm is scant.**

**follicular mucinosis refers to the presence of abnormal collections of acid mucopolysaccharides within the epithelium of hair follicles (and some-|删除0换行|times sebaceous glands)， either as a process sui generis (i.e.， alopecia mucinosa) or secondary to other conditions， such as mycosis fungoides， other cutaneous lymphomas， and angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eo-sinophilia. The term is not a synonym for alopecia mucinosa.

【43】**frond-like means leaf-like.**

【44】germinal centers are characteristic structures of lymph nodes that some-times occur in the skin， especially in pseudolymphomas， but also epi-sodically in lymphomas. Germinal centers consist of macrophages， irmrrulnoblasts， and small and large lymphocytes.

【45】germinative cells designate， among others， cells in the basal layer of the epidermis， follicular matrix， and matrix of a nail， i.e.， those cells that gencrate daughter cells that produce cornified end products， namely， the cornified layer， hair shafts， and nail plates.

【46】glassy membrane is a synonym for the PAS-positive basement membrane that surrounds the inferior part of a hair follicle.

【47】grunulation tissue describes highly vascular， edematous connective tissue that contains a mixed infiltrate of inflammatory cells and that forms in response to some injury， in the case of the skin to those such as incisions andpuncture wounds.

【48】granuloma refers to a collection of histiocytes. Epithelioid histiocytes may be predominant in tuberculoid leprosy， for example， foamy histiocytes in lepromatous leprosy， and both epithelioid histiocytes and foamy his-tiocytes in dimorphous leprosy. Multinucleate histiocytes often are present， in addition to mononuclear histiocytes， in a granuloma. A granuloma may be devoid of inflammatory cells other than histiocytes， e.g.， a naked tubercle of sarcoidosis， or it may be surrounded by a dense mantle of lymphocytes as in some expressions of tuberculosis. When histiocytes are aligned like stakes in a stockade， the arrangement is designated palisaded granuloma. When an abscess is present withi collection of histiocytes， as is common in infections by atypical myco-bacteria and deep fungi， the structure is known as a suppurative granu-loma.

【49】granulomatous dermatitis designates inflammatory-cell infiltrates in which histiocytes predominate. It may be divided into nodular and diffuse types； the nodular type may be subdivided as tuberculoid， sarcoidal， palisaded， suppurative， and foreign body.

【50】guttate means drop-sized and -shaped. The description usually is applied to eruptive lesions of psoriasis and to a distinctive condition termed “gut-tateparapsoriasis" that is unrelated to psoriasis but， as we perceive it， is related to digitate dermatosis， both of which we consider to be ex-pressions of so-called small plaque parapsoriasis， which seems to be among the many morphologic expressions of mycosis fungoides.

【51】hamartoma refers to a circumscribed lesion that has resulted from an error in development and is characterized by an abnormal arrangement of tissues indigenous to an organ. Hamartomas are not neoplasms， be-cause the rate of their growth parallels the growth of the persons who bear them. The termhamartoma” should not be applied to cellular proliferations that begin after tissues have reached maturity structur-ally. Congenital melanocytic nevi of the deep type should be classified as hamartomas， whereas acquired melanocytic nevi are more appro-priately classified as benigin neoplasms. This distinetion is supported by clinical， histopathologic， and biologic differences between melanocytic nevi that are present at birth and those that arise after birth.

【52】hematoma is a nodule formed by bleeding into the lower part of the dermis. subcutaneousfat， or both regions.

【53】“homogenization”ofcollagen refers to a uniform appearance of collagen as a consequence of seeming amalgamation of bundles with loss of the distinctive orthogonal pattern of them. The term is inaccurate because collagen cannot become homogenized. There can be sclerosis， as in late lesions of necrobiosis lipoidica， or packing of bundles of collagen， as in fully developed lesions of scleroderma， but not homogenization.

other organs， we advise that it be eschewed. In the realm of melano-cytic neoplasia， for example， there is no place for the terms“dysplasia，”“dysplastic cells，"“dysplastic nevus，"and "dysplastic nevus syndrome.”

【15】ecchymosis is a broad， flat purpuric lesion that results from bleeding into the upper part of the dermis.

【16】elastotic material is synonymous with solar elastosis， i.e.， basophilic spa-ghetti-like connective tissue produced by fibrocytes that for many years have been exposed to damaging effects of sunlight.

【17】**endophytic means growing iinward from the skin surface.**

【18】epidermal hyperplasia refers to increased numbers of spinous cells in the epidermis. We use it as a synonym for acanthosis.

【19】epidermal nevus denotes a congenital malformation characterized by papil-lated or digitated epidermal proliferation accompanied by hyperkera-tosis.

【20】epidermal proliferation refers to increased numbers of spinous cells in the epidermis； we use it as a synonym for acanthosis.

【21】**epidermopoiesis means the making ofepidermis， i.e.， the process of matura-tion whereby epidermal basal cells become transformed into cornified cells.**

【22】epidermotropism describes the movement of cells toward and into the epi-dermis. Neoplasms metastatic to skin sometimes involve the epidermis， in addition to the dermis. The most common of these is melanoma、and epidermotropically metastatic melanoma may be difficult to dif-ferentiate from primary cutaneous melanoma. The stimulus for move-ment of cells of a melanoma into the epidermis is unknown. Neoplastic ymphocytes of mycosis fungoides， especially in the plaque stage of that disease， tend to pepper the epidermis.

【23】epithelioid refers to the cohesive arrangement of non-epithelial cells in a manner like epithelial cells， e.g.， typical epithelioid histiocytes in sar-coidosis and atypical “histiocytes”in epithelioid sarcoma. Epithelioid cells have oval nuclei and pink cytoplasm when stained by hematoxylin and eosin.

【24】**epithelioid tubercle describes a collection of epithelioid histiocytes； when not surrounded by lymphocytes， they are termed naked tubercles， a charac-teristic feature of the granulomas of sarcoidosis and its simulators.**

【25】**epithelium denotes a layer ofcells that covers the surfaces of the body and of membranes that line it. Epithelia are derived from all three germ lay-ers， although most of them arise from ectoderm and endoderm.**

【26】**Epithelia are classified on the basis of their number of layers into simple and stratified， and on the basis of cellular characteristics into squamous， cuboidal， and columnar. Simple squamous epithelium con-sists of a single layer of flat cells like those found in the air spaces of the un gssi.m iElpairt hmeloirap thhoalt line the lumina of blood vessels and body cavities are similar morphologically to simple squamous type， but are classified separately as endothelium and mesothelium， respectively. Specialized columnar epithelium with capa-bility to secrete mucus is characteristic for the lining of the stomach， the cervical canal of the uterus， and the conjunctiva. Pseudostratified columnar epithelium is found in the male urethra and in large excre-tory ducts of a parotid gland and consists of a single layer of tall cells whose nuclei are situated at different levels and thus create the impres-sion of being arranged in several layers. Stratified columnar epithelium may be seen in large ducts ofexocrine glands. Stratified epithelium that does not cornify is typical of mucous membranes of the mouth， upper esophagus， and vagina. 【27】**erosion signifies loss of part or all of the epidermis without loss of any dermis， in contrast to ulcer， which denotes loss of the entire epidermis and at least part of the dermis.**

**erythroderma means red skin and refers to nearly universal redness of the skin as occurs mostly in a variety of inflammatory diseases， e.g.， psoria-sis， pityriasis rubra pilaris， and allergic contact dermatitis， but also in a neoplastic disease， i.e.， mycosis fungoides， especially in Sezary’s syn-drome. Allergic reactions to certain drugs may be expressed as erythro-derma. Seborrheic dermatitis is reputed to eventuate in an erythro-derma， but that assumption probably is untrue. 【29】**exo-endophylic means growing outward and inward from the skin surface.**

【30】ecophytic means growing outward from the skin surface.

【31】**fascicles are small bundles of oval or spindle cells that tend to interweave in storiform pattern.**

【32】**fibrillar denotes arrangement in fibrils， i.e.， delicate slender strands of con-nective tissue.**

【33】**fibrin is a filamentous protein derived from fibrinogen by the action of thrombin during coagulation of the blood. It is seen in histologic sec-tions stained by hematoxylin and eosin as fibrillary eosinophilic mate-rial.**

【34】**fibrosis is a formation of fibrous tissue characterized by an increase in the amount of collagen at a particular site. Fibrocytes are increased in number in the early stages of fibrosis， but they are reduced at a much later stage characterized by sclerosis. Fibrosis is a consequence of any pathologic process associated with loss of parenchyma and its frame-work， such as occurs in long-standing inflammatory processes like ca-seous tuberculosis and gummatous syphilis. In general， the quantity of fibrosis is related to the extent of damage to tissue caused by an acute inflammatory process or by a chronic one. Fibroplasia is a synonym for fibrosis. When fibroplasia occurs in response to a benign or malignant neoplasm， it is called "desmoplasia，”e.g.， desmoplastic Spitz’s nevus and desmoplastic melanoma.**

【35】**fibrotic tructs are linear bands of fibrosis that form at sites of follicles that have become extinct as a consequence of the effects of dense infiltrates of inflammatory cells.**

**fibrous septa are struts formed of bundles of collagen and fibrocytes that separate compartments， such as lobules of adipose tissue， from one another. In sections of normal subcutaneous tissue， fibrous septa are thin and outline rectangles of fat lobules. They are oriented both per-|删除0换行|pendicular and parallel to the skin surface. Fibrous septa also are known as fibrous trabecula.**

【37】**fibrous tracts are linear bands of fibrous tissue that form normally behind hair follicles that have retracted in catagen and telogen. They appear independent of any inflammatory-cell infiltrates.**

【38】通用删除16(英):<u>**figurate means to represent by a figure， outline， or visible shape and is usually applied to erythemas like erythema annulare centrifugum. Figurate presentations also are associated with inflammatory diseases like the urticarial stage of bullous pemphigoid， erythema multiforme， and Lyme disease， and the plaque stage of the neoplastic disease， my-cosis fungoides.“Figurate" is a better term for these erythemas than“gyrate，” which means to move in a spiral.**</u>

【39】**foam cells arc lipid-laden macrophages in which the pale cytoplasm con-tains numerous vacuoles from which lipids had been extracted during fixation in formalin and subsequent processing in alcohols of different grades. The lipid nature of the droplets can be demonstrated in frozen sections by fat stains such as scarlet red， oil red O， or Sudan black. Foam cells are not specific for a single pathologic process， but predomi-nate in lipidoses and xanthomatoses， a broad category of diseases char-acterized by deposits of excessive amounts of lipids in various organs of the body， including the skin. Any resolving inflammatory process asso-ciated with degradation of red blood cells consequent to extravasation of numerous erythrocyies， as well as inflammatory processes that in-volve adipose tissue with necrosis of adipocytes， e.g.， lupus erythema-tosus profundus， may be accompanied by foam cells.**

【40】**focal acantholytic dyskeratosis signifies a focus of suprabasal cleft， above which are acantholytic and dyskeratotic cells in the spinous and granu-lar layers， and above them， columns of parakeratosis.**

【41】**follicular germ， imprecisely termed "hair germ，”is a primordium of the folliculo-sebaceous-apocrine unit. It is a crescentic collection of closely-crowded germinative cells at the base of an embryonic epidermis， below which are crowded mesenchymal cells of an embryonic follicu-lar papilla. The basal cells of a follicular germ are columnar and are aligned in a palisade. Follicular germinative cells consist mostly of nu-cleus devoid of a detectable nucleolus； cytoplasm is scant.**

**follicular mucinosis refers to the presence of abnormal collections of acid mucopolysaccharides within the epithelium of hair follicles (and some-|删除0换行|times sebaceous glands)， either as a process sui generis (i.e.， alopecia mucinosa) or secondary to other conditions， such as mycosis fungoides， other cutaneous lymphomas， and angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eo-sinophilia. The term is not a synonym for alopecia mucinosa.

【43】**frond-like means leaf-like.**

【44】germinal centers are characteristic structures of lymph nodes that some-times occur in the skin， especially in pseudolymphomas， but also epi-sodically in lymphomas. Germinal centers consist of macrophages， irmrrulnoblasts， and small and large lymphocytes.

【45】germinative cells designate， among others， cells in the basal layer of the epidermis， follicular matrix， and matrix of a nail， i.e.， those cells that gencrate daughter cells that produce cornified end products， namely， the cornified layer， hair shafts， and nail plates.

【46】glassy membrane is a synonym for the PAS-positive basement membrane that surrounds the inferior part of a hair follicle.

【47】grunulation tissue describes highly vascular， edematous connective tissue that contains a mixed infiltrate of inflammatory cells and that forms in response to some injury， in the case of the skin to those such as incisions andpuncture wounds.

【48】granuloma refers to a collection of histiocytes. Epithelioid histiocytes may be predominant in tuberculoid leprosy， for example， foamy histiocytes in lepromatous leprosy， and both epithelioid histiocytes and foamy his-tiocytes in dimorphous leprosy. Multinucleate histiocytes often are present， in addition to mononuclear histiocytes， in a granuloma. A granuloma may be devoid of inflammatory cells other than histiocytes， e.g.， a naked tubercle of sarcoidosis， or it may be surrounded by a dense mantle of lymphocytes as in some expressions of tuberculosis. When histiocytes are aligned like stakes in a stockade， the arrangement is designated palisaded granuloma. When an abscess is present withi collection of histiocytes， as is common in infections by atypical myco-bacteria and deep fungi， the structure is known as a suppurative granu-loma.

【49】granulomatous dermatitis designates inflammatory-cell infiltrates in which histiocytes predominate. It may be divided into nodular and diffuse types； the nodular type may be subdivided as tuberculoid， sarcoidal， palisaded， suppurative， and foreign body.

【50】guttate means drop-sized and -shaped. The description usually is applied to eruptive lesions of psoriasis and to a distinctive condition termed “gut-tateparapsoriasis" that is unrelated to psoriasis but， as we perceive it， is related to digitate dermatosis， both of which we consider to be ex-pressions of so-called small plaque parapsoriasis， which seems to be among the many morphologic expressions of mycosis fungoides.

【51】hamartoma refers to a circumscribed lesion that has resulted from an error in development and is characterized by an abnormal arrangement of tissues indigenous to an organ. Hamartomas are not neoplasms， be-cause the rate of their growth parallels the growth of the persons who bear them. The termhamartoma” should not be applied to cellular proliferations that begin after tissues have reached maturity structur-ally. Congenital melanocytic nevi of the deep type should be classified as hamartomas， whereas acquired melanocytic nevi are more appro-priately classified as benigin neoplasms. This distinetion is supported by clinical， histopathologic， and biologic differences between melanocytic nevi that are present at birth and those that arise after birth.

The term is inaccurate because collagen cannot become homogenized. There can be sclerosis， as in late lesions of necrobiosis lipoidica， or packing of bundles of collagen， as in fully developed lesions of scleroderma， but not homogenization.

【0】cal therapy intervention because the client was referred by the cardiologist who is treating her for cardiac arrhythmia?**

【1】It is not always the case that the referring physician is aware of a client's current cardiovascular status. Referral may not always mean the client is appropriate for participation in an exercise pro-gram. Because the therapist noted the inregular heart rate， he was alert to the possibility of other signs of inappropriate exercise response.

【2】The main red flag here is the abnormal response to exercise stress in someone who is already being treated for a cardiac anomaly (arhythmia). The variable BP and irregular heartbeat suggest an unstable situation.

【3】Result： In this case， it just happened that the client was going from her appointment with the therapist to a visit with her family physician. A note summarizing the therapist's findings， including the vital signs and response to exercise， was sent to the physician.

【4】A copy of the letter was also faxed to the physician's office and to the cardiologist. The therapist followed up with a phone call to the client for an update on her status. The client was given an electrocardiogram (ECG)， which was found to be abnormal， and was admitted to the hospital for further testing.

【5】The therapist was very instrumental in referring this cli-ent， based on medical screening (i.e.， systems review， exercise test) results. Information about the client's cardiovascular status gleaned by the therapist during the assessment was new and important for medical management.

【6】参考段删除-1:<u>From Vernier DA： The meaning of screening. The application of vital signs should be used in physical therapy practice. ADVANCE for Physical _Therapists & PT Assistants 15通用删除7(英):<u>(18)</u>：47-49，2004._</u>

【7】contraction. The upper chambers of the heart contract in an unsynchronized pattern， causing the atrium to quiver rather than to contract and often causing blood to pool， allowing for clots to form. These clots can break loose and travel to the brain， causing a stroke.

【8】Individuals with transient episodes (in and out of AF) or developing a new onset of AF are at greater risk of clot migra-tion than those who have a long-term history， especially if they are already taking blood thinners. Medical consult is more imperative for anyone who has not previously been identified as having AF and/or who is not receiving anticoagulants.

【9】The therapist can easily and quickly screen individuals at risk and teach them to screen themselves by checking the pulse for the telltale signs of an irregular heartbeat. A regular heart-beat is characterized by a series of even and continuous pulsa-tions， whereas an irregular heartbeat often feels like an extra or missed beat. To help determine the steadiness of the heartbeat， the therapist or individual keeps time by tapping the foot.

【10】Risk Factors. Persons at risk for fibrillation who require screening include those who have had a previous heart attack or a history that includes high BP， CHF， digitalis toxicity， pericarditis， or rheumatic mitral stenosis.

【11】Other factors that can overstimulate the sinus node include emotional stress， excessive production of thyroid hormone(hyperthyroidism)， alcohol and caffeine consumption， and high fevers. In many instances， particularly in younger per-sons， there is no apparent cause.

【12】Recent studies have shown that presence of the organism Helicobacter pylori in the stomach is associated with persis-tent AF. In addition， high concentrations of CRP， which con-firm the presence of systemic inflammation， are present in people with AF. A potential noncardiovascular disease that predisposes to AF may be chronic gastritis caused by chronic7H. pylori infection.

【13】Clinical Signs and Symptoms. Symptoms of fibrilla-tion vary， depending on the functional state of the heart and the location of the fibrillation. Fibrillation may exist with-out symptoms. The affected individual is usually aware of the irregular heart action and reports feeling “palpitations.”Careful questioning may be required to pinpoint the exact description of sensations reported by the client.

Some individuals experience the symptoms of inadequate blood flow and low oxygen levels， such as dizziness， chest pain， and fainting. Chronic AF may cause CHF， which is|删除0换行|often experienced as shortness of breath during exercise and fluid accumulation in the feet and legs.

【15】More than six palpitations occurring in 1 minute or pro-longed， repeated palpitations， especially if accompanied by chest pain， dyspnea， fainting， or other associated signs and symptoms， should be reported to the physician.

【18】**Sinus Tachycardia**

【19】Sinus tachycardia， defined as an abnormally rapid heart rate， usually taken to be more than 100 bpm， is the normal physiologic response to such stressors as fever， hypoten-sion， thyrotoxicosis， anemia， anxiety， exertion， hypovole-mia， pulmonary emboli， myocardial ischemia， CHF， and shock.

【20】Sinus tachycardia is usually of no physiologic significance； however， in clients with organic myocardial disease， the result may be reduced cardiac output， CHF， or arrhythmias. Because heart rate is a major determinant of oxygen require-ments， angina or perhaps an increase in the size of an infarc-tion may accompany persistent tachycardia in clients with CAD.

【21】Clinical Signs and Symptoms. The symptoms of tachy-cardia vary from one person to another and may range from an increased pulse to a group of symptoms that would restrict normal activity of the client. Anxiety and apprehension may occur， depending on the pain threshold and emotional reac-tion of the client.

【22】**CLINICAL SIGNS AND SYMPTOMS**

【23】**_Sinus Tachycardia_**

| **Restlessness**  |

【25】**Sinus Bradycardia**

【26】In sinus bradycardia， impulses travel down the same pathway as in sinus rhythm， but the sinus node discharges at a rate less than 60 bpm. Bradycardia may be normal in athletes or young adults and is therefore asymptomatic.

【27】In most cases， sinus bradycardia is a benign arrhythmia and may actually be beneficial by producing a longer period of diastole and increased ventricular filling. In some clients who have acute MI， it reduces oxygen demands and may help minimize the size of the infarction.

【28】Eye surgery， meningitis， intracranial tumors， cervical and mediastinal tumors， and certain disease states (e.g.， MI， myx-edema， obstructive jaundice， and cardiac fibrosis) may pro-duce sinus bradycardia.

【29】Clinical Signs and Symptoms. Syncope may be pre-ceded by sudden onset of weakness， sweating， nausea， pallor， vomiting， and distortion or dimming of vision. Signs and symptoms remit promptly when the client is placed in the horizontal position.

【30】Physician referral for sinus bradycardia is needed only when symptoms， such as chest pain， dyspnea， light-headedness， or hypotension occur.

【31】**CLINICAL SIGNS AND SYMPTOMS**

| --- |
| **Sinus Bradycardia**  |
| **Reduced pulse rate**  |

【33】**CARDIOVASCULAR DISORDERS**

【34】**Hypertension**

【35】Blood pressure is the force against the walls of the arteries and arterioles as these vessels carry blood away from the heart. When these muscular walls constrict， reducing the diameter of the vessel， BP rises； when they relax， increasing the ves-sel diameter， BP falls .

【36】A high BP reading is usually a sign that the vessels can-not relax fully and remain somewhat constricted， requiring the heart to work harder to pump blood through the ves-sels. Over time the extra effort can cause the heart muscle to become enlarged and eventually weakened. The force of blood pumped at a high pressure can also produce small tears in thelining of the arteries， weakening the arterial vessels. The evidence of this effect is most pronounced in the vessels of the brain， kidneys， and the small vessels of the eye.

【37】Hypertension is a major cardiovascular risk factor， associ-ated with elevated risks of cardiovascular diseases， especially MI， stroke， PVD， and cardiovascular death. Although dia-stolic changes were always evaluated closely， research now shows that the risks increase progressively as systolic pressure goes up， especially in adults over the age of 50 years.删除14:<u>76，77</u>

【38】Hypertension is often considered in conjunction with peripheral vascular disorders for several reasons： both are dis-orders of the circulatory system， the course of both diseases are affected by similar factors， and hypertension is a major risk factor in atherosclerosis， the largest single cause of PVD.

Hypertension is defined by a pattern rn(of consistentlyelevated diastolic pressure， systolic pressure， or both mea-sured over a period of time， usually several months. Medical|删除0换行|researchers have developed classifications for BP based on risk .

【40】A 2014 clinical practice guideline from panel members of the Eighth Joint National Committee suggested that in patients aged over 60 years， blood pressure should be targeted to <150/90 mm Hg. This guideline is based on the influence of age and comorbidities affecting hypertension. Those patients under 60 years and those patients with diabetes or chronic kidney disease should be targeted to 140/90 mm Hg， whereas those over 80 years should be targeted at <150/90 mm Hg.

【41】**Pulse Pressure**

【42】See Chapter 4 for more information on this topic.

【43】**Blood Pressure Classification**

【44】Hypertension can also be classified according to type (systolic or diastolic)， cause， and degree of severity. Primary (or essen- _tial) hypertension is also known as idiopathic hypertension and_ accounts for 90% to 95% of all hypertensive clients.

【45】Secondary hypertension results from an identifiable cause， including a variety of specific diseases or problems such as renal artery stenosis， oral contraceptive use， hyperthyroid-ism， adrenal tumors， and medication use.

【46】Originally， birth control pills contained higher levels of estrogen， which was associated with hypertension， but today the estrogen and progestin contents of the pill are greatly reduced. The risk of high BP with oral contraceptive use is now considered quite low， but using oral contraceptives does still increase the risk of heart attack， stroke， and blood clots in certain women (e.g.， age over 35 years， tobacco use， diabetes).

【47】The risk may be increased for older women who smoke， but the risk for all women returns to normal after they discon-tinue the pill. The risk of venous thromboembolism associated with newer oral contraceptives remains under investigation.

【48】Drugs that constrict blood vessels can contribute to hyper-tension. Among the most common are phenylpropanolamine in over-the-counter (OTC) appetite suppressants， including herbal ephedra， pseudoephedrine in cold and allergy rem-edies， and prescription drugs such as monoamine oxidase(MAO) inhibitors (a class of antidepressant) and corticoste-roids when used over a long period.

【49】Intermittent elevation of BP interspersed with normal _readings is called labile hypertension or borderline hyperten-_ sion. More and more adults over age 50 years and many older adults have a type of high BP called isolated systolic hyperten-sion (ISH) characterized by marked elevation of the systolic pressure (140 mm Hg or higher) but normal diastolic pres-sure (less than 90 mm Hg).

【50】ISH is a risk factor for stroke and death from cardiovas-cular causes. Elevated systolic pressure also raises the risk of heart attack， CHF， dementia， and end-stage kidney disease.80It has been suggested that for every 10 mm Hg rise in systolic pressure there is a 26% increase in mortality.删除14:<u>81</u>

Two other types of hypertension include masked hyperten-sion (normal in the clinic but periodically high at home) and white-coat hypertension， a clinical condition in which the cli-ent has elevated BP levels when measured in a clinic setting|删除0换行|by a health care professional. In such cases， BP measurements are consistently normal outside of a clinical setting.

【52】Masked hypertension may affect up to 10% of adults； white-coat hypertension occurs in 15% to 20% of adults with stage I hypertension.82 These types of hypertension are more common in older adults. Antihypertensive treatment for white-coat hypertension may reduce office BP but may not affect ambulatory BP. The number of adults who develop sustained high BP is much higher among those who have masked or white-coat hypertension.删除14:<u>82</u>

【53】At-home BP measurements can help identify adults with masked hypertension， white-coat hypertension， ambulatory hypertension， and individuals who do not experience the usual nocturnal drop in BP (decrease of 15 mm Hg)， which is a risk factor for cardiovascular events.83 Excessive morning BP surge is a predictor of stroke in older adults with known hypertension and is also a red flag sign. Medical referral is indicated in any of these situations.

【54】**Risk Factors**

【55】Modifiable risk factors for hypertension are primarily life-style factors such as stress， obesity， and poor diet or insuf-ficient intake of nutrients . Stress has been shown to cause increased peripheral vascular resistance and cardiac output and to stimulate sympathetic nervous system activity. Potassium deficiency can also contribute to hypertension.

【56】The Seventh Report of the Joint National Committee on Prevention， Detection， Evaluation， and Treatment of High Blood Pressure 通用删除1(英):<u></u> suggested adding a BP category called “prehypertension”to identify adults consid-ered to be at risk for developing hypertension and to alert both individuals and health care providers of the importance of adopting lifestyle changes. Screening for prehypertension provides important opportunities to prevent hypertension and cardiovascular disease.84 There have also been suggestions from others such as the Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT) to adopt a lower systolic blood pressure of120 mm Hg. Afinding in the SPRINT was that cardiovascular disease and death was reduced by 25% and all-cause mortal-ity by 27% in patients who reached the target of <120 mmHg. This trial did restrict study to th Hg1ose hypertensive adults， including older adults (>75 years of age)， who were at an above-average risk for developing cardiovascular disease， and diabetic patients and those that already had a CVA.85-87

【58】Nonmodifiable risk factors include family history， age， gen-der， postmenopausal status， and race. The risk of hyperten-sion increases with age as arteries lose elasticity and become less able to relax. There is a poorer prognosis associated with early onset of hypertension.

【59】A sex-specific gene for hypertension may exist88 because men experience hypertension at higher rates and at an earlier age than women do until after menopause. Hypertension is the most serious health problem for African Americans (both men and women and at earlier ages than for whites) in the United States .

【60】**Clinical Signs and Symptoms**

【61】Clients with hypertension are usually asymptomatic in the early stages， but when symptoms do occur， they include occipital headache (usually present in the early morning)， vertigo， flushed face， nocturnal urinary frequency， spon-taneous nosebleeds， and blurred vision .

【64】**Transient Ischemic Attack**

【65】Hypertension is a major cause of heart failure， stroke， and kidney failure. Aneurysm formation and CHF are also associ-ated with hypertension. Persistent elevated diastolic pressure damages the intimal layer of the small vessels， which causes an accumulation of fibrin， local edema， and possibly intra-vascular clotting.

【66】Eventually， these damaging changes diminish blood flow to vital organs， such as the heart， kidneys， and brain， result-ing in complications such as heart failure， renal failure， and cerebrovascular accidents or stroke.

【67】Many persons have brief episodes of transient ischemic attacks (TIAs). The attacks occur when the blood supply to part of the brain has been temporarily disrupted. These isch-emic episodes last from 5 to 20 minutes， although they may last for as long as 24 hours. TIAs are considered by some as a progression of cerebrovascular disease and may be referred to as“ministrokes."

TIAs are important warning signals that an obstruction exists in an artery leading to the brain. Without treatment，10% to 20% of people will go on to have a major stroke within3 months， many within 48 hours.89 Immediate medical refer-ral is advised for anyone with signs and symptoms of TIAs， especially anyone with a history of heart disease， hyperten-sion， or tobacco use. Other risk factors for TIAs include age|删除0换行|(over 65 years)， diabetes， and being overweight. The ABCD90score is used and supported by the American Heart Associa-tion and American Stroke Association guidelines to triage patients with a TIA for hospitalization. The ABCD score is calculated as follows： age greater than or equal to 60 years (1point)； blood pressure greater than or equal to 140/90 mm Hg upon presentation (1 point)； clinical features： unilateral weakness (2 points) or speech/language impairment without weakness (1 point)； duration greater than or equal to 60 min-utes (2 points) or 10 to 59 minutes (1 point)； and diabetes mellitus (1 point). The ABCD score can vary from 0 to 7and increasing scores predict increased risk of a CVA.

【71】Orthostatic hypotension is an excessive fall in BP of 20 mm Hg or more in systolic BP or a drop of 10 mm Hg or more of both systolic and diastolic arterial BP on assumption of the erect position with a 10% to 20% increase in pulse rate(Case Example 6.10). It is not a disease but a manifestation of abnormalities in normal BP regulation.

The last category includes diseases _.1，_ affecting the autonomic nervous system， such as Guillain-Barre syndrome， diabetes mellitus， or multiple sclerosis.

【141】**A. General considerations：**

【142】**1\. The cerebellum is parcellated both anatomically and functionally into specific zones.**

【143】**a. The archicerebellum consists of the flocculonodu-lar lobe； it has major connections with the vestibu-lar system and is important for control of eye move-ments.**

【144】b. The paleocerebellum is composed of the vermis of the anterior lobe (lobule I-V) as well as the pyra-mis， uvula and paraflocculus. Most of its afferents are from the spinal cord. Its major functional role involves muscle tone and control of axial and limb moyements.

【145】**c. The neocerebellum comprises the middle vermis and the hemispheres.**

【146】d. The cerebellar cortex may be divided into longitu-dinal zones that project to specific nuclei.

【147】1) The vermal zone projects to the fastigial nucleus

【148】2) The intermediate zone projects to the nucleus globosus and emboliformis

【149】**3) The lateral zone projects to the dentate nucleus e. The somatotopic representation within each nu-cleus is：**

【150】**1) Caudal body parts are anterior； rostral parts pos-terior， trunk is lateral； limbs medial.**

【151】**f. Functional anatomy of the nuclei：**

【152】**1) Fastigial nucleus**

【153】**a) Upright posture， muscles of the trunk**

【154】**b) Important for sitting， standing and walking**

【155】2) The globosus and emboliform nuclei：

**a) Involved with segmental reflexes that control stability|删除0换行|b) Important for the initiation of movements de-rived from somatosensory input (propriocep-tion)|删除0换行|c) Stabilizes proximal joints that facilitate pyra-midal movements

【163】**a) Important in the facility of fine movement by promoting their initiation， coordinating exten-sor and flexor musculature at multiple joints， controlling the spatial coordination of hard and finger movements. Lesions of the nu-cleus and its connections cause postural ki-netic tremors (rubral tremor). This tremor is distinguished by increasing amplitude of os-cillation that occurs at right angles to the line of movement**

【164】**The Afferent and Efferent Cerebellar Pathways of Clinical Relevance**

【165】**_Inferior Cerebellar Peduncle_**

【166】**This is known as the restiform body and is most often in-volved in vertebral artery and PICA strokes， as well as by compression from tumors， demyelinating disease and stroke.**

【167】**a. It is comprised of：**

【168】**1) The dorsal spinal cerebellar tract which carries pro-prioceptive and exteroceptive information from the lower extremity and trunk. Cervical spondylosis and any spinal cord compressive disease， as well as the re-viewed acquired and congenital diseases of the cervical cord affect this pathway. No patient with signifieant cervical stenosis from any cause can tandem walk. It originates from Clarke's column of the spinal cord.**

【169】**2) The cuneocerebellar tract that arises from the external arcuate nucleus and relays proprioceptive information from the arm and neck**

【170】**3) The vestibulocerebellar tract projects bilaterally to the flocculonodular lobe. A cause of cervical induced nys-tagmus.**

【171】**4) Reticulocerebellar tracts from the lateral and parame-dian nuclei of the brainstem are important for tone and cerebellar influences on segmental reflexes**

【172】5) The arcuate cerebellar tract arising from the medullary arcuate nuclei

【173】**6) Trigeminocerebellar tract which originates in the spinal and main sensory nuclei of cranial nerve V. This nu-cleus is important for migraine， head pain， and facial reflexes (trigeminal reflexes， i.e.， light causing cough)**

【174】**7) Olivocerebellar tract is an afferent tract for somatic modalities from the contralateral inferior olivary nu-cleus.**

【176】1\. Fastigiobulbar tract (juxtarestiform body) and cerebellar reticular efferents)

【177】**_The Middle Cerebellar Peduncle (the Brachium Pontis)_**

【178】**Connects the cerebellum to the pons. Corticospinal fibers synapse in the pontine gray， project to the intermediate zone of the cerebellum and thence to the cerebellar zone of the thalamus in the ventrolateral nucleus. These afferents then project to area 3b of the somato sensory cortex and thence to area 4 of the primary motor cortex.**

【179】Lesions of this distributed pathway cause specific symp-tom complexes at each level of involvement.

**Pontine grey lesions cause hemiparesis and ataxia of the contralateral side. Descending corticospinal fibers are respon-sible for the weakness and are the origin of the middle cere-|删除0换行|bellar peduncle (MCP) which projects to the intermediate zone of the cerebellum and then to the thalamus and cortex. A cause of ataxic gait.**

【181】**The lateral zone of the cerebellum， if involved， causes greater ataxia of the arm then the leg as does involvement of the middle cerebellar peduncle. Thalamic lesions involving cerebellar radiations are notable for ataxia of stance. Disrup-tion of cerebellar connections from 3 b of SI to M1 of area 4cause Brunn's frontal lobe ataxia.**

【182】**_The Superior Cerebellar Peduncle (SCP)_**

【183】**The superior cerebellar peduncle is the primary connection of the cerebellum to the midbrain. It is the primary efferent pathway of the cerebellum.**

【184】**The clinically most important efferent pathways are the dentatorubral and dentothalamic tracts which are the anatomic basis of the postural kinetic and cerebellar outflow tremors， seen with midbrain and thalamic lesions.**

【139】**CEREBELLAR DISEASE**

【141】**A. General considerations：**

【142】**1\. The cerebellum is parcellated both anatomically and functionally into specific zones.**

【143】**a. The archicerebellum consists of the flocculonodu-lar lobe； it has major connections with the vestibu-lar system and is important for control of eye move-ments.**

【144】b. The paleocerebellum is composed of the vermis of the anterior lobe (lobule I-V) as well as the pyra-mis， uvula and paraflocculus. Most of its afferents are from the spinal cord. Its major functional role involves muscle tone and control of axial and limb moyements.

【145】**c. The neocerebellum comprises the middle vermis and the hemispheres.**

【146】d. The cerebellar cortex may be divided into longitu-dinal zones that project to specific nuclei.

【147】1) The vermal zone projects to the fastigial nucleus

【148】2) The intermediate zone projects to the nucleus globosus and emboliformis

【149】**3) The lateral zone projects to the dentate nucleus e. The somatotopic representation within each nu-cleus is：**

【150】**1) Caudal body parts are anterior； rostral parts pos-terior， trunk is lateral； limbs medial.**

【151】**f. Functional anatomy of the nuclei：**

【152】**1) Fastigial nucleus**

【153】**a) Upright posture， muscles of the trunk**

【154】**b) Important for sitting， standing and walking**

【155】2) The globosus and emboliform nuclei：

**a) Involved with segmental reflexes that control stability|删除0换行|b) Important for the initiation of movements de-rived from somatosensory input (propriocep-tion)|删除0换行|c) Stabilizes proximal joints that facilitate pyra-midal movements

【157】**d) Lesions cause：**

【158】**1) Delayed check**

【159】**2) Truncal titubation**

【160】3) Oscillation of the extremities

【161】e) Facilitate control of oscillations during the last 1/3 of movement.

【162】3) The dentate nucleus

【163】**a) Important in the facility of fine movement by promoting their initiation， coordinating exten-sor and flexor musculature at multiple joints， controlling the spatial coordination of hard and finger movements. Lesions of the nu-cleus and its connections cause postural ki-netic tremors (rubral tremor). This tremor is distinguished by increasing amplitude of os-cillation that occurs at right angles to the line of movement**

【164】**The Afferent and Efferent Cerebellar Pathways of Clinical Relevance**

【165】**_Inferior Cerebellar Peduncle_**

【166】**This is known as the restiform body and is most often in-volved in vertebral artery and PICA strokes， as well as by compression from tumors， demyelinating disease and stroke.**

【167】**a. It is comprised of：**

【168】**1) The dorsal spinal cerebellar tract which carries pro-prioceptive and exteroceptive information from the lower extremity and trunk. Cervical spondylosis and any spinal cord compressive disease， as well as the re-viewed acquired and congenital diseases of the cervical cord affect this pathway. No patient with signifieant cervical stenosis from any cause can tandem walk. It originates from Clarke's column of the spinal cord.**

【169】**2) The cuneocerebellar tract that arises from the external arcuate nucleus and relays proprioceptive information from the arm and neck**

【170】**3) The vestibulocerebellar tract projects bilaterally to the flocculonodular lobe. A cause of cervical induced nys-tagmus.**

【171】**4) Reticulocerebellar tracts from the lateral and parame-dian nuclei of the brainstem are important for tone and cerebellar influences on segmental reflexes**

【172】5) The arcuate cerebellar tract arising from the medullary arcuate nuclei

【173】**6) Trigeminocerebellar tract which originates in the spinal and main sensory nuclei of cranial nerve V. This nu-cleus is important for migraine， head pain， and facial reflexes (trigeminal reflexes， i.e.， light causing cough)**

【174】**7) Olivocerebellar tract is an afferent tract for somatic modalities from the contralateral inferior olivary nu-cleus.**

【175】**_Efferent Tracts in the inferior Cerebellar Peduncle_**

【176】1\. Fastigiobulbar tract (juxtarestiform body) and cerebellar reticular efferents)

【177】**_The Middle Cerebellar Peduncle (the Brachium Pontis)_**

【178】**Connects the cerebellum to the pons. Corticospinal fibers synapse in the pontine gray， project to the intermediate zone of the cerebellum and thence to the cerebellar zone of the thalamus in the ventrolateral nucleus. These afferents then project to area 3b of the somato sensory cortex and thence to area 4 of the primary motor cortex.**

【179】Lesions of this distributed pathway cause specific symp-tom complexes at each level of involvement.

**Pontine grey lesions cause hemiparesis and ataxia of the contralateral side. Descending corticospinal fibers are respon-sible for the weakness and are the origin of the middle cere-|删除0换行|bellar peduncle (MCP) which projects to the intermediate zone of the cerebellum and then to the thalamus and cortex. A cause of ataxic gait.**

【181】**The lateral zone of the cerebellum， if involved， causes greater ataxia of the arm then the leg as does involvement of the middle cerebellar peduncle. Thalamic lesions involving cerebellar radiations are notable for ataxia of stance. Disrup-tion of cerebellar connections from 3 b of SI to M1 of area 4cause Brunn's frontal lobe ataxia.**

【182】**_The Superior Cerebellar Peduncle (SCP)_**

【183】**The superior cerebellar peduncle is the primary connection of the cerebellum to the midbrain. It is the primary efferent pathway of the cerebellum.**

【184】**The clinically most important efferent pathways are the dentatorubral and dentothalamic tracts which are the anatomic basis of the postural kinetic and cerebellar outflow tremors， seen with midbrain and thalamic lesions.**

【16】**IDENTIFYING ALARM SYMPTOMS**

【17】Chest pain by itself is an alarm symptom because it can be due to serious causes that require prompt attention. By far， the most common serious cause is acute cardiac isch-emia， which includes stable angina， UA， and MI. Albeit less common， other serious conditions to be considered include aortic dissection， PE， spontaneous pneumothorax， pneumo-nia， and acute GI processes (eg， cholecystitis， pancreatitis) with referred pain.

【18】In general， the suspicion for these serious diagnoses is raised by the results of careful questioning regarding the charac-ter and pattern of the pain， associated symptoms， and associated medical conditions. A primary distinction is the differentiation of anginal pain from noncardiac chest pain.

The first step is to determine the acuity of the symptoms. Although there may be overlap， chronic and recurring episodes without any change in symptom pattern are less likely to be emergent and may be evaluated in the outpatient setting. Such diagnoses will include stable angina， Gl pain， and musculosk-eletal pain. In contrast， an acute or ongoing chest pain episode is more likely to represent an urgent situation and should be evaluated in the ED or inpatient setting. These diagnoses will include UA， MI， aortic dissection， PE， pericarditis， and pneu-mothorax. In both situations， it is important to assess for alarm|删除0换行|symptoms and the probability of underlying CAD. Keep in mind， however， that in addition to the history， proper deci sion making will also necessitate a targeted physical exami-nation， ECG， and other laboratory testing， as appropriate. See Figure 27-1 for the diagnostic algorithm for chest pain.

【36】Angina is often precipitated by effort or physical activity. Thus， it is important to determine whether functional limitations preclude proper assessment of effort-related chest pain or， conversely， whether effort-related chest pain is limiting the patient’s physical activity.

Therapeutic approaches include glucose infusions， diazoxide or octreotide therapy， and， some-times， subtotal pancreatectomy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[178-180\]</u>. Physiologic and morphologic studies have recently indicated that PHHI is a hyperfunctional β-cell disorder associated with different patho-logic changes 通用删除6(英):<u>\[181\]</u>. In addition， molecular studies have dem-|删除0换行|onstrated that PHHI results from at least three different genetic defects： 通用删除7(英):<u>(1)</u> The first are mutations in the two subunits SURI and KIR6.2 genes of the sulfonylurea receptor (SUR) at locus11p15.1通用删除6(英):<u>\[182-184\]</u>. 【63】_Focal PHHI_ Focal PHHI is found in a quarter to a half of all cases of PHHI 通用删除6(英):<u>\[124，185\]</u>. Macroscopically， the pancreas has a normal appearance. Usually the lesion is unifocal 通用删除6(英):<u>\[124\]</u> and it has been located either in the head and body 通用删除6(英):<u>\[179\]</u> or in the body and tail of the pancreas 通用删除6(英):<u>\[181\]</u>. Focal lesions require systematic analysis of serial sections of all available pancreatic tissue to be detected. Histologically， there is an accumulation of islet cell clusters， which are separated by thin rims of acinar cells or strands of connective tissue. Occasionally they may be attached to small ducts forming ductulo-insular complexes. Some cells are large and display hypertrophic nuclei and the proliferation rate seems to be increased. By using immunohis-tochemistry islet-like clusters appear to be composed of all four islet cell types； however， B cells are more numerous than in normal islets， representing 70-90% of all endocrine cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[181\]</u>. B cells are large， strongly immunoreactive for proinsulin， and show an ultrastructural pattern of functional hyperactivity. The islets outside the focus show endocrine cells with normal size. appearance， and distribution.

【64】_Diffuse PHHI_ Diffusenesidioblastosis is the mostfrequent proliferative lesion associated with PHHI. As in focal PHHI. the pancreas displays no gross abnormalities. Histologically， nesidioblastosis involves diffusely the tail and the body， while the head is less frequently affected. The key lesions are β cell hypertrophy as evidenced by nuclear enlargement通用删除6(英):<u>\[192\]</u>，prom-inent ductulo-insular complexes， abundant poorly defined endocrine cell clusters (some large) with often irregular out-lines， and islets of variable size 通用删除6(英):<u>\[181，187，188，193，194\]</u>.Mor-phometric studies revealed an increased nuclear volume of B cells in comparison to age-matched controls. A tetraploid pat-tern of DNA content has been found in enlarged β cell nuclei. Immunohistochemical investigations have found a tendency for an increased number of β cells anda decrease in 8cells， with an increased β to 8cell ratio 通用删除6(英):<u>\[189，195\]</u>. In a minority of patients， routine histology， despite systematicinvestigation of serial sec-tions， fails to reveal clear-cut diagnostic lesions. Immunohis-tochemical analysis may disclose subtle differences from age-matched controls

Its function is to tighten during contralateral rotation and contralateral side flexion， initially transferring rotational forces to the axis from the head， and then to limit rotation and side flex-ion of the atlanto-occipital and atlantoaxial segments.**

Because the occiput and the axis are directly connected by the ligament， induced rotation of the axis should be immediate and in the same direction as the side flexion. The test is carried out with the patient lying supine or seated and the therapist palpating the spinous proccss of the axis. The head is side flexed around the axis of the craniovertebral joints (around the nose)， and the therapist fcels for immediatc contralateral motion of the spin-ous process as the axis rotates to the same side. For flexion and extension.**

【27】**Assessment of the Vertebrobasilar System**

**Clinical testing for vertebrobasilar ischemia is based on construct va-lidity and not criterion validity， so the tests are only assumed to be|删除0换行|effective because they make sense in the light of the understood anatomy， physiology， pathology， and pathophysiology. Their sensitiv-ity and specificity is unknown， so it is not possible to say that a nega-tive test categorically clears the patient's vertebrobasilar system. Rather， if the tests do demonstrate a problem， there is a greater or lesser de-gree of probability that there is a vertebral artery defect， depending on the sign or symptom elicited (that is whether it is cardinal or noncar-dinal). One study on one patient found that the objective clinical tests commonly used in the investigation of vertebrobasilar insufficiency(Hautard’s， Maine’s， Smith and Estridge’s， and Underberg’s) failed to demonstrate a problem on a patient who was known to have an oc-cluded artery. However， even with the lack of research evidence， test-ing the vertebral artery is a resonable procedure provided certain pre-cautions are taken. It should be understood that testing the integrity of the artery is not simply carrying out Hautard’s or one of the other tests but also including such tests into the overall neurological examination， including the history. In the case study in which the so-called vertebral artery tests failed to predict the presence of vertebrobasilar pathology， the overall examination did. Although the examination is principally for the vertebrobasilar system， the therapist is using central nervous system function as a monitor. It has been established that damage to the central system is relatively common in motor vehicle accidents (dis-cussed earlier)， and the therapist will more likely pick up signs of con-cussion or possibly more serious neurological damage than verte-brobasilar ischemia in this examination. Contraindications for testing the vertebral artery include**

【29】**A history of cardinal signs and/or symptoms**

【30】**The presence of a fracture**

【31】**The presence of craniovertebral instability**

【32】**A very careful and graduated examination sequence would be demanded by the presence of suspect symptoms or by recent trauma (less than 6weeks) to safeguard the patient from the possible adverse effects of the examination itself.**

【33】**The purpose of testing is**

【34】**1\. To reproduce signs and/or symptoms potentially attributable to vertebrobasilar insufficiency either by testing or from the patient’s history**

【35】**_2\._ To differentiate those signs and/or symptoms if they are noncardinal**

【36】**3.To determine the risk to the patient of treating his or her neck with any treatment that threatens the vertebral artery**

【37】**The main causes of signs and symptoms potentially sourced from the vertebrobasilar system are**

【38】**The tissues vascularized by the system itself**

【39】**The cervical nonvascular tissues (which we know from clinical and experimental evidence can cause many of these signs and symptoms84-88)**

【40】**The vestibular apparatus and neurological projections**

【41】**The testing sequence outlined in this chapter will gradually increase the stress on the vertebral artery so that the examination can be curtailed at the first sign of ischemia. It begins with the least stressful of tests， the history， and progresses gradually to the most stressful， the full occlusion position of extension and rotation. A number of clinicians have suggested that the full occlusion position and even extension be left untested as a safety con-sideration， especially because our treatment techniques should not be go-ing into that range. However， our responsibility to the patient goes a little further than our own clinic. We must ensure that the function of the pa-tient is safe. Combined rotation and extension is a functional movement. and if the patient is capable of going into that position， it must be tested.**

【42】**History If indirect open-ended questions do not elicit useful responses， direct questions must be asked about central nervous system symptoms. Has the patient had any dizziness? If so， what type? Was the onset of dizziness immediate or delayed? Is it still present? If so， is its onset/off-set related to head or body position and movements， medication， intake， and so forth? Are there any visual disturbances such as blurred vision or field defects， and are these related to head position and movements? Do you experience any paresthesia or anesthesia， and if so， where? Do you have ataxia， drop attacks， problems waking， clumsiness， tendencies to stumble or fall， or any other movement problems? Do you faint episod-ically or have problems concentrating or staying alert? Is there any am-nesia? If so， is it postconcussion or is it ongoing? The latter indicates something more than concussion， and the patient needs to get back to the physician. Has the patient noted recent deafness， speech defects， swallowing difficulties， or tinnitus?**

【43】**Observation The therapist should be making observations while tak-ing the patient’s history. For the central nervous system function part of the examination， look and listen for the following：**

【44】**Nystagmus**

【45】**Dysphasia**

【46】**Dysarthria**

【47】**Dysphagia**

【48】**Ataxia**

【49】**Unsteadiness**

【50】**Loss of concentration**

【51】**Sternomastoid/trapezius atrophy**

【52】**Horer's signs**

【53】人名段删除-1:<u>**a. Enophthalmos**</u>

【54】**b. Ptosis**

【55】人名段删除-1:<u>**C. Miosis**</u>

【56】**d. Anhydrosis**

【57】**e. Facial flushing**

【58】**Objective Tests Carotid Pulses The assessing of the carotid pulses is the first step in the assessment of the vertebral artery. Atherosclerosis， being a systemic condition， has the potential to affect all arteries， and there is a good chance that if the carotid arteries are occluded， the ver-tebrals will be， too. Absence or a severe reduction in the strength of the carotid pulse should require caution from the examining therapist. Vari-ous studies have determined that a decrease in flow through the verte-bral artery results in an increased flow through the common carotid， par-ticularly in the contralateral artery.89.90 Accordingly， the carotid pulse should be taken and the sides compared for gross differences. This should be done in the rotated， extended， and combined rotated and extended po-sitions， as well as in the neutral position. The therapist looks for an in-crease in the strength of the pulse over that found in the neutral position. A side to side difference in carotid pulse strength with a change in head position may indicate hypoplasia， aplasia， atresia， or occlusion. If a side to side difference is associated with a history of blatant neurological symptoms or if the pulse changes with a position change， the patient should be referred back to the physician. If the patient's complaints are of a vaguer nature and if the resting pulse is different from side to side， further testing can be carried out， but with caution.**

【59】**Neurological Examination The neurological examination can be car-ried out without stressing the spine or the arterial system. The cranial nerves and long tracts are examined and assessed as discussed ear-lier. Multisegmental hypotonia， hypertonia， and weakness can also be tested using palpation， passive movements of the limbs， and strength testing.**

**Early Vestibular Tests Parts of the vestibular system can be examined without stressing the cervical spine and its arteries. However， the need to protect the potentially damaged vertebral artery or severe musculoskele-tal damage limits just how much you can do. The Hallpike-Dix test，prob-ably the most stressful clinical test available for the vestibular apparatus， is contraindicated until the vertebral artery is excluded as a possible source of the patient’s symptoms. A modified test based on an observation made|删除0换行|by Cope and Ryan can be utilized. They observed that the wearing of a soft collar effectively eliminates the neck (joints or arteries) as a cause of dizziness or vertigo.’ A hard collar can be used， or the therapist can fix the patient’s head and neck and then rock the patient backward and for-ward， side to side， and in circles in ever larger amplitudes until symptoms or signs are reproduced or until maximum safe excursions have been reached. If symptoms are reproduced during this test， the neck has been eliminated as the source of symptoms， so it is unlikely that the vertebral artery or the cervical musculoskeletal structures are playing in a role in any dizziness that the patient may be experiencing.**

【61】**lf the test is positive for noncardinal symptoms， the cause is unlikely to be ccrvical in origin， because the position of the spine has remained con-stant during the test. The patient is asked about any symptoms that occur during the test， and the eyes are monitored for nystagrnus and pupil changes.**

【62】**The so-called vertebral artery tests obviously test many things other than the vertebral artery， but this is the main concemn. To try to clarify the thinking behind neurovascular or dizziness testing， the tests can be divided in two categories， tests that reproduce the patient’s symptoms and those that differentiate them.**

【63】**Reproduction Tests The purpose of this part of the examination is to see if the therapist can reproduce the dizziness by moving the head， body， and neck. The reproduction of cardinal symptoms requires an im-mediate referral to the physician because the reproduction of central neu-rological signs or symptoms with changes in head position must be con-sidered to be a result of neurovascular compromise until proven otherwise by exhaustive objective testing such as magnetic resonance angiography， Doppler ultrasonography， or angiograms. The reproduction of dizziness or any other noncardinal sign or symptom indicates the need for the therapist to carry out differentiation tests to try to determine the source. Dizziness in itself is not a contraindication to treatment and is frequently the indication to perform manual techniques if it is believed that the cervical spine is the source of the dizziness. From cadaveric ex-92.93periments，92.93 the fully stressed position for one vertebral artery is cer-vical extension， rotation， and traction. This is often called the vertebral artery stress test， but it must be understood that although this position is most likely to occlude the vertebral artery， it also puts other tissues under stress and is therefore not specific to the vertebral artery. The po-sition simply tests whether or not cervical movement causes dizziness， not what tissue causes it.**

【64】**At least 30 degrees of rotation is required for partial occlusion of the artery in cadavers， and in the living the critical angle for blood flow dis-turbance in the vertebral artery was less than 45 degrees， with at least another 10 to 15 degrees required before completc obstruction occurred in some subjects. It is therefore of little use to do these tests in patients who do not have the required amount of cervical motion.’**

【65】**Testing in patients who are experiencing noncardinal symptoms (re-member that the presence of cardinal symptoms contraindicates these tests) is carried out in stages. The cadaveric studies quoted earlier sug-gest that traction is occlusive but minimally so， extension is less occlu-sive than rotation， and rotation combined with extension is more occlu-sive than either alone. The addition of traction on the combined rotation and extension position is maximally occlusive， and 50% of body weight traction (which is not difficult to achieve in a 120-lb person) will oc-clude every artery tested. This last maneuver is unnecessary because it is not functional， will not be a treatment， and is potentially dangerous.**

【66】**The test position must be sustained for a set period or until signs or symptoms are provoked. The time each position is held for varies from one authority to another from 10 seconds to a minute. Grant and the Australian Physiotherapy Association’s protocol for premanipulative test-ing suggest 10 seconds as a compromise that takes into consideration clinical logistical requirements， patient safety， and physiological needs. There is some experimental evidence that changes in cvoked potentials in hearing occur within 15 seconds of vertebrobasilar occlusion.**

【67】**I suggest that certain cranial nerves be tested while holding the patient's position and that this testing be started at around the 10-second mark in the test. It will take about 5 or 6 seconds to run through the selected cranial nervc tests， taking the duration of the position to about 15 or 16 seconds.**

**The cranial nerves that lend themselves to being tested in these oc-clusive positions are|删除0换行|(Oculomotor， trochlear， and abducens (horizontal and vertical gaze and convergence)**

【69】**Edinger-Wesiphal (consensual light reflex)**

【70】**Vagal/accessory (phonation and uvular movement)**

【71】**Hypoglossal (tongue protrusion)**

【72】**It is especially important that the cranial nerves are re-tested if symp-toms such as dizziness are provoked while the patient is still experi-encing the evoked symptoms. Language， speech， and voice changes can be detected by having the patient act as the timer for each

【58】**Objective Tests Carotid Pulses The assessing of the carotid pulses is the first step in the assessment of the vertebral artery. Atherosclerosis， being a systemic condition， has the potential to affect all arteries， and there is a good chance that if the carotid arteries are occluded， the ver-tebrals will be， too.
