【1】**She saw her physician again on Thursday. He advised her to continue working， to increase her medication， and to work through the pain. By the middle of the following week， the symptoms had increased to the point where she simply could not continue to work. She returned to her physician， who took her off work and referred her to physical therapy.**

**On attendance， she stated that the neck pain was present mainly on movement and on prolonged flexion. The pain woke her occasionally while sleeping， although she could not say what provoked it-sleeping position or movement. The lateral upper arm pain was present to some|删除0换行|extent all of the time but was worse when the neck was worse. The paresthesia was intermittent， being felt whenever the neck was flexed or when washing her hair and more recently whenever she lifted her arm more than 90°from her side.**

【3】**She did not complain of dizziness or paresthesia anywhere other than in the left hand. She denied any history of cervical problems and had no medical history of relevance. X-rays were negative and her physi-cian did not feel that an MRl or CT scan was necessary.**

【4】**Objective Examination**

【5】**Cranial nerve， long tract， and fracture tests were negative. Progressive dizziness testing through Hautard’s test was negative. Craniovertebral ligament testing was negative.**

【6】**Flexion was about 50% of the expected range and reproduced neck and lateral upper arm pain and her paresthesia. Extension was about75% of the expected range and caused local posterolateral neck pain. Right-side flexion was full range but reproduced her paresthesia. Left-side flexion was about 50% of right-side flexion and produced postero-lateral neck pain and her paresthesia. Right rotation was full range and painfree. Left rotation was about 50% of right and produced postero-lateral neck pain， left lateral upper arm pain， and the paresthesia.**

【7】**Muscle testing found mild fatigable weakness of the lateral rotators of the left shoulder and moderate fatigable weakness of the left elbow flexors and wrist extensors. There was slight loss of pinprick sensation over the paresthetic area but no loss of light touch in this or any other area. Her reflexes were equal and normal on both sides. Moderate to strong compression of the cervical spine produced left neck pain. Trac-tion did not have any effect.**

【8】**Do you have a diagnosis， treatment plan， and prognosis for this lady?**

【9】**What are you thinking at this point? How will you proceed with the examination?**

【10】**Cervical Case 14 Continuation**

【11】**Diagnosis From the patient’s symptoms it seems likely that she has a disk hemniation compressing the sixth nerve root. The amount of com-pression seems moderate because the sensation loss and weakness are not profound and there is no change in the deep tendon reflexes. Possi-bly she damaged her disk in the accident and this caused some com-pression of the sixth nerve root. Continuing to work may have caused more hermiation and increased nerve compromise.**

【12】**Neither the subjective examination or the objective examination in-dicate any central neurological or neurovascular involvement.**

【13】**Traction did not make her symptoms worse (although it did not re-lieve them either)， so it is not contraindicated as a treatment. The lack of lancinating pain would suggest that the nerve root is not inflamed， so she should be able tolerate traction.**

【14】**As a point of interest， I did not use the upper limb neuromeningeal tension or provocation tests because there did not seem to be any point. The clinical signs were very clear—distinctly affected range of motion with some of the movements reproducing her paresthesia. The pares-thesia and hypoesthesia appear in a clearly delineated C6 zone， and her weakness is distributed in the C6 myotome.**

【15】**Treatment She should remain off work until the continuous pain sub-sides and changes to intermittent pain. A hard collar should be consid-ered for this patient because physiological movements are causing arm pain and paresthesia. Mechanical traction is also a possibility after a trial manual traction treatment or two to ensure that it will not exacerbate her condition.**

【16】**Prognosis Some factors suggest a good prognosis and some factors in-dicate a bad one. On the plus side， the pain was delayed and there was no immediate severe loss of motion. On the down side is the overriding presence of neurological symptoms. This presence is one of the worse prognostic factors in post-whiplash patients.**

【17】**The patient was treated with a hard collar， manual and then me-chanical traction， and painfrce exercises every day. She was also advised on sleeping positions--her pillows were reduced from two to one and in order to keep her off of her stomach， a golf ball was placed in her pajama pockct.**

【18】**This treatment scheme was continued， with modifications and addi-tions， for 3 weeks. The patient noted no improvement in the last two treatment sessions. The collar was removed at this point. The lateral arm pain was no longer present. The posterolateral neck pain was very lo-cal to left mid neck. The paresthesia was still present. but less notice able， and was felt on overhead arm movements away from the side such as hair washing.**

【19】**On examination， the range of motion had increased. Extension was limited to about 10% of the expected range and caused local soreness. Flexion was full range and painfree. Right-side flexion was slightly lim-ited， while all other movements were full range and painfree.**

【20】**The muscle weakness was observed only on testing the wrist exten-sors and was very mild starting at a grade 4+ and reducing to a grade3+ over six repetitions. Pinprick sensation was normal and the tendon reflexes remained normal.**

【21】**This lady had made substantial improvement but her pain had not leveled off. Where do you go from here? Does she need any other clin-ical examinations? Do you continue with her current treatment or change it? Does she go back to work?**

【22】**Please turn to page 406 for solutions.**

【23】**Subjective Examination**

【24】**A 53-year-old man complaining of right lateral elbow pain was referred by his physician with a diagnosis of tennis elbow. The pain had been present for 4 weeks and was felt during and after staining his sundeck. For the first few days， the pain was present all of the time but was worse whenever he used his hand. On attendance， the pain was felt only on use but it was disabling. He had not been able to work as a plumber since the injury.**

【25】**The patient had no history of elbow pain but said that he suffered the occasional neck ache for no apparent reason. This pain was felt in the posterior neck and was not referred to his arms. He had no medical his-tory of relevance.**

【26】**Objective Examination**

【27】**The elbow had full range and painfree movements. Isometric wrist ex-tension and radial deviation were painful at the lateral aspect of the el-bow. There was tenderness to palpation over the lateral epicondyle. The pain on isometric testing was less when the test was carried out with the patient wearing a tennis elbow support.**

【28】**Do you have a diagnosis and what are the potential causes?**

【29】**What are you thinking at this point? How will you proceed with the examination?**

【30】**Cervical Case 15 Continuation**

【31】**This man is suffering from an epicondylar tennis elbow as demonstrated by the isometric tests and the location of the tenderness. However， there are numerous causes of tennis elbow， including： cervical biomechanical dysfunction， direct trauma， wrist hypomobility， elbow hypomobility， and tre overuse.**

【32】**Repeating the isometric tests in various head and neck positions can quickly screen the neck. If the patient’s pain is significantly reduced， then the neck is playing a role. If the pain is completely relieved， there is no pathology at the elbow. However， only biomechanical testing can definitively exclude the neck clinically. A positive examination only demonstrates the presence of a biomechanical dysfunction. It is up to the therapist to judge the dysfunction’s association with the tennis el-bow. Cervical dysfunction may be contributing or causing this man’s el-bow problem.**

【33】**Direct trauma would be obvious in the patient’s history， which is not a factor in this case.**

【34】**If the wrist cannot exiend， then the wrist extensors may become over-active in an attempt to fully extend the wrist. Biomechanical testing will demonstrate the hypomobility.**

【35】**The common elbow dysfunction that underlies tennis elbow is the abducted ulna. Here the ulna is unable to fully flex or supinate and shifts the wrist into ulna deviation. This limits radial deviation and the radial deviators overwork trying to attain full range. In this case， the biome-chanical examination of the wrist did not show any dysfunction.**

【36】**True overuse is， in mny opinion， an unusual cause of tennis elbow. A history of significant overuse that is unfamiliar for that patient is nec-essary in order to make this diagnosis.**

【37】**In this case， the screening tests for the neck are negative. Biome-chanical testing of the neck found hypomobility at the atlantooccipital joints into extension bilaterally and hypomobility at the left C3/4 zy-gopophyseal joint.**

【38】**Diagnose and treat.**

【39】**Is Her Post-MVA Headache Arising From Her Neck?**

【40】**Subjective Examination**

【41】**A 34-year-old woman complaining of neck pain and headaches is re-ferred for treatment. She gave a history of being involved in a motor ve-hicle accident， when the car she was driving was struck from the rear2 weeks earlier. She experienced a mild posterior， right neck ache al-most immediately. By the next morning， the cervical pain was much worse and accompanied by a right occipitotemporal headache. The cer-vical pain and headache were initially present continuously and relieved only by analgesics. But over the last week， the headache became inter-mittent and was felt upon waking and at the end of the day. The cervi-cal pain was also present at the end of the work day， on various move-ments， and on prolonged flexion positions such as reading. She experienced no other pains or paresthesia.**

【42】**She did not hit her head during the accident， denies being knocked unconscious， and was able to remember everything about the accident. She had no medical history of relevance or any previous neck pain. She had not experienced any dizziness， nausea， or visual symptoms.**

【43】**In general she thought that her pain was improving. She was able to do more， especially over the previous few days. lnitially she took a cou-ple of days off work as a taxi dispatcher， but then returned to work. Al-though working aggravated her neck， the pain was less the last few days.**

【44】**From this information can you determine if the headache is referred from the cervical spine； if the prognosis is good， bad， or indifferent； or if the patient needs to wear a cervical collar?**

【45】**What are you thinking at this point? How will you proceed with the examination?**

【46】**Cervical Case 16 Continuation**

【47】**The headache is probably referred from the neck. The onset of the more severe cervical pain and the onset of the headache occurred simultane-ously. The distribution of her headache is typical of a cervicogenic headache because its onset and provocative factors coincide.**

【48】**Her prognosis is good. The onset of pain was delayed. There were no neurological signs or symptoms and she was making a steady re-covery. Additionally she was fully functional.**

【49】**This patient should not need to be put into a collar because she not only functioned without a collar but also improved without a collar.**

【50】**Objective Examination**

【51】**Extension was about 50% of the expected range and reproduced her right cervical pain. Flexion was almost full range and pulled on the pos-terior neck. Right rotation and right-side flexion were about 60% and30%， respectively， of the expected range with both reproducing her neck pain. Left-side flexion and left rotation were full range and painfree. None of the limited ranges produced spasm， but all had a harder than usual end feel， which in the case of right rotation felt pathomechanical.**

【52】**Compression and traction were painless. The craniovertebral stress tests were negative.**

【53】**All neurological tests including those for the cranial nerves and spinal nerve roots were negative. Biomechanical testing indicated a loss of ex-tension with a pathomechanical or subluxed end feel of the right C2/3zygopophyseal joint， which was also painful during the test. Although none of the tests reproduced her headache， she did complain of its on-set after the examination was finished.**

【54】**Do any of these objective findings alter the likelihood of the headache being referred from the neck， or her prognosis， or her need for a collar? What treatment would you initiate?**

【55】零碎段删除-1:<u>**1O**</u>

【56】**Subjective Examination**

【57】**A 56-year-old man is seen complaining of pain in the left upper trapezius with radiating pain into the lateral upper arm with paresthesia in the left medial upper arm and forearm and ulna border of the hand and the little finger. The upper arm pain had been present for 6 weeks， gradually in-creasing in severity over that time until it had become a constant ache. The paresthesia had been felt for the last week and was becoming more intense.**

【58】**He had been receiving treatment at another clinic with no improve-ment， and when the paresthesia started， he switched clinics. The treat-ment consisted of manual therapy and exercises， and when this failed to provide relief， mechanical traction was substituted.**

【59】**The patient could relate no apparent cause and had no history of cer-vical or arm pain. The patient had no medical history of relevance. He had quit smoking a year earlier but retained his smoker’s cough. He works as a millwright in a paper mill.**

【60】**Objective Examination**

【61】**Flexion was full range and painfree. Extension was full range and pro-duced mild pain in the upper left trapezius. Left-side flexion was full range and painfree. Right-side flexion was about 30% of that seen with left-side flexion and had a strong spasm end feel. Right-side flexion also reproduced the upper trapezius and lateral arm pain and the paresthesia in the ulna border of the lower arm and hand. Both rotations were full range and painfree. Isometric left-side flexion was painful but all other isometric tests were negative. Compression， traction， and posteroante-rior pressures were all negative. Severe pinprick sensation decreased over the ulna border of the hand and the entire fifth finger. There was weakness of finger flexion and finger abduction and adduction. No re-flex changes were noted. The upper limb tension test for the ulna and**
**median nerve components were both positive in that they reproduced the paresthesia as well as the lateral arm pain.**

【62】**Offer a diagnosis and treatment.**

【63】**What are you thinking at this point? How will you proceed with the examination?**

【64】**Cervical Case 17 Continuation**

【65】**The absence of a cause is a yellow flag and the condition is worsening as evidenced by the onset of paresthesia in the eighth cervical and first and second thoracic dermatomal areas. However， the pattemn of motion restriction is unusual in that flexion and extension and the rotations are largely unaffected. Because the posteroanterior pressures were painless(as were compression and traction)， the spinal segments are less likely to be involved. These findings (or their lack) would tend to exclude a disk herniation as a cause. The patient’s age would allow spinal steno-sis as a potential cause； however， the pain does not seem to be related to neck positions. The failure of mechanical treatment is another cause for concern.**

【66】**Weakness of the intrinsic hand muscles has been recognized as an uncommon result of disk herniation， but may be present in thoracic out-let syndrome and various other brachial plexus lesions， including Pan-coast syndrome. In general， this is not typical of the cervical problems normally seen by orthopedic therapists and requires great care on the part of the therapist. If this is Pancoast’s syndrome， what do you expect to find on further examination? What are the common causes?**

【67】**Please turn to page 408 for solutions.**

【68】零碎段删除-1:<u>**ASE**</u>

【69】**Subjective Examination**

【70】**A 45-year-old man complaining of paresthesia in the right hand is re-ferred by his family doctor with a diagnosis of carpal tunnel syndrome. The paresthesia was felt in the palmar aspect of the right hand covering the middle and index fingers and thumb. The symptoms had been pres-ent for a week and had no apparent cause.**

【71】**The patient had no history of wrist or neck pain. He is a controlled insulin-dependent diabetic but has no other medical history of relevance. He is a nonsmoker and works as a management consultant.**

【72】**Velocity conduction studies were negative.**

【73】**Objective Examination**

【74】**The wrist and fingers had full range painfree movements. Isometric tests were negative. Phalen’s and Tinnel's tests reproduced his symptoms as did sustained extension. Venous obstruction tests (circumferential pres-sure just above the wrist) were negative. Sensation over the hand was normal.**

【75】**The scanning examination of the neck was negative.**

【76】**Is the above information sufficient to make a diagnosis and initiate treatment?**

【77】**What are you thinking at this point? How will you proceed with the examination?**

【78】**Cervical Case 18 Continuation**

【79】**The differential diagnoses with these symptoms are thoracic outlet syn-drome， ulnar nerve entrapment at the elbow or wrist， cervical radicu-lopathy， and carpal tunnel syndrome. Cervical radiculopathies produce segmental symptoms. The closest distribution of paresthesia that would typically come from the neck would be due to pressure on the sixth nerve root. This could give paresthesia in the thumb， index finger， and the radial part of the middle finger but it is felt on the dorsal rather than the palmar aspect of the hand. Ulnar nerve entrapment would give pares-thesia along the ulna border of the hand and two fingers. Thoracic out-let syndrome tends to affect the entire hand and frequently has a vas-cular component. All in all， carpal tunnel syndrome does seem the likeliest diagnosis. The negative nerve conduction velocity studies do not exclude the diagnosis but may simply not be sufficiently sensitive.**

【80】**There is no obvious cause for the paresthesia， although the patient is an insulin-dependent diabetic and the paresthesia could bc an early man-ifestation of diabetic neuropathy. However， the absence of cause could possibly indicate a double crush syndrome， which could explain the negative nerve conduction studies. The upper limb neural tension tests can be useful in determining if a double crush syndrome cxists. In this case， the tests for the median nerve components reproduced the symp-toms when the neck was side flexed away from the symptomatic side.**

【81】**This finding required a biomechanical examination， which demon-strated hypomobility with a pathomechanical (jammed) end fecl of the right zygopophyseal joint of C5/6. A biomcchanical examination of the wrist and elbow failed to find any dysfunction.**

【82】**What are your thoughts on etiology and treatment?**

【83】**1\. A double crush syndrome occurs when neural tissue is compromised at two or more** **points， neither of which is sufficient alone to cause symptoms but， when taken together，** **become clinically significant because their combined contribution decreases axoplas-mic flow.**

【1】A few lines should be devoted to two interesting morphologic expres-sions of psoriasis， namely， the pustular and the erythrodermic. Pustular psoriasis is merely explosive psoriasis in which the process is so accelerated that it bypasses guttate macules and papules and proceeds directly to pus-tules. Erythrodermic psoriasis is universal， or nearly so， and exhibits gener-alized redness and scaling. The histopathologic findings are just like those of fully developed lesions of psoriasis， except that there is little， if any， scale as a consequence of exfoliation.

【19】\[TYRIASIS rosea and guttate parapsoriasis， at first glance， seem to have more histopathologic features in common than they have differences. Both have a superficial perivascular predominantly lym-phocytic infiltrate， spongiosis， and parakeratosis. They differ primarily in that pityriasis rosea has a somewhat denser infiltrate， extravasated erythro-cytes， more noticeable spongiosis， and cpidermal hyperplasia. Another dif-ference is a greater tendency toward formation of scale-crusts in guttate parapsoriasis， and those scale-crusts usually are very elongated. Last， some lesions of guttate parapsoriasis exhibit tiny clusters of lymphocytes within epidermal foci poor in spongiosis， and lymphocytes aligned as solitary units in foci in the basal layer. In some instances， however， it may be extremely diflicult to differentiate between the two diseases histopathologically.

【20】**Pityriasis rosea tends to involve the torso from the neck to the knees and to consist of oval to round， salmon-pink papules and plaques with delicate scales that form collarettes. On the trunk， the lesions align themselves along lines of cleavage of the skin (Langer’s lines). Days or a week or two before the appearance of the eruption， a larger scaly lesion (“mother”or “herald”patch) had become manifest. Biopsy of this larger lesion reveals histopatho-logic changes similar to those in the later smaller lesions of pityriasis rosea， but the perivascular infiltrate of lymphocytes often is both superficial and deep， there is less spongiosis， and epidermal hyperplasia is more psoriasi-form. Pityriasis rosea usually resolves without treatment in about six to nine weeks.**

【21】**Clinically， guttateparapsoriasis consists of widespread， drop-sized pink or tan papules covered by fine， wafer-like scales. The lesions are not pruritic， but they persist indefinitely and are refractory to treatment. Histo-pathologically， guttate parapsoriasis shows little or no spongiosis within the epidermis in a routine section. The finding of plasma in scale-crusts， however， implies that spongiosis must have been present in the epidermis previously.**

【22】We consider digitate dermatosis to be a variant of guttate parapsoriasis. Clinically， it consists of large， ovoid， scaly patches situated mostly on or near the trunk that persist despite treatments of various kinds， and histopatho-logically， it is indistinguishable from guttate parapsoriasis. Lesions of gut-tate parapsoriasis and digitate dermatosis may be present together in the same patient. Even more important is the observation that some patients with typical patches and plaques of mycosis fungoides， confirmed histo-pathologically， also may have typical lesions of guttate parapsoriasis and digitate dermatosis， the latter pattern verified histopathologically， too.

【23】Careful study of lesions of guttate parapsoriasis-digitate dermatosis reveals subtle signs of mycosis fungoides in many lesions， namely， lymphocytes aligned as solitary units in the basal layer focally， one or two tiny clusters of lymphocytes within the spinous zone in the presence of but a tad of spongio-sis， a few lymphocytes within the epidermis larger than those in the dermis， and one or two foci of wiry bundles of collagen arranged haphazardly in the papillary dermis where they are accompanied by lymphocytes， sometimes in patchy array. In sum， we now conclude that guttate parapsoriasis-digitate dermatosis (smallplaqueparapsoriasis)， likeparapsoriasis en plaque， parapsoriasis variegata， xanthoerythroderma perstans， and poikilo-derma vasculare atrophicans (large plaque parapsoriasis)， is a distinctive morphologic macular/patch expression of mycosis fungoides.

【24】Superficial types of figurate erythemas (e.g.， erythema annulare cen-trifugum) also must be considered in the histopathologic differential diag-nosis of pityriasis rosea. Both diseases are characterized by a superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate， edema of the papillary dermis， spongio sis， and focal parakeratosis. Although histopathologically it is impossible to distinguish between pityriasis rosea and superficial figurate erythemas， those two conditions are differentiated readily from guttate parapsoriasis， clinically and histopathologically. Lesions of pityriasis rosea and erythema annulare centrifugum both are characterized clinically by oval shapes and collarettes of scales at their peripheries. Clinically， a lesion of erythema annulare centrifigum seems to be a caricature of a lesion of pityriasis rosea. The rare vesicular variant of pityriasis rosea， which occurs mostly in blacks， must be differentiated histopathologically from fully developed lesions of allergic contact dermatitis， nummular dermatitis， and“id”reactions. A\]-though this differentiation is not always possible， vesicular lesions of pityri-asis rosea tend to have less epidermal hyperplasia and fewer eosinophils than those three diseases that tend to eventuate in vesicles.

【44】**ICHENplanus-like keratosis may be confused easily with lichen planus histopathologically， especially in specimens taken by punch technique. Ostensibly， both are superficial perivascular dermatiti-des with lichenoid， mostly lymphocytic infiltrates that obscure the dermo-epidermal junction where there are vacuolar alteration and necrotic kerati-nocytes (interface dermatitides， lichenoid type). Lichen planus-like keratosis begins as a solar lentigo or reticulated seborrheic keratosis that， in time， is associated with a dense lichenoid infiltrate composed mostly of lympho-cytes. The keratosis usually is removed by shave excision technique， and the lesion gencrally extends broadly from one end of the histopathologic section to the other， or nearly so. In contrast， lichen planus is idiopathic. A lesion of it usually is biopsied by punch excision technique and， more often than not， the lesion does not extend across the width of even a 4-mm specimen.**

【45】**Clinically， a lichen planus-like keratosis usually develops as a solitary， reddish-brown， scaly lesion， predilectively on sun-exposed skin， especially of the chest and arms of older persons. The lesion often is misdiagnosed clini-cally as basal-cell carcinoma. In time， lichen planus-like keratosis tends to regress with residual changes that may be indistinguishable from thosc in regression of primary cutaneous malignant melanoma. Those findings are a thinned epidermis and a papillary dermis "thickened" by delicate fibropla-thinned epidermis and a papillary sia， melanophages， a sprinkling of lymphocytes， necrotic keratinocytes， and telangiectases. In fact， the papillary dermis in resolved lesions of lichen planus-like keratosis (and primary melanoma) and in atrophie lesions of lichen planus is reduced in volume because of the loss of dermal papillae that ordinarily account for much of the volume of the skin above the reticu-lar dermis.**

【120】**N their fully developed form， allergic contact der-matitis and irritant contact dermatitis are both intra-epidermal vesicular dermatitides that appear after exposure to different kinds of contactants， namely， allergens in the former and irritant substances in the latter.**

【121】Histopathologically， allergic and irritant contact dermatitides have in common intra- and intercellular edema， edema of the papillary dermis， and superficial perivascular mixed inflammatory-cell infiltrates. Both also may be associated with subepidermal vesiculation. In allergic contact dermatitis， that occurrence is secondary to either bursting of intra-epidermal spongiotic vesicles or extensive edema of the papillary dermis. In irritant contact der-matitis， that phenomenon comes about as a consequence of rupture of intra-epidermal ballooning vesicles or of sevveereepidermalnecrosis with subsequent dermo-epidermal separation.

【122】Allergic contact dermatitis results from exposure of previously sensi-tized persons to contact allergens. It is a delayed type of hypersensitivity reaction， in contrast to irritant contact dermatitis， which is not a hypersen-sitivity reaction at all. Irritant contact dermatitis results from direct injury to the skin by a variety of agents such as strong acids and alkalis， and by less irritating substances such as croton oil and sodium lauryl sulfate.

【123】Clinically， allergic contact dermatitis appears as edematous pink pap-ules that soon become papulovesicles. That these are actually vesicles often can be appreciated better by gentle palpation than by observation. With progression， the vesicles become discernible clearly and， in severe cases， huge bullae may form. Biopsy specimens taken serially reveal the early stage of allergic contact dermatitis to consist of spongiosis that becomes decidedly focal (spongiotic dermatitis)， a fully developed stage that shows epidermal hyperplasia in addition to spongiotic vesicles (spongiotic psoriasiform der-matitis)， and a late stage in which there is psoriasiform hyperplasia (psori-asiform dermatitis) devoid of spongiosis. In long-enduringlesions of allergic contact dermatitis， there usually are histopathologic evidences of persistent rubbing (i.e.， lichen simplex chronicus) in the form of a papillary dermis thickened by coarse bundles of collagen arranged in vertical streaks and of compact orthokeratosis.

The histopathologic differential diagnosis of allergic contact dermatitis at all stages of the process involves consideration ofearly nummular derma-titis， dyshidrotic dermatitis， “id”reactions， and vesicular dermatophytic in-fections， all of which may show the same histopathologic features in sec-tions stained by hematoxylin and eosin. The presence of hyphae within the cornified layer establishes the diagnosis of dermatophytosis. The other four|删除0换行|conditions cannot be differentiated histopathologically from one another. Some patients may present themselves with widespread papulovesicular， vesicular， and even bullous eruptions that on the hands and feet may be interpreted as dyshidrotic dermatitis and “id”reactions， on other arcas of the integument as allergic contact dermatitis， and on other sites as nummu-lar dermatitis. Given this circumstance clinically and the identity of these four conditions histopathologically， these four spongiotic dermatitides seem to be related to one another.

【125】Photo-allergic contact dermatitis， such as to salicylanilides， and photo-allergic dermatitis， such as to systemically administered chlorpromazine， are similar histopathologically to allergic contact dermatitis， except that in the photodermatitides the infiltrate of inflammatory cells tends to be both deep as well as superficial， and the epidermis tends to harbor a few necrotic keratinocytes. Clinically， photo-allergic contact dermatitis and photo-aller-gic dermatitis usually are confined to regions of the skin that ordinarily are exposed to sunlight.

【126】Irritant contact dermatitis may range clinically from slight erythema and scaling to severe blisters and ulcerations. Like allergic contact dermati-tis， irritant contact dermatitis has a photo-related counterpart， namely， __ phototoxic contact dermatitis caused by substances that become irritants only afler photo-activation. Phototoxic dermatitis may result from systemi-cally administered chemicals such as psoralens， and phototoxic contact der-matitis may result from chemicals such as psoralens applied topically. The phototoxic lesions are similar to irritant contact dermatitis clinically and histopathologically， and they， too， occur only on areas exposed to ultraviolet light.

【41】**_The genetics of hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer_**

The genetic defect in HNPCC is a mutation occurring in one of several different DNA mismatch repair genes. DNA mismatch repair genes are responsible under normal conditions for repairing errors that occur in DNA that has been freshly copied. The polyps and cancers in HNPCC patients show evidence of genomic instability|删除0换行|for short repeated sequences， a phenomenon called microsatellite instability. Germline mutations at four different gene loci have been described： MSH2， MLH1， PMS1 and PMS2. Of these， the first two are the most common and make up two-thirds or more of patients with HNPCC.

【56】**Vascular lesions**

【57】**The commonest of these are angiodysplasia or vascular ectasia. These lesions are most likely to be changes secondary to the degeneration of the venules in the wall of the gut that accompanies the process of aging.**

【58】Arterioles that supply the mucosa terminate in submu-cosal capillaries. These capillaries in turn form venules， which penetrate the circular muscle of the gut wall. The pressure resulting from the contraction and relaxation of the circular muscle of the gut in the course of normal peristalsis causes these ectatic venules to bulge and over time to become tortuous. This pressure is presumably transmitted to the capillaries， which dilate， giving rise to the characteristic mucosal tufts seen on angiography. Ultimately， the increased pressure results in the malfunc-tioning of the precapillary sphincters. At this stage in its natural history the vascular lesion behaves hemodynami-cally like an arteriovenous malformation.

【59】Vascular ectasia or angiodysplasia is most commonly seen in the right side of the colon， but may occur else-where in the colon and in the stomach and small intes-tine. On occasion they may be the source of profuse acute hemorrhage， but more often they give rise to occult blood loss presenting as iron deficiency anemia. Gastric angiodysplasia， in particular， is more com-monly encountered in patients with chronic renal fail-ure often on hemodialysis， although such patients may have angiodysplasia in other areas of the gastrointesti-nal tract as well. There has also been an association of angiodysplasia with von Willebrand's disease. The diagnosis is usually made on endoscopy (EGD or colonoscopy) when the characteristic red lesions with a‘fern leaf’ or a ‘red ball of yarn' appearance are encoun-tered. At times only cherry red spots may be noted and then the diagnosis may not be as definitive. Lesions are often missed on endoscopy. Documented chronic occult gastrointestinal blood loss， especially in an elderly patient or in a person on hemodialysis without a cause， even after EGD and colonoscopy， usually means that angiodysplasia has as yet not been identi-fied. 【40】Families in which only colon cancer is inherited are termed to be suffering from Lynch I syndrome. Families in which other cancers are also inherited， such as endometrial， ovarian， duodenal， biliary and pancre-atic cancers， are said to have the Lynch II syndrome.

【41】**_The genetics of hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer_**

The genetic defect in HNPCC is a mutation occurring in one of several different DNA mismatch repair genes. DNA mismatch repair genes are responsible under normal conditions for repairing errors that occur in DNA that has been freshly copied. The polyps and cancers in HNPCC patients show evidence of genomic instability|删除0换行|for short repeated sequences， a phenomenon called microsatellite instability. 【1】**macule refers to a small， flat， non-palpable spot on the skin， up to 1 cm in size， of different color than that of the surrounding normal skin. A flat lesion larger than a macule is known as a patch.**

【2】**malformation denotes a structural abnormality present at birth that re-sulted from an aberration in the embryologic anlage，e.g.， an arteriove-nous shunt or a cleft lip. Although the term“malformation”is used conventionally as a synonym for nevus and hamartoma， it is not a hamartoma (and nevus is merely a synonym for hamartoma). A ham-artoma is a potpourri of tissue elements that are present normally at a particular site， e.g.， trichofolliculoma and nevus sebaceus， whereas a malformation， as its name denotes， represents a fundamental error in embryologic development， e.g.， nevus comedonicus.**

【3】**malignant is a word that describes the behavior of a neoplasm， namely， one that， in the skin， has the potential to kill by destruction locally or by metastases widely. It should not be used synonymously with striking nuclear atypia because there is no necessary correlation between nu-clear atypia and biologic behavior， witness the inflammatory condition， dermatofibroma with “monster" cells， and the neoplastic condition， Spitz's nevus.**

【4】**mantle refers to the cloak-like appearance of cords of epithelial cells， as visualized in two-dimensional sections cut conventionally from speci-mens in preparation for viewing by conventional microscopy， that seem to emanate from both sides of hair follicles at the junction of infundib-ulum and isthmus and that hang like sleeveless outer garments along the sides of an inferior segment of a follicle for a short distance. In actuality， mantles are like skirts， not cloaks， because， when viewed in three dimensions， they encircle follicles. They are affiliated with both vellus and terminal follicles， but are much more striking in association with vellus ones. They give rise to sebaceous units， i.c.， glands and ducts. At first， mantles are comprised of cords of wholly undifferenti-ated epithelial cells that， in time， exhibit a few vacuoles within the cytoplasm of one or two cells， then more vacuoles in more cells， then vacuolated cells whose nuclei are scalloped just like those of mature sebocytes， and then what seems to be efflorescence， initially as blos-soms of sebocytes and eventually as blooming forth of a bounty of flowers in the form of fully formed sebaceous lobules and ducts. Be-cause mantles at all stages of evolution and devolution sometimes are apparent in sections from a single biopsy specimen， mantles seem to have a cycle analogous to， but not directly related with， the cycle of**
**follicles. Fibrofolliculoma is a benign proliferation with differentiation toward mantles.**

【5】**matrical cells of a follicle are situated near the base of a bulb. These cells differentiate into six types of specific epithelium： three components of inner sheath (Henle， Huxley， and cuticle) and three components of hair(cuticle， cortex， and medulla). Matrical cells are different from germi-native cells， the latter emerging from embryonic surface ectoderm to give rise to an entire follicle and the former being situated in follicular bulbs， where they differentiate and mature to form the inner sheath and the hair itself. Matrical cells differ from germinative cells cytologi-cally by being larger (bigger nuclei and more cytoplasm)， having paler nuclei， sporting a prominent nucleolus， and being in mitosis fre-quently.**

【6】melanophage refers to a macrophage that has ingested melanin. The mela-nin is aggregated in irregular clumps in the cytoplasm of the phago-cyte， i.e.， the melanin is coarse， rather than fine or “dusty."

【7】mesenchyme designates embryonic connective tissue derived from meso-derm， which is the source of all types of adult connective tissue. Mesen-chyme is loose tissue that acts as “packing”between developing paren-chymal structures. Mesenchymal cells have multiple potentialities， e.g.， they may differentiate along several lines to become various kinds of connective tissue cells such as fibrocytes， adipocytes， and chondrocytes. Some multipotential mesenchymal cells persist in adults and then， as a consequence of certain stimuli， differentiate into other types of cells.

【8】**metastasis indicates the spread by blood or lymph vessels and， less com-monly， along serosal surfaces of neoplastic cells from a primary neo-plasm to other sites where it tends to be the cause of death.**

【9】For prognostic and therapeutic purposes in the case of melano-mas， distinctions are made among satellite metastases， in transit me-tastases， regional metastases， and distant metastases.Satellite metasta-ses lie in proximity (about 3.0 to 5.0 centimeters) to a primary melanoma but not in direct continuity with it. In-transit metastases are situated more than 5.0 cm from the primary site but proximal to re-gional lymph nodes； regional metastases are in regional lymph nodes， and distant metastases are beyond regional nodes. In terms of progno-sis， however， a metastasis is a metastasis irrespective of the word or words used to modify it， and it signifies a grim prognosis because once metastasis occurs， neoplastic cells are carried far and wide.

【10】**_mixed infiltrate of inflammatory cells refers to one in which two or more_ types of inflammatory cells are apparent，e.g.，lymphocytes and eosino-phils in a response to an arthropod assault， or neutrophils，eosinophils， and lymphocytes in urticaria. In contrast are infiltrates in which a single type of inflammatory cell monopolizes， e.g.， lymphocytes in the deep manifestation of figurate erythema， histiocytes in some lesions of sarcoidosis， and mast cells in urticaria pigmentosa.**

**muroid refers to simulation of mucin as assessed clinically and histopatho-logically. Grossly， mucin is clear and viscid； histopathologically， it is|删除0换行|granular， stringy， and feathery basophilic material. In actuality， the term “myxoid”is deficient. A substance either is or is not mucin； if it is， it should be called that， and if it is not， it should be named precisely.

【12】necrobiosis is applied to connective tissue alterations in certain palisaded granulomatous inflammations of skin， such as granuloma annulare， necrobiosis lipoidica， necrobiotic xanthogranuloma， and rheumatoid nodule. The“necrobiotic”alteration， however， is mostly mucin in gran-uloma annulare， degeneration of collagen in necrobiosis lipoidica and necrobiotic xanthogranuloma， and fibrin in rheumatoid nodules. Be-cause of the imprecision histopathologically and the confusion etymo-logically， the term necrobiosis should not be used except to refer specif-ically to the disease necrobiosis lipoidica.

【13】necrosis means death of living cells as evidenced histopathologically by three critical nuclear changes， namely， pyknosis (darkened shrunken nuclei)， karyorrhexis (fragmented nuclei)， and karyolysis (faded ghosts of nu-clei). Because necrosis pertains to living cells only， it cannot be applied to collagen or elastic tissue. Alterations of those tissues are referred to as degeneration. Among causes of necrosis in skin and other organs， the most common are insufficient supply of oxygen-containing blood (e.g.， infarction)， trauma {e.g.， phototoxicity)， and infection (e.g.， by Clos-tridium welchii in gas gangrene). Several different forms of necrosis can be distinguished， namely， caseous， colliquative， mixed， septic， aseptic， and others.

【14】**neoplasm refers to a proliferation of cells whose growth both exceeds and is uncoordinated with that of normal tissues. Implicit in the concept of neoplasia， in contrast to hyperplasia， is that it persists in the same excessive manner after the stimulus that evoked the change has ceased. A neoplasm， e.g.， a seborrheic keratosis， differs from a hyperplasia， e.g.， a verruca vulgaris， because a hyperplasia regresses after the stimu-lus that evoked it， papillomavirus in this example， has been withdrawn. Neoplasms may be benign， i.e.， they neither kill by local destruction nor by metastasis (e.g.， a melanocytic nevus) or malignant， i.e.， they have the capability to kill by destruction locally or by metastases widely(e.g.， a melanoma).**

【15】Each of the definitions of “neoplasm，"“hyperplasia，”“benign，”and "malignant”set forth in this glossary is flawed partially， as is true for all definitions that attempt to capture morphologic manifestations of biologic phenomena. In most instances， the stimulus responsible for a proliferation of cells in a neoplasm is not known. Nearly all keratoac-anthomas regress without any treatment， yet that proliferation is con-sidered to be a neoplasm， not a hyperplasia. Furthermore， classical definitions of benign and malignant do not yet permit categorization， with conviction， of diseases like Kaposi's sarcoma， lymphomatoid pap-ulosis， and some fibromatoses such as desmoid tumors.

【16】**nevus is a synonym for hamartoma . Nevus cells are melanocytes and therefore are the cells of only one type of true nevus， i.e.， hamartomas known as congenital melanocytic nevi. Paradoxically， acquired melanocytic nevi are benign neoplasms.**

【17】**nodule designates， clinically， a dome-shaped solid lesion formed by cells， deposits， or elements of connective tissue and， histopathologically， dense， discrete collections of inflammatory or neoplastic cells， deposits， or elements of connective tissue in the skin. Clinical nodules evolve， for example， from macules and papules of melanoma， Kaposi’s sarcoma， and mycosis fungoides and may eventuate in tumors that may ulcerate. Examples of histopathologic nodules are sarcoidal and tuberculoid granulomas， lymphoid follicles in pseudolymphomas， and some me-lastases to skin.**

【18】**orthokeratosis designates hyperkeratosis in which nuclei are not retained in cornified cells. In the cornified layer of the epidermis and in infundib-ula， orthokeratosis may be subclassified as compact， laminated， or basket-weave in appearance. Theoretically， a more precise term is “or-thohyperkeratosis” because the number of cornified cells is increased. The latter designation， however， is clumsy and therefore orthokeratosis is preferred.**

【19】**Paget cell refers to a cell that is found in mammary and extramammary Paget’s disease and is characterized by a large， round， or plump oval nucleus and abundant pale-staining cytoplasm. The cytoplasm of Paget cells in extramammary Paget’s disease differs from that of cells of mammary Paget's disease because it contains abundant acid mucopoly-saccharides demonstrable by staining with hematoxylin and eosin and better yet with stains specific for them. In short， the Paget cells of mammary and extramammary Paget’s disease have several features in common， but they are very different from one another， just as are mammary and extramammary Paget’s disease. Despite the name“Pag-et’s disease” in common， the diseases are different.**

【20】**pagetoid cell describes a cell thought to resemble those of mammary and extramammary Paget’s disease by having a large roundish nucleus and abundant pale-staining cytoplasm， as occur， for example， in malignant melanoma and Bowen’s disease. Pagetoid cells are not found in pagetoid reticulosis (Woringer-Kolopp disease) because in that condi-tion the atypical lymphocytes scattered throughout the epidermis have no discernible cytoplasm， but clefts separate them from keratinocytes. Pagctoid cell refers to cytologic features of an epithelial cell like that of Paget’s disease， whereas pagetoid pattern denotes widespread distribu-tion of atypical cells， epithelial or non-epithelial， within an epidermal or adnexal epithelium as oceurs in those Paget diseases. In fact， not only are pagetoid cells different from one another， e.g.： melanocytes and keratinocyles may be pagetoid， but Paget cells themselves are dif-ferent， too. Those of mammary Paget’s disease are adenocarcinoma-tous (apocrine) ones that originate in lactifcrous ducts， whereas those of extramammary Paget’s disease are adenocarcinomatous (apocrine) ones that arise within the epidermis. The two types of cells have differ-ent morphologic features， e.g.， those of extramammary Paget’s disease have more abundant cytoplasm， replete with acid mucosubstances， that compresses the nucleus against the side of the cell and thereby causes it to resemble a signet ring.**

【21】pagetoid pattern indicates scatter of atypical cells throughout the epidermis(and adnexal epithelium) like that seen in mammary and extramam-mary Paget’s disease as is the case often in Spitz's nevi， melanomas， Bowen’s discase， mycosis fungoides， and histiocytosis-X.

【22】palisade describes the appearance of cells aligned in the fashion of stakes like those that form a defense barrier in a fortification， e.g.， columnar epithelial cells at the periphery of an outer sheath of a hair follicle， or on the basal layer of Bowen’s disease， histiocytes around mucin and degenerated collagen in granuloma annulare and around fibrin in rheumatoid nodule， and nuclei of Schwann cells directly apposed to one another at the distal ends of their respective cytoplasm in Verocay bodies of schwannomas.

【23】papillated refers to a shape like that of a nipple， e.g.， nipple-like projections above the skin surface as may be seen in proliferations of keratinocytes in condylomata acuminata and in the extension outward of papillary dermis in acanthosis nigricans.

【24】papillomatosis describes accentuation of the dermal papillae so that they project slightly or markedly above the skin surface as in acanthosis nigricans and some connective tissue nevi. The epidermis overlying the elongated papillae may or may not be thickened.

【25】papule denotes a small (less than 1 cm)， solid or cystic， slightly raised lesion. A papule may be mostly epidermal， c.g.， a plane wart， mostly dermal， e.g.， a lesion of lichen nitidus， or both epidermal and dermal， e.g.， a lesion of lichen planus.

【26】parakerutosis refers to retention of nuclei in cornified cells. This is usually the result of accelerated epidermopoiesis (e.g.， in psoriasis and sebor-rheic dermatitis) or of faulty maturation {e.g.， in solar keratoses and Bowen’s discase). Within the cornified layer of the epidermis， parakera-tosis may occur in mounds， e.g.， guttate psoriasis， in sharp alternation with orthokeratosis， e.g.pityriasis rubra pilaris， in broad zones of con-fluence， e.g. plaques of fully developed psoriasis， and in association with plasma in mounds， e.g.， seborrheic dermatitis.

【27】patch refers to a broad (more than 1 cm) flat lesion， whereas a macule denotes a small (less than 1 cm) flat lesion. A patch may begin as a macule， e.g.， vitiligo， or it may be a patch from the outset， c.g.， nevus spilus (congenital speckled lentiginous nevus).

【28】plaque refers to an elevated， broad (more than 1 cm) lesion often， but not always， formed by coalescence of papules. A plaque of psoriasis may eventuate from extension centrifugally of a papule of psoriasis， or it may develop as a consequence of confluence of several papules. A plaque of congenital melanocytic nevus is a plaque de novo.

【29】pleomorphism indicates variation in sizes and shapes of cellular structures， e.g.， nuclei in an infiltrate， usually of a neoplastic process. Pleomor-phism should not be confused with polymorphism， which refers to different types ofcells being present together in a single infiltrate.

【30】**pop out is a colorful description of the way some benign neoplasms and cysts shoot from the skin immediately after an incision has been made above them and very near to them. The reason for the ease of separa-tion from surrounding tissue is that benign neoplasms and cysts com-press adjacent fibrous tissue and， in the process， a space forms between those abnormal structures and nearly normal skin. The space and the tract of the blade of a scalpel is the route by which the neoplasm or cyst becomes ejected from its abode. It is through such a space that a sur-geon cradles some benign neoplasms and cysts and thereby enables them to “shell out.”**

【31】purpura refers to the purple color caused by visible hemorrhage in skin.

【32】**pustule denotes， clinically， an elevated， circumscribed collection of pus(neutrophils and necrotic debris) and， histopathologically， a collection of neutrophils within an epidermis， infundibulum， and， much less fre-quently， an eccrine duct. A variety of names， some eponymic， have been given to types of pustules in cutaneous epithelium. Discrete ab-scesses in the mid-spinous zone of psoriasis are termed “Munro's mi-croabscesses，”sponge-like abscesses in the upper reaches of the epider-mis of psoriasis and its analogues are known as “spongiform pustules of Kogoj，"and abscesses situated beneath the cornified layer of the epidermis are referred to as “subcorneal pustules."None of these types of pustules is specific for any one disease. So-called Munro’s microab-scesses may be seen in some dermatophytic infections， spongiform pus-tules in halogenodermas， and subcorneal pustules in such disparate conditions as psoriasis and pyoderma gangrenosum. The various histo-pathologic appearances of pustules merely reflect the moment at which biopsy has interrupted migration of neutrophils in their ascent from capillaries in derma papillae to cornified layer.**

【33】**Most pustules in skin are follicular rather than epidermal， and most of those are idiopathic. Many of the remainder are infectious，e.g.， bacterial (staphylococci)， fungal (dermatophytes)， viral (herpes)， and spirochetal (treponema pallidum).**

【34】**racemiform means “like a bunch of grapes” and describes the appearance of arrangement of germinative cells in one expression of trichoblastoma.**

【35】**reticular alteration describes the net-like pattern of an epidermis that re-sults from severe ballooning of keratinocytes and their subsequent rup-ture. The changes are common in viral vesicular diseases such as herpes simplex， zoster-varicella， milker's nodules， orf， and hand， foot， and mouth disease， but also in erythema multiforme， fixed drug eruptions， and pityriasis lichenoides et varioliformis acuta.**

【36】**retiform means net-like and refers to clinical and histopathologic features of a variety of diseases. For example， the root of the word is found in clinical descriptions such as livedo reticularis (cutis marmorata) and retiform parapsoriasis (parapsoriasis variegata) and histopathologic descriptions like reticular alteration (reticular degeneration) and reti-form pattern of trichoblastoma _L_ . _e_**

【37】scar is a type of fibrosis and represents the end stage of an inflammatory process that began with destruction of pre-existing tissue and evolved through granulation tissue. Histopathologically， a scar consists of col-lagen bundles that are oriented mostly parallel to the skin surface and an increased number of fibrocytes and dilated blood vessels that are arranged mostly perpendicular to the skin surface. In contrast， a keloid is a type of fibrosis that has thickened， homogencous， brightly eosino-philic， collagen bundles in random distribution and associated with an increased number of fibrocytes. A dermatofibroma is a type of fibrosis in which there are altered collagen bundles and fibrocytes in haphaz-ard array， siderophages and lipophages often， thick collagen bundles at the periphery of the lesion， and epidermal hyperplasia and hyperpig-mentation. The normal skin markings are usually effaced when these three forms of fibrosing inflammations， i.c.， scars， keloids， and der-matofibromas， involve the papillary dermis.

【38】sclerosis is a type of fibrosis characterized by near-obliteration of boundaries between bundles of collagen and by decreased numbers of fibrocytes. It is usually a sign of long-standing fibroplasia because of the marked alteration of bundles of collagen and the striking diminution in number of fibrocytes. Sclerosis is seen， for example， in the thickened papillary dermis of lichen sclerosis et atrophicus and throughout the papillary and reticular dermis of chronic radiodermatitis. 【6】Referral： A 30-year-old dentist was referred to physical therapy by an orthopedic surgeon for ischial bursitis， sometimes referred to as "Weaver’s bottom." 【7】Background： Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed local inflammation on the ischial tuberosity to confirm the medical diagnosis. He was given a steroid injection and was placed on an antiinflammatory (Celebrex) before he went to physical therapy.

【8】The client reported a mild loss of hip motion， especially of hip flexion， but no other symptoms of any kind. The pain did not radiate down the leg. The client described himself as being “in good shape"and working out at the local gym four to five times per week.

【9】Intervention/Follow-Up： Physicaltherapyintervention included deep friction massage， iontophoresis， and stretch-ing. 【10】The client went back to the orthopedic surgeon for a follow-up visit. A second MRl was done with a diagnosis of “benign inflam-matory mass."He was given a second steroid injection and was sent back to physical therapy. He was seen at a different clinic location by a second physical therapist.

【11】The physical therapist palpated a lump over the ischial tuber-osity， described as“swelling； this was the only new physical find-ing since his previous visits with the first physical therapist.

【12】Treatment concentrated deep friction massage in that area. The therapist thought the lump was getting better， but it did not resolve. The client reported increased painful symptoms， includ-ing pain at work and at night. No position was comfortable； even lying down without pressure on the buttocks was painful. 【30】Ureteral pain usually begins posteriorly in the costoverte-bral angle but may radiate anteriorly to the upper thigh and groin ， or it may be felt just in the groin and genital area. These pain patterns represent the path-way that genitals take as they migrate during fetal devel-opment from their original position， where the kidneys are located in the adult， down the pathways of the ure-ters to their final location. Pain is referred to a site where the organ was located during fetal development. A kid-ney stone down the pathway of the ureters causes pain in the flank that radiates to the scrotum (male) or labia(female).

【31】The lower thoracic and upper lumbar vertebrae and the SI joint can refer pain to the groin and anterior thigh in the same pain pattern as occurs with renal disease. Irritation of the T10-L1 sensory nerve roots (genitofemoral and ilioingui-nal nerves) from any cause， especially from diskogenic dis-ease， may cause labial (women)， testicular (men)， or buttock pain.109 The therapist can evaluate these conditions by con-ducting a neurologic screening examination and using the screening model.

【32】Referred symptoms from ureteral colic can be distin-guished from musculoskeletal hip pain by the history， the presence of urologic symptoms， and the pattern of pain. 【33】Active TrPs along the upper rim of the pubis and the lateral half of the inguinal ligament may lie in the lower internal oblique muscle and possibly in the lower rectus abdominis. 【38】**Clinical Presentation**

【39】The clinical presentation can be deceptive in young people. The fever is not dramatic and may come and go. Loss of appetite associated with systemic disease is often welcomed by teenagers and young adults and is not recognized as a sign of physiologic distress.

【40】With an infectious or inflammatory process， laboratory tests may reveal an elevated ESR. Questions about the presence of any other symptoms may reveal constitutional symptoms such as elevated nocturnal temperature， sweats， and chills， suggestive of an inflammatory process (Case Example 16.13).

【41】**Psoas Abscess**

【42】Any infectious or inflammatory process affecting the abdom-inal or pelvic region can lead to psoas abscess and irritation of the psoas muscle. For example， lesions outside the ureter， such as infection， abscess， or tumor， or abdominal or peri-toneal inflammation， may cause pain with movement of the adjacent iliopsoas muscle that presents as hip or groin pain.

【43】PID is another common cause of pelvic， groin， or hip pain that can cause psoas abscess and a subsequent positive ilio-psoas or obturator test. In this case it is most likely a young woman with multiple sexual partners who has a known or unknown case of untreated Chlamydia.

【44】The psoas muscle is not separated from the abdominal or pelvic cavity. Fig. 8.3 shows how most of the viscera， includ-ing the kidneys， sigmoid colon， jejunum， appendix， pancreas， abdominal aorta， and ureter， lie adjacent to the psoas muscle. Therefore any infectious or inflammatory process  can seed itself to the psoas muscle by direct extension， resulting in a psoas abscess-a localized collection of pus.

【6】### Differential Diagnosis

【7】Gynaecomastia, papillomas, benign and malignant stromal neoplasms, biphasic tumours (fibroadenoma and phyllodes tumour), reactive conditions such as fat necrosis, and metastatic tumours are the main differential diagnoses for male breast cancer. In most cases, based on clinical examination, imaging features, and preoperative core needle biopsy, a diagnosis can be easily established. Metastases from other solid neoplasms are sometimes difficult to diagnose. Metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma is commonly a diagnostic problem. Patients who receive hormonal therapy for prostatic adenocarcinoma almost always develop gynaecomastia, which may show epithelial proliferations mimicking DCIS. Identification of all criteria required to establish the diagnosis of DCIS is important. Immunohistochemical staining for high-molecular-weight cytokeratins may be helpful because hyperplastic lesions show strong positivity, whereas the expression of high-molecular-weight cytokeratins is significantly diminished or lost completely in DCIS. Myoepithelial markers can be used to establish the invasive versus in situ nature of the ductal carcinoma. Expression of prostate-specific antigen is commonly used to confirm the prostate origin of a metastatic carcinoma. It is a useful marker in males to differentiate primary breast cancer from metastases, but rarely a primary male breast cancer can disclose aberrant expression of prostate-specific antigen. Prostate-specific acid phosphatase hasso far not been reported in male breast cancer and can be used to establish the prostate origin of the cancer 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 50 , 51 \]</u>. Identification of intracytoplasmic mucin supports the diagnosis of breast carcinoma, as prostate carcinomas invariably fail to show any intracytoplasmic mucin.

【8】### Prognosis and Therapy Considerations

【9】The same staging system used for female breast cancer is used for staging male breast cancer 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 52 – 55 \]</u>. Tumour stage defined by tumour size and regional lymph node status is the most important prognostic factor of male breast cancer. Although experience with the sentinel lymph node procedure is relatively limited in male breast cancer, findings suggest that it is as accurate in males as in females 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 56 \]</u>. Similar to female breast cancer, in addition to size and stage of the tumour, other biologic factors such as tumour subtype have a clear influence on survival in male breast cancer. Treatment of male breast cancer is the same as for females. It can involve some combination of surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, and hormone or targeted therapy. Since most male breast cancers are hormone receptor-positive, hormone therapy is often used 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 57 \]</u>.

【71】### Definition

【72】Neoadjuvant, primary, or preoperative chemotherapy refers to the treatment of patients with systemic agents before definitive surgical removal of a tumour. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy was introduced in the early 1970s as the treatment of choice for inoperable, locally advanced breast cancer. This approach resulted in significant responses and downstaging of many tumours, permitting mastectomy in some patients. Gradually, the idea of neoadjuvant chemotherapy was extended to include patients with large but operable early-stage breast cancer, allowing the same possibility of tumour downstaging and breast-conserving surgery. Additionally, several randomised clinical trials and meta-analyses showed similar disease-free and overall survivals for patients who received chemotherapy in either an adjuvant or neoadjuvant setting. Today, based on these findings, neoadjuvant chemotherapy is considered an appropriate treatment option for most patients diagnosed with breast cancer where adjuvant chemotherapy was indicated 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 1 – 5 \]</u>. For patients with inflammatory breast cancer, neoadjuvant therapy is regarded as the standard of care. It is the preferred option for locally advanced breast cancer, and this approach allows both clinicians and patients to have an in vivo assessment of therapeutic efficacy, which can then be used as a surrogate marker to predict long-term survival 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 6 – 8 \]</u>. Additionally, neoadjuvant trials have been increasingly recognised as a promising platform for efficient testing of investigational compounds and experimental targeted therapies. Most of the current neoadjuvant therapy regimens include a combination of cytotoxic agents. In recent years, with the development of targeted therapy options, many different treatment protocols, which include hormonal and target-specific agents, have been used in the neoadjuvant setting. Assessment of the quantity and biology of the residual tumour can provide further prognostic information for patients receiving neoadjuvant therapy. The possibility of collecting tumour samples before, during, and after the neoadjuvant treatment offers a unique translational research opportunity to delineate the biologic actions of the often personalised, targeted compounds in vivo. Identifying response markers provides a valuable platform from which to advance personalised cancer therapy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 8 \]</u>.

【9】**KEY FEATURES OF THE HISTORY**

【10】When a patient has evidence of ST elevation (localized to specific leads and not global) on ECG and associated chest pain， the diagnosis is an acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) until proven other-wise. Obtaining the history can help support this diagnosis but does not change the initial management in these cases. Eliciting a detailed history in this setting can be difficult because the provider may not have much time with the patient before he or she is whisked to coronary angiography. It is important to get the most information possible during this time.

【11】The most important information to identify is whether the patient has known coronary artery disease， what the risk factors are， and what events took place surrounding the symptom onset. It is also important to assess whether the patient is on blood thinning medication or antiplate-let medication， whether he or she had bleeding issues， and whether any upcoming surgeries or procedures are planned. These important details are factored in if the patient requires a stent during coronary angiography. This information will help determine whether patients can safely receive a coronary intervention with a stent if necessary， whether they can take required medication afterward， and what kind of stent can be used.

【17】In the setting of a suspected STEMI， often the exam is focused on iden-tifying whether there is any hemodynamic instability and any signs of arrhythmia， heart failure， or adventitious lung or heart sounds. This patient's vital signs were stable without any major discrepancy in each arm and there were no abnormal exam findings. Her heart rhythm was sinus and she was oxygenating adequately on room air.

【18】Despite the critical and often time-sensitive presentation of STEMI， it is important that other acute issues be identified before the patient undergoes coronary angiography. This process typically takes place simultaneously while the interventional team is being notified and the patient is being prepared to go to the catheterization lab. 【26】This case is a nice example of troponin elevation in the absence of either a true type I or type II MI. Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is found in1% to 2% of troponin-positive patients who are suspected of having an acute coronary syndrome . It is thought to be due to a catecholamine surge that results in microvascular dysfunction and inflammatory activation .

Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is more common in women， and there is usually an antecedent emotional trigger leading to the presentation. It should always be part of the differential diagnosis when women present with an acute coronary syndrome. Takotsubo cardiomyopathy can mimic a STEMI presentation， as seen in this scenario. Typically， there is troponin elevation， but to a lesser degree than would be seen with a true STEMI. Studies have looked at ECG abnormalities in Takotsubo cardiomyopa-thy and STEMI in an attempt to differentiate the two， but ultimately the ECG alone cannot confirm the presence of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy and， owing to the negative impact of prolonging coronary angiography|删除0换行|in the presence of ST elevation， it remains the test of choice to confirm the diagnosis. Other studies have looked at the presence of circulating cate-cholamines in STEMI patients and patients with Takotsubo cardiomyopa-thy， and nearly 75% of patients with the latter had elevations higher than those seen in patients with STEMI .

【28】The Mayo Clinic developed criteria for the diagnosis of Takotsubo car-diomyopathy in 2004， and revised them in 2008. The presence of all four of the following criteria must be met ：

【29】1\. Transient hypokinesis， akinesis， or dyskinesis of the left ventricular mid-segments with or without apical involvement； the regional wall motion abnormalities extend beyond a single epicardial vascular distribution； a stressful trigger is often but not always present

【30】2.Absence of obstructive coronary artery disease or angiographic evidence of acute plaque rupture

【31】3\. New ECG abnormalities (ST-segment elevation or T-wave inversion)， or modest elevation in cardiac troponin

【32】4\. Absence of pheochromocytoma and myocarditis

【37】**SUMMARIZING THE SCENARIO**

This case scenario seemed to be a classic presentation of STEMI based on the ECG findings and the patient’s symptoms. Prompt evaluation and coronary angiography proved that she in fact did not have an MI， but|删除0换行|rather Takotsubo cardiomyopathy precipitated by profound emotional stress. The history should have led you to consider this as a possibility even though STEMI had to be ruled out.

【39】Most STEMI presentations do not have elevated troponin levels at the time they are drawn initially in the emergency department. As dis-cussed in earlier chapters， the current assays used do not detect myo-cardial injury for 3 to 4 hours. In classic presentations of acute coronary syndromes， patients develop chest pain or discomfort worrisome enough for them to seek medical attention not long after onset. The initial tro-ponin level typically is obtained within that 3- to 4-hour time frame of onset of pain， leading to undetectable levels on the first blood draw. In our case scenario， the patient had symptoms for 2 hours before presenta-tion， and the initial troponin level was already elevated. This agrees with information reported by Tomich 通用删除7(英):<u>(2017)</u>， who noted that troponin levels were elevated in 90% of patients with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy and， in addition， elevated at the time of admission.

【40】Researchers have attempted to identify patternspresent on ECG， ratios of various biomarkers， and other features of Takotsubo cardiomy-opathy to try to differentiate it from an acute coronary syndrome； how-ever， coronary angiography remains the gold standard to firmly diagnose the condition. Coronary artery disease may be present in patients who manifest Takotsubo cardiomyopathy； however， it is the absence ofobstruc-tive disease and the presence of myocardial inflammation that ultimately confirms this diagnosis.

【41】If this patient had presented without evidence of STEMI， the clinical suspicion of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy could have been further sup-ported by an early imaging study such as an echocardiogram. This would have demonstrated apical akinesis consistent with a picture of apical bal-looning syndrome， or Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. Although coronary angiography would still have been necessary to eliminate the possibility that ischemic heart disease had a role in the patient's symptoms， MI would have become second on the differential list to Takotsubo cardiomyopathy， rather than the primary working diagnosis， which in turn would have changed the prognostic implications.

Takotsubo cardiomyopathy has become more widely understood since it was first reported. It should be considered in any patient pre-senting with symptoms consistent with acute coronary syndrome and a|删除0换行|precipitating stressful event. Keep in mind the stressful event does not need to be negative and does not always have to be an emotional trigger. Physical stressors such as an acute illness with associated cardiac symp-toms should also raise the suspicion that Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is a possible cause.

【23】**1.3.1 Summary**

【24】**The prevalence and incidence of patients with dementia in the population is increasing because of the increasing life expectancies. Dementia is a clinical syndrome not a cause of disease. Neuropsychological testing in dementia has two goals： to increase the correctness of the differential diagnosis concerning the neuropathological cause and to help predict the psychosocial consequence of mild cognitive impairment and dementia(the ability to live at home and the need for external help). The first goal is based on the assumption that a specific neuropathological cause will also have a specific functional consequence. In reality， however， this assumption will not always be valid since some kinds of dementia have specific functional consequences and others have unspecific or varying impairments. Neuropsychology can only be of help for the first group of diseases by providing a possible diagnosis. However， for both groups neuropsychological assessment can help to measure the handicaps and to estimate whether the patients are still able to live independently. Up to now， there are no valid biomarkers for most kinds of dementia. Therefore the differential diagnosis is based on the clinicalassessment， whereby neuropsychology plays a major role.**

【1】### 4.4.1 Oral Contraceptives

【2】The estrogen in certain oral contraceptives suppresses ovarian androgen production and increases sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), resulting in an overall decrease in testosterone bioavailability 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 36 \]</u>. The FDA-approved oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for the treatment of acne include ethinyl estradiol with different progestins: norgestimate, norethindrone, and drospirenone 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 37 \]</u>. Although a Cochrane review in 2009 concluded that combined OCPs were more effective than placebo in controlling acne vulgaris, it has yet to be determined which combined OCPs are superior 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 38 \]</u>. There was a slightly greater improvement in acne with ethinyl estradiol/drospirenone versus ethinyl estradiol/norgestimate in one clinical trial, perhaps related to the antiandrogenic progestin 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 39 \]</u>.

【3】The risks associated with OCPs should be considered prior to initiating therapy. Individuals with a history of thromboembolic disease should not be placed on an OCP, and female smokers greater than 35 years of age should be counseled prior to treatment with an OCP due to the increased risk of thrombosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 40 , 41 \]</u>. Other reported side effects include nausea, decreased libido, breast tenderness, headache, breakthrough bleeding, mood disturbances, and potential for weight gain. Due to the risk of hyperkalemia with drospirenone-containing OCPs, these medications are contraindicated in patients with renal or adrenal insufficiency and hepatic dysfunction 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 40 \]</u>. Other than for rifampin, there is no definitive evidence to suggest that antibiotics increase OCP failure rate 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 42 \]</u>. 【73】Abstract

【74】Conventional topical and systemic therapeutics are effective for treating acne vulgaris, but are not perfect solutions. Topical salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide, and retinoid preparations can be irritating and present challenges with compliance. Systemic antibiotics also have issues with tolerability and increasing bacterial resistance, and isotretinoin has attracted negative attention due to its purported links to inflammatory bowel disease and depression. Laser and light-based treatments can potentially offer a viable adjunct or even alternative to these conventional options.

【75】5.1 Introduction
----------------

【76】Conventional topical and systemic therapeutics are effective for treating acne vulgaris, but are not perfect solutions. Topical salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide, and retinoid preparations can be irritating and present challenges with compliance. Systemic antibiotics also have issues with tolerability and increasing bacterial resistance, and isotretinoin has attracted negative attention due to its purported links to inflammatory bowel disease and depression. Laser and light-based treatments can potentially offer a viable adjunct or even alternative to these conventional options.

【77】5.2 Light/Photodynamic Therapy
------------------------------

【78】Light is thought to treat acne by taking advantage of the endogenous porphyrins produced by the pathogenic Propionibacterium acnes bacteria in sebaceous skin, coproporphyrin III and protoporphyrin IX. Porphyrin photoexcitation occurs maximally within the Soret band, with a peak in the blue light spectrum at approximately 410 nm, and additional smaller absorption peaks in the Q bands (500–635 nm) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 1 , 2 \]</u>. Porphyrin excitation initiates a cascade of events that leads to the production of reactive oxygen species and destruction of P . acnes . This reaction can be potentiated by the addition of aminolevulinic acid (ALA), an exogenous photosensitizer that preferentially localizes to sebaceous glands and enhances intracellular porphyrin synthesis, the so-called photodynamic therapy (PDT).

【79】There is a dearth of large, randomized controlled trials of lasers and lights for acne 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 3 \]</u>. One exception was an industry-sponsored evaluation of 266 severe acne patients treated with blue light (417 ± 5 nm) and 20 % aminolevulinic acid (ALA) (BLU-U ® and Levulan ® Kerastick, DUSA Pharmaceuticals, Inc.) versus blue light and vehicle alone 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 4 \]</u>. In this study, vehicle or ALA was applied for 45 min incubation followed by 16 min and 40 s of blue light (10 J/cm 2 total dose), one treatment every 3 weeks for four treatments. Interestingly the investigators found a decrease in inflammatory lesions of 37.5 % for the ALA group versus 41.7 % reduction in the vehicle group. Noninflammatory lesion counts were not performed. The study indicates that blue light alone is as effective as blue light plus ALA.

【80】Blue light penetrates to a depth of approximately 90–150 μm. Although it is unlikely that significant amount of this wavelength reaches the sebaceous gland, exposure to blue light at a wavelength of 405–420 nm destroys P . acnes . Furthermore, blue light may inhibit the production of interleukin-1 alpha and intercellular adhesion molecule-1 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 5 \]</u>, as well as tumor necrosis factor alpha and matrix metalloproteinase 2, all inflammatory mediators implicated in the pathogenesis of acne 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 6 \]</u>.

【81】Within the visible light spectrum, a longer wavelength of light correlates with deeper skin penetration, as there is less melanin absorption and less scattering by connective tissue. Red light penetrates deeper than blue light, to approximately 2 mm of depth. It effectively reaches the sebaceous glands and activates porphyrins via the Q band at 630 nm.
