Anaplastic lymphoma kinase \[ALK 通用删除11(英):<u>(p80)</u>\] and t(2；5) translocation are usually absent in cutaneous ALCL. Identification of IRF4-MUMI rearrangement by FISH indicates cutaneous ALCL， but it is found in 20%-26% of cases 通用删除6(英):<u>\[159，160，216\]</u>.**

**Clinical data， such as history of MF or precedent patches， plaques， or erythroderma， would support the diagnosis of MF undergoing large cell transformation (~50% of those cases are CD30+). Pagetoid reticulosis is a vari-ant of MF with prominent epidermotropism and frequent CD30 expression. The skin may be frequently involved by ATLL， with diffuse infiltrate of medium- to large-sized cells often expressing CD30. Correlation with clinical and laboratory data \[human T-lymphotropic virus Type l|删除0换行|(HTLV-1)\] helps in differential diagnosis. Classical HL only sporadically involves the skin and has to be differen-tiated from LYP.**

**LYP and primary cutaneous ALCL share the expression of CD30 and exhibit an excellent prognosis， but differ in the clinical presentation. LYP is characterized by chronic course of years to decades of recurrent papulonodular lesions， each of which undergoes spontaneous regression after weeks or months. In contrast to ALCL， LYP shows a prominent inflammatory background， which superficially resembles reactive process rather than lymphoma. Patients with LYP are at risk for secondary cutaneous or nodal lymphomas. It can be challenging and， in individual cases， even impossible to differentiate between LYP and primary cutaneous ALCL in patients presenting with a short his-tory of multifocal papulonodular lesions because， although|删除0换行|spontaneous regression of tumors is a hallmark of LYP， this has also been observed in patients with multifocal cutane-ous ALCL.**

Tumor cells show an aber-rant lack of CD2 (D) and CD5 (F) and are positive for CD3 (E)， CD7 (G)， CD56 (I)， granzyme B (J)， and TIA-1 (K).</u>

【9】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【10】The differential diagnosis includes PTCL， SPTL， CD8+ MF， pagetoid reticulosis， LYP (type D)， primary cutaneous yo+T-cell lymphoma， and recently reported indolent CD8+ lym-phoid proliferation of the ear 通用删除6(英):<u>\[6，173-176\]</u>.

【11】**PRIMARY CUTANEOUS FOLLICULAR HELPER T-CELL LYMPHOMA**

【12】This is a rare variant of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma character-ized by follicular helper T-cell (TrH) phenotype . Tumor cells are positive for pan-T-cell antigens and follicu-lar helper markers \[CD10， BCL6， programmed death (PD)-1， CXCL13， and inducible T-cell costimulator (ICOS)\]通用删除6(英):<u>\[177\]</u>. Relations of these lymphomas with the provisional entity of primary cutaneous small to medium CD4+ pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma， which are positive for PD-1， CXCL13， and BCL6but do not express CD10， are uncertain at this moment.

【13】**LYMPHOMATOID PAPULOSIS**

【14】The spectrum of CD30+ lymphoproliferative diseases of the skin includes CD30+ cutaneous ALCL， LYP， as well as bor-derline cases. LYP is an atypical lymphoproliferative process associated with recurrent skin lesions (papules) that often regress and reappear 通用删除6(英):<u>\[178-190\]</u>. LYP occurs predominantly in adults， but pediatric cases have been reported.

【15】**DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FOR LYP**

<mark>【16】人名段删除-1:Clinical Criteria</mark>teria**</u>

【17】**Recurrent self-healing grouped or disseminated papulo-nodular skin lesions (self-healing is defined as spontaneous regression of each individual tumor lesion within weeks or months， whether or not new lesions occur).**

【18】**LYP 通用删除6(英):<u>\[12，190\]</u> may manifest concurrently with MF， which is typically characterized by patches and eventually plaques or tumors.**

【19】通用删除16(英):<u>**FIGURE 44.25Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with TFH phenotype (CD10\*). Skin with a diffuse lymphoid infiltrate (A-C) showing the following phenotypes： CD2+ (D)， CD3-(E； some cells dimlyt)，CD5+(F)， CD7-(G)， CD4+(H)， CD8-(I)，CD10+(J)， and BCL6+ (K).**</u>

【20】**Histologic Criteria**

【21】LYP type A. Wedge-shaped infiltrate with scattered or clustered CD30+ tumor cells， intermingled with numerous inflammatory cells， such as small lympho-cytes，neutrophils， eosinophils， and histiocytes. This type is the most common histologic presentation.

【22】LYP type B. Epidermotropic infiltrate of small atypical CD30\* or CD30-lymphoid cells with cerebriform nuclei that histologically resemble MF.

【23】**LYP type C. Cohesive sheets of CD30+ large atypical lymphoid cells with only a few admixed reactive inflammatory cells.**

【24】LYP type D. Epidermotropic infiltrate of small- to medium-sized atypical CD8+ and CD30+ lymphoid cells that histologically resemble primary cutaneous aggressive epidermotropic CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma.

【25】**MORPHOLOGY**

【26】**Morphologically， three major types of LYP are recog-nized， designated types A， B， and C. Type A is the most common histologic variant (~70%-80% of cases) and shows numerous inflammatory cells (histiocytes， granulo-cytes， and eosinophils) and large CD30+ tumor cells with irregular nuclei 通用删除1(英):<u></u>. Type B**

【27】(“lymphocytic”type) shows numerous lymphoid cells with cerebriform nuclei， which may often lack CD30 expression通用删除6(英):<u>\[180，182，184\]</u>. The third variant， type C， is characterized by diffuse large cell infiltrate similar to ALCL (termed ALCL， LYP-like)； it differs from ALCL by clinical features， which are similar to other types of LYP (recurrent asymptomatic papular nodular lesions over years). Some patients may dis-play a mixed pattern (A and B， A and C， and even A， B， and C) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[182\]</u>. Recently， a variant of LYP resembling aggressive CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma has been identified and termed type D 通用删除6(英):<u>\[174\]</u>. This subtype displays cytotoxic phe-notype (BF1+， CD3+， CD4-， CD8+)， with at least one cyto-toxic marker (TIA-1， granzyme B). The correct diagnosis of this variant relies on clinical presentation， which is typical for LYP.

【28】**IMMUNOPHENOTYPE**

【29】**Majority of cases are CD4+， but CD8+ LYP has been reported通用删除6(英):<u>\[180，191\]</u>. Lesional cells express pan-T-cell markers， often with an aberrant loss of one or more antigens， CD25， and CD30. CD8+ LYP defines a distinctive entity with characteristic light microscopic and phenotypic findings and has a predilection for young males 通用删除6(英):<u>\[191\]</u>. CD56 expression has been reported in LYP cases 通用删除6(英):<u>\[192\]</u>. Almost all LYPs express one or more of the cytotoxic proteins (TIA-1， granzyme B，perforin).**

【30】通用删除16(英):<u>FIGURE 44.26 LYP. (A) Low magnification shows a pleomorphic lymphoid infiltrate in the dermis. (B) High magnification show large neoplastic cells mixed with inflammatory cells. Tumor cells express EMA (C) and CD30(D).</u>

【31】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【32】The distinction between primary cutaneous ALCL and LYP is based on the relative predominance of CD30\* atypical large cells， but there is a degree of histologic overlap between those disorders and differentiating between LYP and ALCL(as well as MF and other T-cell lymphomas) may be very dif-ficult， if not impossible in some cases 通用删除6(英):<u>\[189，193\]</u>. Additionally， patients with LYP may have associated lymphoid malig-nancies， usually HL and MF 通用删除6(英):<u>\[182，194-196\]</u>. In 5%-20% of patients， LYP may be proceeded by， associated with， or fol-lowed by another type of malignant lymphoma， including MF， cutaneous ALCL， or HL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[183，197\]</u>. Clinical information is very important in the diagnosis of LYP since it appears malignant histologically， but has a benign clinical course通用删除6(英):<u>\[198\]</u>. CD8+LYP has to be differentiated from primary cuta-neous aggressive epidermotropic CD8+ T-cell lymphoma. Cases with clinical features of LYP but with morphology suggestive of primary aggressive CD8+ T-cell lymphoma have been reported and classified as LYP type D 通用删除6(英):<u>\[174\]</u>.

【33】Strong TRAF1 expression in the tumor cells of most LYP cases (42/49， 84%) helps to distinguish LYP from primary or secondary ALCL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[178\]</u>. Although single-cell analysis of CD30+cells in LYP showed a common clonal T-cell origin in all LYP cases 通用删除6(英):<u>\[199\]</u>， T-cell clonality can only be found in a minority(22%) of archival LYP specimens， even when employing a highly sensitive detection method， and is thus of limited diag-nostic value 通用删除6(英):<u>\[200\]</u>. Therefore， final diagnosis of LYP has to be based mainly on clinical and morphologic/immunophenotypic findings rather than on results of clonality studies 通用删除6(英):<u>\[200\]</u>.

【34】**PRIMARY CUTANEOUS ALCL**

【35】ALCL is divided into two categories： (systemic) ALCL and pri-mary cutaneous ALCL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[11，180，183，188，190，201-212\]</u>. Primary cutaneous ALCL manifests in most patients with a solitary or grouped rapidly growing and ulcerating large tumors or thick plaques. Spontaneous complete or partial regression of the tumor(s) is reported in up to 44% of patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[183，203，213\]</u>. Both types are characterized by diffuse large cell CD30+ infiltrate with pleomorphic， often horseshoe-shaped nuclei (hallmark cells). Primary cutaneous ALCL differs from systemic ALCL and secondary (CD30\*) PTCLs involving the skin by being limited to the skin at the time of diagnosis and (in a vast major-ity of cases) by lack of ALK expression and/or t(2；5) transloca-tion 通用删除6(英):<u>\[74，203，205\]</u>. Most patients with primary cutaneous ALCL have limited disease， but multicentric involvement may occur. Although partial or complete spontaneous regression may occur， frequent relapses and dissemination may occur.

【36】**DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FOR CUTANEOUS ALCL**

【37】人名段删除-1:<u>**Clinical Criteria**</u>

【38】Solitary， grouped， or multifocal nodular lesions 通用删除6(英):<u>\[12，190\]</u>

【39】No clinical evidence of LYP， MF， or other types of cutaneous T-cell lymphomas

【40】**Absence of extracutaneous involvement assessed by staging procedures**

【41】**Histologic Criteria**

【42】· Dense nodular dermal infiltrate composed of large pleomorphic， anaplastic， or immunoblastic cells with large， irregularly shaped nuclei and an abun-dant pale or eosinophilic cytoplasm. Clusters of small reactive lymphocytes and eosinophils may be found within and surrounding the tumor cells.

【43】Immunophenotypically， CD30+ is expressed by at least 75% of tumor cells. In addition， CD4 or CD8 is expressed in most cases with a variable loss of pan-T-cell antigens (CD2， CD3， and CD5).

【44】**MORPHOLOGY**

【45】The morphologic features of primary cutaneous ALCL are similar to those of its systemic counterpart. There is either a diffuse monomorphic large cell infiltrate or a highly pleo-morphic infiltrate with numerous multinucleated giant cells resembling Reed-Sternberg cells . Neutrophil-rich variants were also reported. The latter vari-antis more common. The tumor involves the upper and lower dermis， but both epidermotropism and subcutaneous tissue involvement are uncommon.

【46】**IMMUNOPHENOTYPE**

【47】**Phenotypically， tumor cells are positive for CD45， CD43， and CD30 (strong membranous and Golgi staining)； pan-T-cell markers (CD2， CD3， CD5， CD7)， often with an aberrant loss of one or more antigens (most commonly CD7)； and frequently cytotoxic proteins (granzyme B， TIA-1， and/or perforin). Most tumors are CD4\*. In contrast to secondary skin involvement by systemic ALCL， primary cutaneous ALCLs typically do not express ALK and epithelial membrane antigen (EMA). Rare cases of ALK+ primary cutaneous ALCL have been reported， characterized by cytoplasmic (or rarely nuclear and cytoplas-mic) ALK expression， variant ALK rearrangement， and posi-tive FISH studies with ALK break-apart (BA) probe 通用删除6(英):<u>\[214，215\]</u>. In some cases， ALK expression may represent transformed MF with secondary ALK translocation 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1971</u>**

【48】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【49】The differential diagnosis of primary cutaneous ALCL includes other CD30+ disorders：systemicCALCL， ATLL， LYP， PTCL， pagetoid reticulosis/MF， classical HL， and MF undergoing large cell transformation. Activated T and B cells in reactive cutaneous disorders may also express CD30. The distinction between primary and secondary CD30+ T-cell lymphomas， as well as between transformed MF and de novo primary cutane-ous ALCL， is not possible based solely on the histologic and immunophenotypic features. Positive ALK usually indicates systemic ALCL， but subset of systemic ALCL is ALK- and rare cases of primary cutaneous ALCL with cytoplasmic ALK expression have been reported (usually in pediatric

Identification of IRF4-MUMI rearrangement by FISH indicates cutaneous ALCL， but it is found in 20%-26% of cases 通用删除6(英):<u>\[159，160，216\]</u>.**

**Clinical data， such as history of MF or precedent patches， plaques， or erythroderma， would support the diagnosis of MF undergoing large cell transformation (~50% of those cases are CD30+). Pagetoid reticulosis is a vari-ant of MF with prominent epidermotropism and frequent CD30 expression. The skin may be frequently involved by ATLL， with diffuse infiltrate of medium- to large-sized cells often expressing CD30. Correlation with clinical and laboratory data \[human T-lymphotropic virus Type l|删除0换行|(HTLV-1)\] helps in differential diagnosis. Classical HL only sporadically involves the skin and has to be differen-tiated from LYP.**

**LYP and primary cutaneous ALCL share the expression of CD30 and exhibit an excellent prognosis， but differ in the clinical presentation. LYP is characterized by chronic course of years to decades of recurrent papulonodular lesions， each of which undergoes spontaneous regression after weeks or months. In contrast to ALCL， LYP shows a prominent inflammatory background， which superficially resembles reactive process rather than lymphoma. Patients with LYP are at risk for secondary cutaneous or nodal lymphomas. It can be challenging and， in individual cases， even impossible to differentiate between LYP and primary cutaneous ALCL in patients presenting with a short his-tory of multifocal papulonodular lesions because， although|删除0换行|spontaneous regression of tumors is a hallmark of LYP， this has also been observed in patients with multifocal cutane-ous ALCL.**

【58】**CUTANEOUS y6 T-CELL LYMPHOMA**

【59】Cutaneous yǒ T-cell lymphoma is a clonal T-cell prolifera-tion with an aggressive clinical behavior and chemoresis-tance； preference for involvement of extremities in the form of disseminated plaques， nodules， or tumors； and frequent involvement of mucosal and other extranodal sites 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，3\]</u>. This provisional entity also includes cases previously diag-nosed as SPTL with yo phenotype (SPTL-y8) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[3，217\]</u>. Three subtypes of cutaneous yo T-cell lymphoma are recognized：epidermotropic， dermal， and subcutaneous 通用删除6(英):<u>\[3\]</u>. Mucosal and other locations (apart from skin) are frequently involved， but the disease usually spares the lymph nodes. Cases with a panniculitis-like growth pattern may present with hemo-phagocytic syndrome (HPS) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[6，176\]</u>. The prognosis is poor with 5-year survival of 11%.

【60】Tumor cells are intermediate to large in size with a cyto-toxic phenotype： TCR-BF1-， TCR-yl， CD2+， CD3+， CD5-， CD7+/-， CD56+， CD4-， and CD8-(although rare CD8+ cases have been reported). The term“SPTL”is now restricted to a group of cases characterized morphologically by an exclusive involvement of subcutaneous tissues， immunohistochemi-cally by a T-cytotoxic ap phenotype， and biologically by a relatively good prognosis (SPTL-0B) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[218\]</u>.

【61】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【62】**The main differential diagnosis includes SPTL. SPTL dif-fers by the subcutaneous architecture (rather than subcutane ous and/or dermal/epidermal in y8 T-cell lymphoma) and the immunophenotype (CD4-， C8+， CD56-， and TCR-B1+). HPS is more common in yo T-cell lymphomas than SPTL.**

【63】**PRIMARY CUTANEOUS CD4+ SMALL/MEDIUM-SIZED PLEOMORPHIC T-CELL LYMPHOMA**

【64】PCSM-TCL is a rare and provisional category of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. It presents with solitary/localized pap-ules， nodules， plaques， or tumors， most often of the head and neck area (especially the face) or the upper trunk， has favorable prognosis and is characterized morphologically and phenotypically by CD4+ pleomorphic T-cell infiltrate of small- to intermediate-sized cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，3，12，74，75，219-2231</u>. Patients have no history of the patches and plaques typi-cal of MF. Multifocal l1esions are uncommon and are associated with an aggressive course requiring systemic chemotherapy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[221\]</u>.

【11】**Disease Definition**

【12】__ Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma， nasal type is an aggressive， primarily extranodal lym-phoma characterized by vascular destruc-tion， necrosis，cytotoxic phenotype， and association with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). Most cases are of NK cell origin， but a sub-set showsSacytotoxicT-cell phenotype.

【13】**Epidemiology**

【14】\-More frequent in Asian and native atin American populations.

【15】__ Usually adults. More common in males than females.

【16】May occur in the setting of immunosuppres-sion (e.g.，posttransplant).

【17】**Preferential Sites of Involvement**

【18】\-Upper aerodigestive tract： nasal cavity (proto-typic)， nasopharynx， paranasal sinuses， and palate (“lethal midline granuloma").

【19】__ The skin， soft tissue， gastrointestinal tract， and testis are common sites of involvement.

【20】**\- Bone marrow involvement is uncommon.**

【21】Secondary lymph node involvement is rare. The WHO 2016 classification recognizes a subtype of nodal peripheral T-cell lymphoma unspecified (PTCL) cases as node-based EBV-positive PTCL.Unlikeeextranodal NK/T-ceellll 1lymphomna. nasal type，these PTCL cases lack angioinvasion and necrosis.

【22】**ClinicalFeatures**

【23】__ Skin lesions are usually nodular， and ulcer-ation is common . Erythematous or violaceous plaques and tumors.

【24】\-If nasal1 involvement： symptomsof nasal obstruction or epistaxis.Eventually， extensive midfacial destructive lesions with large ulcers.

【25】High-stage disease (involvement of multiple sites) at presentation is common.

【26】\- B symptoms may be present.

【27】\- Hemophagocytic syndrome may occur

【28】_Less common presentations： Cutaneous pre-_ sentation with subtle macular lesions or with patches resembling mycosis fungoides has been reported. Persistent prominent facial swelling. Intestinal lesions may present with perforation. Other involved sites may present with mass lesions.

【29】**Histomorphology**

【30】\- Pattern： Dense diffuse lymphoid infiltrate in the dermis with frequent pannicular extension. Angiocentric and angiodestructive pattern is characteristic ， though not always present in every biopsy. Ulceration and necrosis are common . Apoptosis is frequent.

【31】_Less common patterns： Epidermotropism and_ Pautrier microabscesses may be seen. Interface change at the dermal-epidermal junction. Vascular fibrinoid changes without angioinva-sive infiltration. Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia.

【32】__ Neoplastic cells： Broad cytologic spectrum(small-， intermediate-sized， large or anaplas-tic). Admixture of small and large cells is common. Nuclei may be irregularly folded or elongated. Usually granular chromatin(but vesicular in large cells). Inconspicuous to small nucleoli. Moderate cytoplasm (often pale or clear). Frequent mitotic figures.

【33】_1_ Reactive cells： Neutrophils are common if ulceration is present. Some cases may have mixed inflammatory infiltrate (small lymphocytes， plasma cells， eosinophils， and histiocytes) or granulomatous inflammation.

【34】**Immunophenotype**

【35】\- Most typical pattern： CD2+， CD3+，CD56+， and EBV+. Positive cytotoxic proteins (TIA-1.granzymeB，perforin). Frequently positive：CD43. CD45RO， HLA-DR， and CD25. CD7 and CD30 may be expressed . Frequently negative：CD4， CD8， CD5，betaF1，CD16，and CD57.

【36】As the name indicates， extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma， nasal type may be of NK-cell ori-gin((more commons)COr T-cell origin. Depending on the cell of origin， there may be some differences in immunophenotype.

【37】**Unlike T cells. NK cells lack surface CD3.** Therefore， NK cells are CD3-negative by flow cytometry (since flow generally analyzes sur-face membrane proteins). However， NK cells express the epsilon chain of CD3 within the cytoplasm. Since the epitope of CD3 antibody targets the epsilon chain， NK cells stain posi- **tive with CD3 immunohistochemistry.**

【38】__ While CD56 expression is generally present， some cases of cytotoxic T-cell origin may be CD56-negative. Therefore， in the setting of angiocentrism and cytotoxic phenotype，EBV in situlhybridization(EBER)Sshouldbe obtained.

【39】\- If an atypical infiltrate is both CD56- and EB V-negative， the process is likely not extra-nodal NK/T-cell lymphoma， nasal type.

【40】**Genetics**

【41】\- As the name indicates， extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma， nasal type may be of NK-cell ori-gin or T-cell origin. Depending on the cell of origin， PCR results will be different. NK-cell origin (most common type) will be associated with negative T-cell clonality (germline con-figuration). Monoclonalrearrangementof T-cell receptor genes occurs in a minority of cases (cytotoxic T-cell origin).

【44】__ Variable but generally poor. Prolonged sur-vival reported in rare cases.

【46】\- Adverse risk factors： high titer of circulating EBV DNA， advanced stage disease， unfavor-able International Prognostic Index(IPI)， invasion of bone and skin， presence of EBV-positive cells in the bone marrow.

【51】(Cases with involvement of subcutaneous tis-sue may resemble subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma (SPTCL). While both are composed of cytotoxic TIA1-positive cells， SPTCL is CD56-negative and EBV-negative and lacks dermal involvement.

【63】**Pearls and Pitfalls**

【64】**1\. Ulceration is seen in some cases of advanced， tumor-stage mycosis fungoi-des (MF). The presence of ulceration at initial presentation would ：suggesta non-MF process.**

【65】**2\. Some pseudolymphomasmay also demonstrate ulceration. These include pityriasis lichenoides and infectious processes， such as leishmaniasis and inflamed molluscum contagiosum.**

【66】**3\. If ulceration is not seen in a skin biopsy， it does not necessarily mean that the patient does not have ulcerated lesions elsewhere， since dermatologists often avoid biopsying lesions with secondary changes. Careful correlation of clinical and histopathologic findings is essential.**

【67】**4\. Angiocentrism is not always present in every biopsy of an angioinvasive lym-phoid process. Clues for the diagnosis would include infarct-like necrosis and cytotoxic immunophenotype. EBV in situ hybridization (EBER) and careful clinical pathologic correlation would be essential for proper classification.**

【68】**5\. Infiltration and destruction of blood ves-sel walls is generally not a feature of intravascular lymphomas (atypical lym-phocytes within vessel lumens).**

**_6\._ The threshold of positivity is variable for different markers. For example， for ana-plastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL； one|删除0换行|of the cutaneous CD30-positive lympho-proliferative disorders)， CD30 must be positive in at least 75% of atypical cells(i.e.， even if 60% of an infiltrate marks with CD30， that level of staining is not sufficient for ALCL， and other entities should be considered in the differential diagnosis). A high cutoff is also used for CD56 (i.e.， if only a small subset of cells stain with CD56 in a lymphoid infiltrate， thatprocess is consideredCD56-negative) .**

【70】**7\. While several lymphomas may express EBV， the identification of EBV may or may not be part of the minimum diag-nostic criteria for a particular lymphoma. For example， Burkitt lymphoma is frequently EBV-positive， but if a case of Burkitt lym-phoma were EBV-negative， this would not change the diagnosis. In contrast， a nasal T-cell lymphoma that is CD3-positive and CD56-negative but nega-tive for EBV would not be classified as extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma nasal _type._**

【71】**8\. In situ hybridization for Epstein-Barr encoded RNA (EBER) is the most reli-able method to demonstrate the pres-ence of EBV. Immunohistochemical stains for LMP1 are inconsistent.**

【94】\- Hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoprolifera-tive disorder is part of the group of EBV(Epstein-Barr virus)-positive T-cell and NK-cell lymphoproliferative diseases of child-hood. 【95】__ Hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoprolifera-tive disorder is a primarily cutaneous disorder of polyclonal or (most often) monoclonal T cells or NK cells with a broad spectrum of clinical aggressiveness. 【71】### 7.2.7 Complications

【72】Mainly: epididymitis, orchitis, prostatitis, salpingitis, pelviperitonite, perihepatitis, infertility, sterility and arthritis.

【73】### 7.2.8 Differential Diagnosis

【74】Other urethritis, gonococcal urethritis particularly, as well as the ones caused by Mycoplasma sp. Ureaplasma urealyticum , Trichomonas vaginalis or chemical or traumatic urethritis. Men with testicular pain or increase may have tumor or testicular torsion.

【75】### 7.2.9 Observations

【76】*   The Chlamydia trachomatis infection has high incidence and prevalence worldwide. Women are the majority of cases. More than 90 million cases are identified in the world each year and most of them are asymptomatic. A third of women with this infection will have pelvic inflammatory disease.

【77】*   Routines employed in several developed countries to research Chlamydia trachomatis in sexually active teenagers reveal important rates of positivity. It provides diagnosis and early treatment and tends to prevent complications and sequelae in the upper genital tract.

【78】*   Quinolones and Tetracyclines are contraindicated for pregnant women, nursing mothers and children.

【79】*   In 2006, a new variant of Chlamydia trachomatis (swCT) was found in Sweden, but not identified by molecular biology tests commercially available. This happened because many patients with clinical processes compatible with Chlamydia had negative tests. We believe that over time this strain will spread all over the world, since cases were reported in Denmark, Norway and Ireland.

【242】**A. General considerations： Hereditary spastic paraparesis is a clinically and genetically heterogenous disorder with in-ter and intra familial variation. It is divided into AD， AR， X-linked and syndromic forms. In addition， spastic para-paresis complicates many acquired forms of spinal cord pathologies and is a major component of both demyelinat-ing and dysmyelinating conditions.**

【243】**At present， 18 genetic loci have been reported of which ten are AD， three X-linked and five are autosomal reces-sive. The pure form is an insidiously progressive spastic paraparesis with a neurogenic bladder and distal vibratory loss in the legs.**

【244】**Uncomplicated HSP refers to the pure form in which both the corticospinal and dorsal column systems are involved. Complicated HSP has additional neurological deficits that include optic neuritis， macular and cerebel-lar degeneration， ichthyosis， seizures， cataracts， cognitive dysfunction， and extrapyramidal signs.**

【241】**Hereditary Spastic Paraparesis (Strumpell-Lorrain Syndrome)**

【242】**A. General considerations： Hereditary spastic paraparesis is a clinically and genetically heterogenous disorder with in-ter and intra familial variation. It is divided into AD， AR， X-linked and syndromic forms. In addition， spastic para-paresis complicates many acquired forms of spinal cord pathologies and is a major component of both demyelinat-ing and dysmyelinating conditions.**

【243】**At present， 18 genetic loci have been reported of which ten are AD， three X-linked and five are autosomal reces-sive. The pure form is an insidiously progressive spastic paraparesis with a neurogenic bladder and distal vibratory loss in the legs.**

【244】**Uncomplicated HSP refers to the pure form in which both the corticospinal and dorsal column systems are involved. Complicated HSP has additional neurological deficits that include optic neuritis， macular and cerebel-lar degeneration， ichthyosis， seizures， cataracts， cognitive dysfunction， and extrapyramidal signs.**

【241】**Hereditary Spastic Paraparesis (Strumpell-Lorrain Syndrome)**

【242】**A. General considerations： Hereditary spastic paraparesis is a clinically and genetically heterogenous disorder with in-ter and intra familial variation. It is divided into AD， AR， X-linked and syndromic forms. In addition， spastic para-paresis complicates many acquired forms of spinal cord pathologies and is a major component of both demyelinat-ing and dysmyelinating conditions.**

【243】**At present， 18 genetic loci have been reported of which ten are AD， three X-linked and five are autosomal reces-sive. The pure form is an insidiously progressive spastic paraparesis with a neurogenic bladder and distal vibratory loss in the legs.**

【244】**Uncomplicated HSP refers to the pure form in which both the corticospinal and dorsal column systems are involved. Complicated HSP has additional neurological deficits that include optic neuritis， macular and cerebel-lar degeneration， ichthyosis， seizures， cataracts， cognitive dysfunction， and extrapyramidal signs.**

【245】**B. Genetic features： The average age of onset of symptoms is due to which genetic locus may be involved in uncom-plicated HSP； otherwise they present similarly.**

【241】**Hereditary Spastic Paraparesis (Strumpell-Lorrain Syndrome)**

【242】**A. General considerations： Hereditary spastic paraparesis is a clinically and genetically heterogenous disorder with in-ter and intra familial variation. It is divided into AD， AR， X-linked and syndromic forms. In addition， spastic para-paresis complicates many acquired forms of spinal cord pathologies and is a major component of both demyelinat-ing and dysmyelinating conditions.**

【243】**At present， 18 genetic loci have been reported of which ten are AD， three X-linked and five are autosomal reces-sive. The pure form is an insidiously progressive spastic paraparesis with a neurogenic bladder and distal vibratory loss in the legs.**

【244】**Uncomplicated HSP refers to the pure form in which both the corticospinal and dorsal column systems are involved. Complicated HSP has additional neurological deficits that include optic neuritis， macular and cerebel-lar degeneration， ichthyosis， seizures， cataracts， cognitive dysfunction， and extrapyramidal signs.**

【245】**B. Genetic features： The average age of onset of symptoms is due to which genetic locus may be involved in uncom-plicated HSP； otherwise they present similarly.**

【247】2\. The average age of onset after age 20 is most typical of SGP8 and SGP6

【248】**3\. Approximately 50% of AD uncomplicated HSP are linked to SPG4**

【251】**6\. Two genes have been identified for an X-linked form of complicated HSP**

【252】**C. Clinical features of uncomplicated HSP：**

【253】**1\. Bilateral lower extremity weakness； anterior tibialis， hamstrings and iliopsoas muscles are most involved**

【6】**Viral Torticollis**

【7】Also called rheumatic stiff neck， this condition is characterized by ten-der stiff neck， mainly on lateral or rotatory movements rather than on flexion， due to acute spasm of sternomastoid muscle， presumably as a result of a viral infection. It has nothing to do with rheumatic fever or rheumatoid arthritis.

【8】**Trauma**

【9】Stiff neck may result from trauma to the neck say a hard blow， lead-ing to contusion and strain of the ligaments and muscles.

【10】**Congenital Anomalies**

【11】Congenital anomalies of the cervical vertebrae may be responsible for torticollis in some cases.

Congenital torticollis refers to a condition in which there is devel-opmental shortening of the sternomastoid muscle of one side. Inability to turn the newborn's head 90° in both directions after l week of age should arouse suspicion of this diagnosis. You may feel a firm lump in the midportion of the affected muscle during|删除0换行|the first 2 to 3 months. Left untreated， the muscle becomes fibrotic and shortened， resulting in permanent limitation of neck move-ments. The head and face also become asymmetrical.

【13】This entity may well be the same as sternomastoid tumor.

【14】**Remaining Causes of Stiff Neck**

【15】Lumbar puncture， poliomyelitis， tetanus， intracranial hemorrhage or tumor， rheumatoid arthritis， meningeal leukemia， spastic cerebral palsy， myositis ossificans progressiva， etc.

【16】Stridor is defined as an audibly harsh， noisy inspiratory sound as a re-sult of incomplete obstruction of the laryngeal area or trachea. Often it is accompanied by croupy cough，hoarseness， dyspnea， restlessness and feeding difficulties.

【17】In stridor manifesting at birth， always consider the possibility of traumaaiiff intubation had been done， and obstruction caused by mucus， meconium or blood. This kind of stridor usually disappears within 24 hours.

【18】Find out if the stridor is worsening? If the answer is in affirma-tive， there is strong possibility of an anatomical obstruction or vocal cord paralysis.

【19】Is the stridor accompanied by significant respiratory distress? Laryn-geal atresia and tracheal atresia， both serious conditions， need to be con-sidered in this situation.

【20】Hoarseness accompanying stridor in a newborn suggests a laryn-geal problem with the sole exception of laryngomalacia.

【21】Stridor with brassy or barking cough in a newborn points to a tracheal problem.

【22】Does the newborn tend to keep the neck in an hyperextended posi-tion? Does he have dysphagic symptoms? If yes， chances are of your dealing with a case of vascular rings.

【23】Physical examination should， in particular， ascertain if the newborn has severe dyspnea with cyanosis and chest retraction. Any glossoptosis， micrognathia， or choanal atresia?

【24】In stridor manifesting during postneonatal period and later， find out if the child had been hale and hearty prior to the onset of this problem. Does he have fever， cough， hoarseness， sore throat

**Stridor|删除换行|or dyspnea? Is he in the habit of putting foreign body into his mouth?

【26】While conducting clinical check-up， you must focus on certain vital points. Is the stridor purely inspiratory， expiratory or both? Is it inter-mittent， or persistent? Is there respiratory distress. Is there any extrinsic neck mass? Any evidence of injury? Is the throat congested?

【27】**STRIDOR MANIFESTING IN THE NEONATAL PERIOD Laryngomalacia**

【28】Also called congenital laryngeal stridor， this condition is responsible for nearly 90% of cases of stridor in the neonatal period. The cause is abnormal collapse of the supraglottic tissues (elongated or curved epiglottis， redundant aryteno-epiglottic folds) during inspiratory phase.

【29】Manifestations occur usually after the first week or two of birth. Stridor is characteristically intermittent. It is mainly inspiratory though， at times， it may be partly expiratory. During sleep and rest， it disappears whereas crying or excitement aggravates it. It is much less in prone position but is increased in supine position. The voice， cry， feeding and general health of the baby remain unaffected. Dyspnea with indrawing of the lower part of the chest during inspiration occur in a large majori-ty of the cases.

【30】After the age of 6 months， the manifestations begin to regress.The condition disappears by the age of 18 to 24 months.

【31】**Atretic Obstructive Lesions in the Upper Airway**

【32】Congenital atretic lesions of the upper airway usually cause death soon after birth. In supraglottic web， the infant has inspiratory stridor in association with hoarseness， subdued cry and chest indrawing. La-ryngeal webs and cyst cause hoarse cry， dyspnea and inspiratory stri-dor. Stridor as a result of subglottic pathology (congenital subglottic stenosis， hemangioma， angioma， papilloma，lymphangioma， polypi) is both inspiratory and expiratory. Hoarseness may be present. Cry is normal. Brassy or croupy cough may sometimes accompany the clini-cal picture.

【33】**Differential Diagnosis in Pediatrics**

【34】Tracheomalacia， tracheal cyst or tracheal stenosis leads to expi-ratory stridor.

【35】Laryngeal obstruction from presence of mucus， meconium or blood together with edema from trauma of intubation is an important cause of inspiratory stridor. It resolves well within 24 hours， particularly if aspiration of the obstructive stuff can be carried out under direct vision without loss of time.

【36】Vocal cord paralysisParalysis of the recurrent laryngealnerve(usually right) may occur in hydrocephalus associated Arnold-Chiari malformation or in brainstem injury. Bilateral paralysis may occur.

【37】Manifestations， more marked in bilateral involvement， include in-spiratory stridor， hoarseness， weak cry and choking during feeding.

【38】Laryngoscopy shows lack of mobility of the vocal cords.

【39】**Vascular Rings**

【40】Stridor in vascular rings (double aorta or an abnormally placed subcla-vian artery) is， as a rule， intermittent and both inspiratory and expira-tory though it may be purely inspiratory or expiratory. Accompanying features include intractable cough which may be brassy or bitonal， and opisthotonos. An attempt at flexing the neck worsens the stridor.

【41】Diagnosis is by exclusion of other causes and by lateral X-ray of the airway.

【42】Outside compression from mediastinal or neck tumors (say lymphan-gioma， goiter) may produce stridor. There usually is some more evi-dence of compression， making the diagnosis easy.

【43】**STRIDOR MANIFESTING IN LATER INFANCY AND CHILDHOOD**

【44】人名段删除-1:<u>**Acute Laryngotracheobronchitis**</u>

【45】This condition， caused usually by H. influenzae or parainfluenzae virus and also termed croup， is the most common cause of acute

**Stridor|删除换行|inspiratory stridor. It occurs in children， usually under 3 years of age.

【47】Following one or two days history of "cold"， the child develops inspiratory stridor， usually at night. He begins to hyperventilate and is quite upset. As the stridor persists， cyanosis and lower chest retraction develops. With further progression of the disease， impairment of the consciousness occurs. Trachea and bronchi may become partially ob-structed by thick secretions resulting in expiratory stridor and coarse rhonchi in the lung fields.

【48】人名段删除-1:<u>**Acute Epiglottitis**</u>

【49】This state of acute septicemia usually caused by H. influenzae type B， Staphylococcus or Pneumococcus， is characterized by rapid development of inspiratory stridor， dyspnea， muffling of the voice， dysphagia and drooling. The child is febrile and flushed. With increasing respiratory effort， inspiratory stridor diminishes. Throat examination shows an in-tensely red and swollen epiglottis.

【50】**Foreign Body**

【51】Sudden development of inspiratory stridor in a child who was other-wise fine， particularly if he is left to eat unattended and is fond of tak-ing small objects into the mouth， must arouse suspicion of a foreign body having got impacted in the larynx.

【52】Laryngeal diphtheria may be responsible for inspiratory stridor. Addition-al manifestations include hoarseness， aphonia， brassy or barking cough， dyspnea and cyanosis， restlessness， anxiety and prostration. Neck shows lymphadenitis and brawny edema (bull-neck).

【53】Diagnosis is by observing the characteristic membrane in the throat. In a vast majority of the cases， laryngeal involvement is secondary to faucial diphtheria. You may， however， readily see the membrane in the larynx by laryngoscopy.

【54】In order to establish the diagnosis， you must take a throat/ laryn-geal swab and examine the smear for the organisms which are seen as rods with bipolar bar.

【55】Any trauma to the larynx， resulting from instrumentation， corrosive agents or inhalation of smoke， may be responsible for laryngeal edema and acute stridor.

【56】Laryngospasm， associated with tetany of whatsoever etiology， may manifest with inspiratory stridor， apneic episodes and cyanosis. The attacks last over a few minutes and keep recurring.

【57】**Retropharyngeal Abscess**

【58】A retropharyngeal abscess manifests with inspiratory stridor only when pressure is put on the larynx. Clinical features include an abrupt onset of high fever， dysphagia， refusal of feeding， throat pain， hyperextension of the neck and noisy respiration. A careful examination reveals a bulge in the posterior pharyngeal wall. This spectrum of manifestations is pre-ceded by an acute nasopharyngitis or pharyngitis.

【59】**Retropharyngeal Lymphadenitis**

【60】A nonfluctuating lymphadenitis may produce a tender bulge in the retropharyngeal space and a clinical picture closely resembling retropha-ryngeal abscess.

【64】**Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS)**

【65】_The term， sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS)， is applied to the_ sudden， unexpected death of an apparently healthy infant (typically 2to 3-month-old) who was put to sleep without any suspicion of such an anticipation. A conventional autopsy fails to reveal the cause of death. When an apparently healthy infant suffers from an episode in which he stops breathing， develops cyanosis or pallor and becomes unresponsive but is successfully resuscitated， the term； apparent life-threatening event (ALTE) should be employed. This state has also be termed near-miss or aborted SIDS. Such an infant runs significant risk of SIDS. In case of an infant with SIDS in a family， risk of the next or subsequent infant suffering from SIDS is 5-times the usual risk.

【66】The crux of the pathologic findings pointsto occurrence of hypoxia preceding the tragic event. Paradoxically， autopsy shows no hyperplasia of the carotid bodies. This observation weighs against the presence of chronic hypoxia.

【67】Etiology remains unclear. Allergy to cow's milk， enlargement of thymus， suffocation， deficiency of parathyroids or adrenals， hyperna-tremia and fulminant respiratory infection causing laryngeal obstruc-tion and/or spasm figure among the conditions that have been incrim-inated in its etiology. On top of all this， such states as prolonged sleep apnea associated with CNS disorders， vascular rings， familial prolon-gation of QT interval (Ramano Ward and Jervell and Lango-Nielsen syndromes)， accidental suffocation and child abuse and neglect (CAN) could camouflage as SIDS. A common etiology involving an abnor-mality of cardiorespiratory control， in which state of consciousness or CNS activity plays a modulating role， appears to be shared by all cases of true SIDS.

【68】In case ofinfants at risk (low birth weight， near-miss， or ALTE， sibs of SIDS case)， history should be obtained in relation to physiological handicaps before birth， e.g. low Apgar score， abnormality in control of respiration， heart rate and temperature， and postnatal growth retar-dation. It is appropriate to question the parents about infant's feeding， medication， etc.

【69】Physical examination should obtain information on the infant's nu-tritional status， hydration， evidence of infection， CAN and neurological handicap. Respiratory system must particularly be evaluated. He must also be observed while being given a feed.

【70】With this clinical evaluation， it should be possible to rule out a known medical cause for the catastrophe. In suspected cases， investiga-tions should include blood analysis for serum glucose， sodium， potassi-um， calcium， phosphorus， magnesium，BUN， pH and blood gas analysis， urinalysis， microbiological tests as dictated by the merits of the case， ECG monitoring， EEG， barium swallow， esophageal pH studies， chest X-ray and skeletal survey and 4 to 8 hour sleep studies.

【71】Apnea of 20 seconds or more is significant. It may be of three types：

【72】1\. Central as a result of absent neurological output from the res-piratory center，

【73】2\. Obstructive as a result of closure of the upper airway (even lower airway may be involved) so that the infant fails to experi-ence airflow despite considerable respiratory effort，

【74】3\. Mixed as result of combination of an obstructive episode and cen-tral apnea. Though， apnea has been incriminated in the etiology of SIDS， the cause and effect relationship remains unclear.

Anatomical and developmentalanomalies of the upper airway may cause obstruction and， perhaps， SIDS or ALTE， e.g. posterior displacement of the tongue as in Pierre Robin syndrome， reduced airway diameter following neck flexion， cleft palate， laryngo-malacia， tracheomalacia， bronchomalacia， laryngeal cleft or other anomalies， tracheoesophageal fistula of H-type，|删除0换行|bronchomalacia， vascular rings， immature or abnormal neuromus-cular control of oropharyngeal muscles， etc. In the presence of a viral respiratory infection， proneness to airway obstruction may be enhanced.

【76】Introduction of some fluids into the larynx may stimulate reflex apnea and reflux with aspiration， and cause SIDS.

【77】**Cardiac Anomalies (Arrhythmias)**

【78】The role of cardiac arrhythmias (R on T phenomenon， sick sinus syndrome) in the causation of SIDS remains debatable. No significant difference in cardiac rhythm is found between infants dying of SIDS and the normal controls. In ALTE， a proportion of the infants exhibit increased vagal tone. The resultant bradycardia is， perhaps，triggered by events such as a reflux.

【79】**Gastroesophageal Reflux**

【80】Reflux， a common finding in first 6 months of life， has been shown to produce apnea in some studies. How far it contributes to occur-rence of SIDS remains unclear.

【81】Abnormality in autonomic nervous system in infants with ALTE is evidenced by increased heart rate， and decreased heart-rate viability， shorter QT index and higher ventilatory response to CO，.

【82】In SIDS， increased levels of dopamine in carotid bodies are found. In infants with abnormal autonomic nervous system， a relationship be-tween SIDS and short-chain opioid peptides， e.g. B-casomor-phine， has been postulated.

【83】The role of such chemical mediators as catecholamines， endor-phins， and serotonin in causation of SIDS has also been speculat-ed.

【84】**Brainstem and Carotid Body Defects**

【85】Evidence suggests that brainstem and carotid body defects may be responsible for some cases of SIDS. The former circuit controls res-piratory or cardiac stability. The integrity of the latter is important for oxygen responsiveness as also sheer survival.
**_490_**

【87】Overwrapping leading to overheating of the preterm infants， who are susceptible to apnea when exposed to high environmental temperature， has been suggested as a factor in the etiology of SIDS. The concept， however，remains unproven.

【27】**STRIDOR MANIFESTING IN THE NEONATAL PERIOD Laryngomalacia**

【28】Also called congenital laryngeal stridor， this condition is responsible for nearly 90% of cases of stridor in the neonatal period. The cause is abnormal collapse of the supraglottic tissues (elongated or curved epiglottis， redundant aryteno-epiglottic folds) during inspiratory phase.

【29】Manifestations occur usually after the first week or two of birth. Stridor is characteristically intermittent. It is mainly inspiratory though， at times， it may be partly expiratory. During sleep and rest， it disappears whereas crying or excitement aggravates it. It is much less in prone position but is increased in supine position. The voice， cry， feeding and general health of the baby remain unaffected. Dyspnea with indrawing of the lower part of the chest during inspiration occur in a large majori-ty of the cases.

【30】After the age of 6 months， the manifestations begin to regress.The condition disappears by the age of 18 to 24 months.

【31】**Atretic Obstructive Lesions in the Upper Airway**

【32】Congenital atretic lesions of the upper airway usually cause death soon after birth. In supraglottic web， the infant has inspiratory stridor in association with hoarseness， subdued cry and chest indrawing. La-ryngeal webs and cyst cause hoarse cry， dyspnea and inspiratory stri-dor. Stridor as a result of subglottic pathology (congenital subglottic stenosis， hemangioma， angioma， papilloma，lymphangioma， polypi) is both inspiratory and expiratory. Hoarseness may be present. Cry is normal. Brassy or croupy cough may sometimes accompany the clini-cal picture.

【34】Tracheomalacia， tracheal cyst or tracheal stenosis leads to expi-ratory stridor.

【35】Laryngeal obstruction from presence of mucus， meconium or blood together with edema from trauma of intubation is an important cause of inspiratory stridor. It resolves well within 24 hours， particularly if aspiration of the obstructive stuff can be carried out under direct vision without loss of time.

【36】Vocal cord paralysisParalysis of the recurrent laryngealnerve(usually right) may occur in hydrocephalus associated Arnold-Chiari malformation or in brainstem injury. Bilateral paralysis may occur.

【37】Manifestations， more marked in bilateral involvement， include in-spiratory stridor， hoarseness， weak cry and choking during feeding.

【38】Laryngoscopy shows lack of mobility of the vocal cords.

【40】Stridor in vascular rings (double aorta or an abnormally placed subcla-vian artery) is， as a rule， intermittent and both inspiratory and expira-tory though it may be purely inspiratory or expiratory. Accompanying features include intractable cough which may be brassy or bitonal， and opisthotonos. An attempt at flexing the neck worsens the stridor.

【41】Diagnosis is by exclusion of other causes and by lateral X-ray of the airway.

【42】Outside compression from mediastinal or neck tumors (say lymphan-gioma， goiter) may produce stridor. There usually is some more evi-dence of compression， making the diagnosis easy.

【47】Following one or two days history of "cold"， the child develops inspiratory stridor， usually at night. He begins to hyperventilate and is quite upset. As the stridor persists， cyanosis and lower chest retraction develops. With further progression of the disease， impairment of the consciousness occurs. Trachea and bronchi may become partially ob-structed by thick secretions resulting in expiratory stridor and coarse rhonchi in the lung fields.

【48】人名段删除-1:<u>**Acute Epiglottitis**</u>

【49】This state of acute septicemia usually caused by H. influenzae type B， Staphylococcus or Pneumococcus， is characterized by rapid development of inspiratory stridor， dyspnea， muffling of the voice， dysphagia and drooling. The child is febrile and flushed. With increasing respiratory effort， inspiratory stridor diminishes. Throat examination shows an in-tensely red and swollen epiglottis.

【50】**Foreign Body**

【51】Sudden development of inspiratory stridor in a child who was other-wise fine， particularly if he is left to eat unattended and is fond of tak-ing small objects into the mouth， must arouse suspicion of a foreign body having got impacted in the larynx.

【52】Laryngeal diphtheria may be responsible for inspiratory stridor. Addition-al manifestations include hoarseness， aphonia， brassy or barking cough， dyspnea and cyanosis， restlessness， anxiety and prostration. Neck shows lymphadenitis and brawny edema (bull-neck).

【53】Diagnosis is by observing the characteristic membrane in the throat. In a vast majority of the cases， laryngeal involvement is secondary to faucial diphtheria. You may， however， readily see the membrane in the larynx by laryngoscopy.

【54】In order to establish the diagnosis， you must take a throat/ laryn-geal swab and examine the smear for the organisms which are seen as rods with bipolar bar.

【55】Any trauma to the larynx， resulting from instrumentation， corrosive agents or inhalation of smoke， may be responsible for laryngeal edema and acute stridor.

【56】Laryngospasm， associated with tetany of whatsoever etiology， may manifest with inspiratory stridor， apneic episodes and cyanosis. The attacks last over a few minutes and keep recurring.

【57】**Retropharyngeal Abscess**

【58】A retropharyngeal abscess manifests with inspiratory stridor only when pressure is put on the larynx. Clinical features include an abrupt onset of high fever， dysphagia， refusal of feeding， throat pain， hyperextension of the neck and noisy respiration. A careful examination reveals a bulge in the posterior pharyngeal wall. This spectrum of manifestations is pre-ceded by an acute nasopharyngitis or pharyngitis.

【59】**Retropharyngeal Lymphadenitis**

【60】A nonfluctuating lymphadenitis may produce a tender bulge in the retropharyngeal space and a clinical picture closely resembling retropha-ryngeal abscess.

【64】**Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS)**

【65】_The term， sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS)， is applied to the_ sudden， unexpected death of an apparently healthy infant (typically 2to 3-month-old) who was put to sleep without any suspicion of such an anticipation. A conventional autopsy fails to reveal the cause of death. When an apparently healthy infant suffers from an episode in which he stops breathing， develops cyanosis or pallor and becomes unresponsive but is successfully resuscitated， the term； apparent life-threatening event (ALTE) should be employed. This state has also be termed near-miss or aborted SIDS. Such an infant runs significant risk of SIDS. In case of an infant with SIDS in a family， risk of the next or subsequent infant suffering from SIDS is 5-times the usual risk.

【66】The crux of the pathologic findings pointsto occurrence of hypoxia preceding the tragic event. Paradoxically， autopsy shows no hyperplasia of the carotid bodies. This observation weighs against the presence of chronic hypoxia.

【67】Etiology remains unclear. Allergy to cow's milk， enlargement of thymus， suffocation， deficiency of parathyroids or adrenals， hyperna-tremia and fulminant respiratory infection causing laryngeal obstruc-tion and/or spasm figure among the conditions that have been incrim-inated in its etiology. On top of all this， such states as prolonged sleep apnea associated with CNS disorders， vascular rings， familial prolon-gation of QT interval (Ramano Ward and Jervell and Lango-Nielsen syndromes)， accidental suffocation and child abuse and neglect (CAN) could camouflage as SIDS. A common etiology involving an abnor-mality of cardiorespiratory control， in which state of consciousness or CNS activity plays a modulating role， appears to be shared by all cases of true SIDS.

【68】In case ofinfants at risk (low birth weight， near-miss， or ALTE， sibs of SIDS case)， history should be obtained in relation to physiological handicaps before birth， e.g. low Apgar score， abnormality in control of respiration， heart rate and temperature， and postnatal growth retar-dation. It is appropriate to question the parents about infant's feeding， medication， etc.

【69】Physical examination should obtain information on the infant's nu-tritional status， hydration， evidence of infection， CAN and neurological handicap. Respiratory system must particularly be evaluated. He must also be observed while being given a feed.

【70】With this clinical evaluation， it should be possible to rule out a known medical cause for the catastrophe. In suspected cases， investiga-tions should include blood analysis for serum glucose， sodium， potassi-um， calcium， phosphorus， magnesium，BUN， pH and blood gas analysis， urinalysis， microbiological tests as dictated by the merits of the case， ECG monitoring， EEG， barium swallow， esophageal pH studies， chest X-ray and skeletal survey and 4 to 8 hour sleep studies.

【71】Apnea of 20 seconds or more is significant. It may be of three types：

【72】1\. Central as a result of absent neurological output from the res-piratory center，

【73】2\. Obstructive as a result of closure of the upper airway (even lower airway may be involved) so that the infant fails to experi-ence airflow despite considerable respiratory effort，

【74】3\. Mixed as result of combination of an obstructive episode and cen-tral apnea. Though， apnea has been incriminated in the etiology of SIDS， the cause and effect relationship remains unclear.

Anatomical and developmentalanomalies of the upper airway may cause obstruction and， perhaps， SIDS or ALTE， e.g. posterior displacement of the tongue as in Pierre Robin syndrome， reduced airway diameter following neck flexion， cleft palate， laryngo-malacia， tracheomalacia， bronchomalacia， laryngeal cleft or other anomalies， tracheoesophageal fistula of H-type，|删除0换行|bronchomalacia， vascular rings， immature or abnormal neuromus-cular control of oropharyngeal muscles， etc. In the presence of a viral respiratory infection， proneness to airway obstruction may be enhanced.

【76】Introduction of some fluids into the larynx may stimulate reflex apnea and reflux with aspiration， and cause SIDS.

【77】**Cardiac Anomalies (Arrhythmias)**

【78】The role of cardiac arrhythmias (R on T phenomenon， sick sinus syndrome) in the causation of SIDS remains debatable. No significant difference in cardiac rhythm is found between infants dying of SIDS and the normal controls. In ALTE， a proportion of the infants exhibit increased vagal tone. The resultant bradycardia is， perhaps，triggered by events such as a reflux.

【79】**Gastroesophageal Reflux**

【80】Reflux， a common finding in first 6 months of life， has been shown to produce apnea in some studies. How far it contributes to occur-rence of SIDS remains unclear.

【81】Abnormality in autonomic nervous system in infants with ALTE is evidenced by increased heart rate， and decreased heart-rate viability， shorter QT index and higher ventilatory response to CO，.

【82】In SIDS， increased levels of dopamine in carotid bodies are found. In infants with abnormal autonomic nervous system， a relationship be-tween SIDS and short-chain opioid peptides， e.g. B-casomor-phine， has been postulated.

【83】The role of such chemical mediators as catecholamines， endor-phins， and serotonin in causation of SIDS has also been speculat-ed.

【84】**Brainstem and Carotid Body Defects**

【85】Evidence suggests that brainstem and carotid body defects may be responsible for some cases of SIDS. The former circuit controls res-piratory or cardiac stability. The integrity of the latter is important for oxygen responsiveness as also sheer survival.

【29】Manifestations occur usually after the first week or two of birth. Stridor is characteristically intermittent. It is mainly inspiratory though， at times， it may be partly expiratory. During sleep and rest， it disappears whereas crying or excitement aggravates it. It is much less in prone position but is increased in supine position. The voice， cry， feeding and general health of the baby remain unaffected. Dyspnea with indrawing of the lower part of the chest during inspiration occur in a large majori-ty of the cases.

【30】After the age of 6 months， the manifestations begin to regress.The condition disappears by the age of 18 to 24 months.

【31】**Atretic Obstructive Lesions in the Upper Airway**

【32】Congenital atretic lesions of the upper airway usually cause death soon after birth. In supraglottic web， the infant has inspiratory stridor in association with hoarseness， subdued cry and chest indrawing. La-ryngeal webs and cyst cause hoarse cry， dyspnea and inspiratory stri-dor. Stridor as a result of subglottic pathology (congenital subglottic stenosis， hemangioma， angioma， papilloma，lymphangioma， polypi) is both inspiratory and expiratory. Hoarseness may be present. Cry is normal. Brassy or croupy cough may sometimes accompany the clini-cal picture.

【33】**Differential Diagnosis in Pediatrics**

【34】Tracheomalacia， tracheal cyst or tracheal stenosis leads to expi-ratory stridor.

【35】Laryngeal obstruction from presence of mucus， meconium or blood together with edema from trauma of intubation is an important cause of inspiratory stridor. It resolves well within 24 hours， particularly if aspiration of the obstructive stuff can be carried out under direct vision without loss of time.

【36】Vocal cord paralysisParalysis of the recurrent laryngealnerve(usually right) may occur in hydrocephalus associated Arnold-Chiari malformation or in brainstem injury. Bilateral paralysis may occur.

【37】Manifestations， more marked in bilateral involvement， include in-spiratory stridor， hoarseness， weak cry and choking during feeding.

【38】Laryngoscopy shows lack of mobility of the vocal cords.

【39】**Vascular Rings**

【40】Stridor in vascular rings (double aorta or an abnormally placed subcla-vian artery) is， as a rule， intermittent and both inspiratory and expira-tory though it may be purely inspiratory or expiratory. Accompanying features include intractable cough which may be brassy or bitonal， and opisthotonos. An attempt at flexing the neck worsens the stridor.

【41】Diagnosis is by exclusion of other causes and by lateral X-ray of the airway.

【42】Outside compression from mediastinal or neck tumors (say lymphan-gioma， goiter) may produce stridor. There usually is some more evi-dence of compression， making the diagnosis easy.

【43】**STRIDOR MANIFESTING IN LATER INFANCY AND CHILDHOOD**

【45】This condition， caused usually by H. influenzae or parainfluenzae virus and also termed croup， is the most common cause of acute

**Stridor|删除换行|inspiratory stridor. It occurs in children， usually under 3 years of age.

【47】Following one or two days history of "cold"， the child develops inspiratory stridor， usually at night. He begins to hyperventilate and is quite upset. As the stridor persists， cyanosis and lower chest retraction develops. With further progression of the disease， impairment of the consciousness occurs. Trachea and bronchi may become partially ob-structed by thick secretions resulting in expiratory stridor and coarse rhonchi in the lung fields.

【48】人名段删除-1:<u>**Acute Epiglottitis**</u>

【49】This state of acute septicemia usually caused by H. influenzae type B， Staphylococcus or Pneumococcus， is characterized by rapid development of inspiratory stridor， dyspnea， muffling of the voice， dysphagia and drooling. The child is febrile and flushed. With increasing respiratory effort， inspiratory stridor diminishes. Throat examination shows an in-tensely red and swollen epiglottis.

【50】**Foreign Body**

【51】Sudden development of inspiratory stridor in a child who was other-wise fine， particularly if he is left to eat unattended and is fond of tak-ing small objects into the mouth， must arouse suspicion of a foreign body having got impacted in the larynx.

【52】Laryngeal diphtheria may be responsible for inspiratory stridor. Addition-al manifestations include hoarseness， aphonia， brassy or barking cough， dyspnea and cyanosis， restlessness， anxiety and prostration. Neck shows lymphadenitis and brawny edema (bull-neck).

【53】Diagnosis is by observing the characteristic membrane in the throat. In a vast majority of the cases， laryngeal involvement is secondary to faucial diphtheria. You may， however， readily see the membrane in the larynx by laryngoscopy.

【54】In order to establish the diagnosis， you must take a throat/ laryn-geal swab and examine the smear for the organisms which are seen as rods with bipolar bar.

【55】Any trauma to the larynx， resulting from instrumentation， corrosive agents or inhalation of smoke， may be responsible for laryngeal edema and acute stridor.

【56】Laryngospasm， associated with tetany of whatsoever etiology， may manifest with inspiratory stridor， apneic episodes and cyanosis. The attacks last over a few minutes and keep recurring.

【57】**Retropharyngeal Abscess**

【58】A retropharyngeal abscess manifests with inspiratory stridor only when pressure is put on the larynx. Clinical features include an abrupt onset of high fever， dysphagia， refusal of feeding， throat pain， hyperextension of the neck and noisy respiration. A careful examination reveals a bulge in the posterior pharyngeal wall. This spectrum of manifestations is pre-ceded by an acute nasopharyngitis or pharyngitis.

【59】**Retropharyngeal Lymphadenitis**

【60】A nonfluctuating lymphadenitis may produce a tender bulge in the retropharyngeal space and a clinical picture closely resembling retropha-ryngeal abscess.

【64】**Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS)**

【65】_The term， sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS)， is applied to the_ sudden， unexpected death of an apparently healthy infant (typically 2to 3-month-old) who was put to sleep without any suspicion of such an anticipation. A conventional autopsy fails to reveal the cause of death. When an apparently healthy infant suffers from an episode in which he stops breathing， develops cyanosis or pallor and becomes unresponsive but is successfully resuscitated， the term； apparent life-threatening event (ALTE) should be employed. This state has also be termed near-miss or aborted SIDS. Such an infant runs significant risk of SIDS. In case of an infant with SIDS in a family， risk of the next or subsequent infant suffering from SIDS is 5-times the usual risk.

【66】The crux of the pathologic findings pointsto occurrence of hypoxia preceding the tragic event. Paradoxically， autopsy shows no hyperplasia of the carotid bodies. This observation weighs against the presence of chronic hypoxia.

【67】Etiology remains unclear. Allergy to cow's milk， enlargement of thymus， suffocation， deficiency of parathyroids or adrenals， hyperna-tremia and fulminant respiratory infection causing laryngeal obstruc-tion and/or spasm figure among the conditions that have been incrim-inated in its etiology. On top of all this， such states as prolonged sleep apnea associated with CNS disorders， vascular rings， familial prolon-gation of QT interval (Ramano Ward and Jervell and Lango-Nielsen syndromes)， accidental suffocation and child abuse and neglect (CAN) could camouflage as SIDS. A common etiology involving an abnor-mality of cardiorespiratory control， in which state of consciousness or CNS activity plays a modulating role， appears to be shared by all cases of true SIDS.

【68】In case ofinfants at risk (low birth weight， near-miss， or ALTE， sibs of SIDS case)， history should be obtained in relation to physiological handicaps before birth， e.g. low Apgar score， abnormality in control of respiration， heart rate and temperature， and postnatal growth retar-dation. It is appropriate to question the parents about infant's feeding， medication， etc.

【69】Physical examination should obtain information on the infant's nu-tritional status， hydration， evidence of infection， CAN and neurological handicap. Respiratory system must particularly be evaluated. He must also be observed while being given a feed.

【70】With this clinical evaluation， it should be possible to rule out a known medical cause for the catastrophe. In suspected cases， investiga-tions should include blood analysis for serum glucose， sodium， potassi-um， calcium， phosphorus， magnesium，BUN， pH and blood gas analysis， urinalysis， microbiological tests as dictated by the merits of the case， ECG monitoring， EEG， barium swallow， esophageal pH studies， chest X-ray and skeletal survey and 4 to 8 hour sleep studies.

【71】Apnea of 20 seconds or more is significant. It may be of three types：

【72】1\. Central as a result of absent neurological output from the res-piratory center，

【73】2\. Obstructive as a result of closure of the upper airway (even lower airway may be involved) so that the infant fails to experi-ence airflow despite considerable respiratory effort，

【74】3\. Mixed as result of combination of an obstructive episode and cen-tral apnea. Though， apnea has been incriminated in the etiology of SIDS， the cause and effect relationship remains unclear.

Anatomical and developmentalanomalies of the upper airway may cause obstruction and， perhaps， SIDS or ALTE， e.g. posterior displacement of the tongue as in Pierre Robin syndrome， reduced airway diameter following neck flexion， cleft palate， laryngo-malacia， tracheomalacia， bronchomalacia， laryngeal cleft or other anomalies， tracheoesophageal fistula of H-type，|删除0换行|bronchomalacia， vascular rings， immature or abnormal neuromus-cular control of oropharyngeal muscles， etc. In the presence of a viral respiratory infection， proneness to airway obstruction may be enhanced.

【76】Introduction of some fluids into the larynx may stimulate reflex apnea and reflux with aspiration， and cause SIDS.

【77】**Cardiac Anomalies (Arrhythmias)**

【78】The role of cardiac arrhythmias (R on T phenomenon， sick sinus syndrome) in the causation of SIDS remains debatable. No significant difference in cardiac rhythm is found between infants dying of SIDS and the normal controls. In ALTE， a proportion of the infants exhibit increased vagal tone. The resultant bradycardia is， perhaps，triggered by events such as a reflux.

【79】**Gastroesophageal Reflux**

【80】Reflux， a common finding in first 6 months of life， has been shown to produce apnea in some studies. How far it contributes to occur-rence of SIDS remains unclear.

【81】Abnormality in autonomic nervous system in infants with ALTE is evidenced by increased heart rate， and decreased heart-rate viability， shorter QT index and higher ventilatory response to CO，.

【82】In SIDS， increased levels of dopamine in carotid bodies are found. In infants with abnormal autonomic nervous system， a relationship be-tween SIDS and short-chain opioid peptides， e.g. B-casomor-phine， has been postulated.

【83】The role of such chemical mediators as catecholamines， endor-phins， and serotonin in causation of SIDS has also been speculat-ed.

【84】**Brainstem and Carotid Body Defects**

【85】Evidence suggests that brainstem and carotid body defects may be responsible for some cases of SIDS. The former circuit controls res-piratory or cardiac stability. The integrity of the latter is important for oxygen responsiveness as also sheer survival.

【86】**Hyperthermia**

【87】Overwrapping leading to overheating of the preterm infants， who are susceptible to apnea when exposed to high environmental temperature， has been suggested as a factor in the etiology of SIDS. The concept， however，remains unproven.

【91】By definition， tall stature is said to exist when an individual has an height that is above the 97th percentile for age. It is infrequent for the parents to seek advice for a child with tall stature. During the past over 3decades， I had only 18 adolescents and 3 toddlers brought to my OPDs at Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research， Chandigarh， Medical College， Shimla， Govt. Medical College，Jammu， and Narayana Medical College， Nellore， for this complaint. The incidence is， perhaps， not as low. It appears that tall stature is evidently socially more accept-able than short stature. Hence， parents do not care to seek advice for too tall children. Did the height show sudden acceleration only recently?

【93】Physical examination， in the first instance， must record the accu-rate height and body proportions. Are there signs of raised intracranial pressure? Are there any other neurologic signs? Are there any abnor-mal features like arachnodactyly， antimongoloid slant of eyes，obesity， etc?

【41】The term， limping， means to walk lamely or unevenly as when one hip， leg or foot is stiff or hurt. Though， majority of the cases of limp in pediatric practice are minor and transient， the problem often causes considerable anxiety to the parents as long as it continues to trouble the child.

【42】This common problem may be caused by a lesion (as minor as trauma from a protruding nail in the shoe， or as serious as paresis) anywhere in the weight-bearing structure-complex consisting chiefly of spine， hips， knees， ankles and feet. Often the lesion may be inap-parent. Infrequently， the complaint may be projected as an attention-seeking device. Whereas a painful (antalgic) limping is usually secondary to injury， infection or pathologic fracture， Trendelenburg limping is predominantly due to congenital， developmental or neuromuscular/musculoskeletal disorder (polio， cerebral palsy， myopathy，DDH).

【43】A thorough history and physical examination are central to early identification of the cause of limp.

【44】While recording history， you must put considerable efforts to elicit the particular activity that may have caused limp. Was there a trauma： a fall， a pull， or a blow? Any preceding or accompanying fever? Any joint pain? Is the limp on way to recovery， going downhill or showing no change? Is the child aware of any problem with the shoes? Does the shoe pinch or it has a nail or strap buckle that troubles the child? Is the child suffering from some myopathy， tuberculosis， congenital defect， etc.

Physical examination must include observation of the child， while he limps， by the physician. Attempt should be made to determine its cause in the spine， hip， knee， ankle， feet， bones or|删除0换行|soft tissues. Don't forget to look for asymmetry in the size of the legs. Is there any inguinal lymphadenitis? Is there any painful boil? You must also examine shoes for undue tightness， a protruding nail， or a bad buck-le. Does the foot show any corn， wart， blisters， paronyechia， or ingrow-ing toenail?

【46】A good musculoskeletal examination， including grading of mus-cle power， is important. Box 42.1 gives the popular system of grad-ing the muscle power.

【48】**JOINTS/BONES**

【49】**Hips**

【50】_Congenital dislocation of the hip (developmental dysplasia of the hip)：_ A missed and untreated congenital dislocation of the hip may be responsible for a limp and delayed walking. A close examination of such a child shows asymmetry of the thigh， gluteal and knee creases， inability to abduct the hipfully， shortness of the affected leg， reduced spontaneous movements and a bulge of the femoral head.

【51】A good screening test (Ortolani's sign) consists in abducting the hip passively. A clicking sound is heard from the hip at the end of the ma-neuver. It results from the jerking of the subluxated head as it reduces back into the acetabulum.

【52】The Barlow's maneuver is better than Ortolani maneuver. Here， the pelvis is stabilized with one hand， followed by adduction of the opposite hip and application of a posterior force. A dislocatable hip is readily appreciated.

【53】Diagnosis is confirmed by X-ray of the hip joint and/or ultra-sonography. An anteroposterior X-ray view usually reveals superior and lateral displacement of the femoral head from the shallow ac-etabulum.

【54】**Limping**

【55】Congenital coxa vara： In this disorder of unknown etiology， usu-ally encountered after 2 to 3 years of age， physical findings simulate a dislocated hip. The basic defect is that the femoral neck makes less than 135° angle with the shaft. Left unattended， varus deformity shows worsening.

【56】Septic arthritis： Suppuration is the most important cause of painful hip and limp in infants and toddlers. Involvement of hip may be direct extension of osteomyelitis of the femoral neck or a blood-borne infec-tion.

【57】For confirmation of the diagnosis， X-ray hip， showing lateral dis-placement of the femoral head as also the fat close to the capsule due to fluid accumulation， is of considerable value. Aspiration of thick pus from the joint further establishes the diagnosis. If osteomyelitis coex-ists， increased bone uptake is demonstrated by a bone scan.

【58】Toxic or transient synovitis： This disorder of toddlers and children may be responsible for painful hip and limp which responds to as simple a treatment as bed rest. The cause is not clear. Frequently， it is preceded by a viral upper respiratory infection a few days to 2 weeks earlier. All signs of inflammation of the joint are observed. The bacterial infection is， however， not responsible for the condition.

【59】Tuberculosis of the hip： An intermittent slight limp with pain， occur-ring when the subject first gets out of bed and after exercise， is usually the first manifestation of tuberculosis of the hip. Pain is usually referred to the knee or medial aspect of the thigh. Limp and pain may show remission for days or weeks. With progressive destruction of the joint following absorption of the femoral head and neck， the thigh assumes a position of flexion， adduction and medial (earlier it is lateral) rotation.

【60】Perthes disease： Also termed Legg-Calve-Perthes disease， this con-dition of a vascular necrosis of the head of the femur usually occurs in5 to 9 years age group and is an important cause of pain and limp. It may be very difficult to differentiate it from tuberculosis of the hip and transient synovitis of the hip in early stages. It is of value to remember that， unlike in tuberculosis， in Perthes disease we have limitation of on-ly abduction and internal rotation.

【61】In the X-ray， head of the femur shows flatting， fragmentation and condensation and is dense and not lucent. The joint space is widened. 【9】Applying the mnemonic MINT to the various anatomic parts of the eye will aid in systematically developing a list of diagnostic possibilities for eye pain.

【10】**M-Malformations most certainly suggest glaucoma and all the refractive disorders (e.g.， astigmatism， myopia， hypermetropia\].**

【11】**I-Inflammation accounts for most cases. One anatomi-cally recalls conjunctivitis， Sjogren syndrome， keratitis， scleritis， corneal ulcers， iridocyclitis， and optic neuritis.**

【12】Do not forget inflammation of the orbit. Vasculitis from temporal arteritis must be considered with obstruction of the retinal veins or arteries.

【13】N-Neoplasms are unlikely causes but must be considered. T-Trauma should suggest abrasions and foreign bodies， particularly those of the cornea.

【14】Eye pain， like earache， may be referred. Cerebral neoplasms， migraine， and sinusitis may all present with orbital or retroorbital pain. An additional category of etiologies that is not common in earache is systemic disease. Any febrile disease may cause bilateral eye pain， particularly viral influenza.

【15】**Approach to the Diagnosis**

【16】The approach to the diagnosis of eye pain involves a careful search for inflammation of the various anatomic structures； then a drop or two of fluorescent dye is inserted and the cornea inspected for lacerations， herpes ulcers， and foreign bodies. Finally， tonometry may be done. Referral to an oph-thalmologist is often necessary， but the astute clinician will want to x-ray the sinuses， ask about a history of migraine， do a visual field， and rule out systemic diseases beforehand.

【17】**Other Useful Tests**

【35】To develop a list of possible causes of a face mass， let us turn to anatomy. The face is composed of skin， subcuta neous tissues， muscle， bone， teeth， the sinuses， salivary glands， arteries， veins， and nerves. Applying the mnemonic VINDICATE to each one of these structures， we can come up with an excellent list of possibilities：

【36】**Skin and subcutaneous tissues-Carbuncles， cellulitis， sebaceous cysts； lipomas， carcinomas， angioneurotic edema， etc.**

【37】Muscle-Myositis， myomas， hypertrophy

【38】**Bone-Osteomas， metastatic tumor， multiple myelomas osteomyelitis**

【40】**Sinuses-Wegener midline granuloma， nmucormycosis， neoplasm**

【41】**Salivary glands-Mumps， tumors， calculus， Mikulicz syn drome， Sjogren syndrome**

【42】**Arteries and veins-Hemangiomas， arteriovenous fistula Nerves-Neuroma， neurofibromatosis**

【43】**Approach to the Diagnosis**

【44】If infection is suspected， smears and cultures of exudates should be done. X-rays of the skull， sinuses， and jaw may be helpful. A computed tomography (CT) scan will be more definitive. If neoplasm or granuloma is suspected， a biopsy or excision will be necessary. If there is still doubt about the etiology， an oral surgeon or otolaryngologist should be consulted.

【45】**Other Useful Tests**
